2610.12380.summary: High-altitude platform stations (HAPS) are a promising component of non-terrestrial networks (NTNs) for wide-area connectivity. However, serving multiple users over large user footprints requires efficient power-control mechanisms that account for the unique propagation characteristics and strict power constraints of HAPS. This paper develops a tractable analytical and optimization framework for downlink power allocation in HAPS systems under statistical channel state information, 3GPP NTN path loss, and Rician fading. A closed-form expression for the signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) with mean-channel maximal-ratio transmission (MRT) precoding is derived, capturing geometry-dependent inter-user interference coupling. Based on this, two power-control schemes are proposed: quality-of-service (QoS)-constrained power minimization and max-min SINR fairness. The QoS solution is obtained in closed form or through a low-complexity fixed-point iteration, while the max-min solution is obtained through bisection. Numerical results demonstrate up to 6 dB reduction in required transmit power at moderate-to-high target rates and improved worst-user SINR compared to the uniform power, inverse path-loss, and geometry-aware heuristic allocations. The proposed QoS-optimal scheme also achieves a QoS feasibility probability of approximately 0.95 at R_req = 2.5 bits/s/Hz and P_max = 35 dBm, while the uniform power, inverse path-loss, and geometry-aware heuristic allocations achieve less than 0.4. Moreover, the proposed schemes achieve performance comparable to the linear programming (LP)-based benchmarks at a fraction of the computational cost, reducing the average computation time by approximately 99.97% when K = 20.
2610.12380.title: Interference-Aware Downlink Power Control for High-Altitude Platform Stations with QoS and Max-Min Fairness

2610.12413.summary: We establish a previously unnoticed connection between commitment (BC), a fundamental cryptographic primitive, and deterministic identification (DI), a post-Shannon communication setting. Specifically, for additive white Gaussian noise channels $\mathcal{G}$ we show that a reliable commitment protocol can be obtained from deterministic identification codes in both the honest but curious and fully dishonest security settings. This viewpoint allows BC schemes to inherit the asymptotic performance of DI codes. Indeed, we show that commitment is naturally achievable in the linearithmic regime, i.e., with message sets of size $N_n=\exp [\Theta(n\log n)]$, and we establish a lower bound on the linearithmic-scale BC capacity of $\dot C_{\text{hBC}}(\mathcal G)\geq\frac12$ in the honest but curious case and $\dot C_{\text{BC}}(\mathcal G)\geq\frac14$ in the fully dishonest picture. This refines the best previously known characterisation of the commitment capacity over $\mathcal{G}$, which established only an infinite linear-scale capacity.
2610.12413.title: Commitment over Gaussian channels with deterministic identification codes

AI.conclusion: 码本结构、阵列规模和码本规模共同决定近场随机波束成形性能，近场专用码本（RNF）在高增益缩放上最具优势，远场码本用于近场服务存在固有增益上界。
AI.method: 对RVQ、RP、RFF、RNF四种随机码本进行理论分析：以已知RVQ增益分布为基准，对RP推导大阵列体近似并刻画高增益尾部，对RNF刻画高增益尾部，对RFF推导远场波束服务近场用户时的最大可达波束成形增益解析近似及最优远场方向，并分析最大增益随码本规模的缩放；用蒙特卡洛仿真验证。
AI.motivation: 近场通信需考虑球面波前，预定义码本广泛使用，但随机生成码本在近场区域的性能尚未被研究，因此本文填补该空白并给出理论刻画。
AI.relevance_reason: 论文研究近场大规模MIMO码本与波束成形增益，属于无线物理层及MIMO信道相关背景，但为随机码本的理论/统计分析，未涉及AI方法，与CSI获取/压缩/反馈的核心方向仅间接相关。
AI.result: 仿真验证解析结果：RVQ与RP随阵列增大性能显著退化，RNF具有最优的高增益缩放；RFF在有限码本规模下可优于RVQ与RP，但因远场波束与近场信道的相位失配，其最大增益饱和于1以下。
AI.tldr: 研究近场大规模天线系统中四种随机码本（RVQ、RP、RFF、RNF）的波束成形增益分布与高增益尾部及码本规模缩放特性，用大阵列近似和蒙特卡洛仿真验证，发现RNF高增益缩放最优、RFF最大增益饱和小于1。

item.summary: Near-field communication with large antenna arrays requires beamforming techniques that account for spherical wavefront effects. While predefined codebooks are widely used in multiple-antenna wireless systems, the performance of randomly generated codebooks in the near-field region has not been investigated. In this work, we study four randomly generated codebooks for near-field communications: random vector quantization (RVQ), random phase (RP), random far-field (RFF), and random near-field (RNF) codebooks. We use the known RVQ gain distribution as a benchmark. For RP, we derive a large-array bulk approximation and characterize the high-gain tail behavior of the gain distribution. For RNF, we characterize the high-gain tail behavior of the gain distribution. For RFF, we derive an analytical approximation for the maximum achievable beamforming gain when far-field beams are used to serve near-field users, along with the corresponding maximizing far-field direction. We also analyze the maximum-gain scaling with codebook size. Monte Carlo simulations verify the analytical results and show that RVQ and RP degrade significantly as the array size increases, while RNF achieves the most favorable high-gain scaling. RFF can outperform RVQ and RP for finite codebook sizes, but its maximum gain saturates below one due to the phase mismatch between the far-field beams and the near-field channel. These results show how codebook structure, array size, and codebook size affect random beamforming performance in the near-field.
item.title: On the Performance of Randomly Generated Codebooks in Near-Field Communications

AI.conclusion: 基于扩展 PARAFAC 张量模型的 TenDICE 能以较低复杂度有效实现 RIS 辅助 MIMO 的联合直连/间接信道估计，性能接近理论界并优于若干经典方法。
AI.method: 对接收导频信号建立扩展 PARAFAC 张量模型，提出张量接收机 TenDICE，用简单的交替最小二乘（ALS）方案联合估计直连与间接信道。
AI.motivation: RIS 辅助 MIMO 系统中同时存在 BS-UE 直连链路与经 RIS 的间接链路，需要一种能联合估计两类信道、且计算复杂度可控的方法。
AI.relevance_reason: 该文直接针对 RIS 辅助 MIMO 信道估计这一高优先级主题，但采用张量分解/PARAFAC 而非用户偏好的深度学习或生成式方法，AI 成分较弱。
AI.result: 以 NMSE 和频谱效率（SE）为指标，与 LS、KRF、E-TALS 及 CRLB 对比：TenDICE 优于 LS 和 E-TALS，估计直连信道时与 KRF 性能相近。
AI.tldr: 本文提出 TenDICE 算法，基于扩展 PARAFAC 张量模型对 RIS 辅助 MIMO 系统的直连与经 RIS 间接链路进行联合信道估计，采用交替最小二乘求解，性能优于 LS 和 E-TALS，与 KRF 相当。

item.summary: This paper introduces an enhanced channel estimation method for reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) communications. Considering the presence of both the direct link from the base station (BS) to the user equipment (UE) and the indirect link \textit{via} the RIS, we formulate a tensor-based receiver for joint direct and indirect channel estimation called the TenDICE algorithm. The proposed receiver relies on an extended parallel factor analysis (PARAFAC) tensor model for the received pilot signals, from which the involved (direct and indirect link) channels are estimated using a simple alternating least squares scheme. The proposed TenDICE method is compared with the state-of-the-art least squares (LS) method, Khatri-Rao factorization (KRF) method, enhanced trilinear alternating least squares (E-TALS), and the theoretical Cramér-Rao lower bound (CRLB) based on normalized mean square error (NMSE) and spectral efficiency (SE). The proposed TenDICE outperforms the LS and E-TALS methods and performs similarly to the KRF methods while estimating the direct channel.
item.title: Simultaneous Direct and Indirect Channel Estimation for RIS-Assisted MIMO Communications

AI.conclusion: 张量分解结合ESPRIT的低复杂度方案可有效提升Butler矩阵波束成形下mmWave massive MIMO的信道估计性能，为低复杂度、高精度信道获取提供了可行路径。
AI.method: 将接收信号建模为三阶PARAFAC张量，利用已知导频结构通过双线性交替最小二乘（BALS）进行分解以降低复杂度；对解耦的空间因子采用1D与2D ESPRIT提取到达角与离开角并实现自动配对；推导该架构的Cramer-Rao下界（CRLB）。
AI.motivation: 下行mmWave大规模MIMO系统中，传统最小二乘信道估计计算开销大且精度受限，需在保持低复杂度的同时提升信道重建精度。被动Butler矩阵波束成形架构下的信道估计问题尚缺少针对性方案。
AI.relevance_reason: 属于mmWave大规模MIMO信道估计与低复杂度算法，但采用传统张量/ESPRIT方法而非AI方法，AI相关性较弱，仅为背景性参考。
AI.result: 仿真表明所提估计器优于传统最小二乘方法，能实现精确的信道重建，并在中高信噪比下逼近CRLB。
AI.tldr: 提出基于PARAFAC张量分解与BALS优化的低复杂度下行mmWave大规模MIMO信道估计算法，配合Butler矩阵波束成形与ESPRIT角度提取，并推导CRLB。

item.summary: This paper presents a low-complexity tensor-based channel estimation framework for downlink mmWave massive MIMO systems using passive Butler-matrix beamforming. By modeling received signals as a third-order PARAFAC tensor, we exploit known pilot structures via bilinear alternating least-squares (BALS) optimization to reduce computational overhead. The decoupled spatial factors are then processed via 1D and 2D ESPRIT to extract angles of arrival and departure with automatic pairing. Additionally, we derive the Cramer--Rao lower bound (CRLB) for this architecture. Simulations confirm the proposed estimator outperforms conventional least-squares, achieving accurate channel reconstruction and approaching the CRLB at moderate-to-high signal-to-noise ratios.
item.title: Low-Complexity Tensor-Based Channel Parameter Estimation for mmWave MIMO-Assisted Systems

AI.conclusion: 角度分集是目标几何可辨识性的必要条件而非可选优化；仅靠谱斜率不足以判定散射机制与几何。通信链路自身可用于太赫兹目标形状/朝向推断，但多目标场景的性能瓶颈在回波干扰而非角度覆盖。
AI.method: 建立物理驱动的多基地前向模型：300 GHz载波、50 GHz带宽，融合PO与PTD散射、镜像源多径格点、分子吸收与定向喇叭天线；揭示PO机制层级中六种机制共享三个频率指数、谱斜率无法唯一定位机制的隐含性质；采用发射机数量不变的2D-CNN与物理信息RBF-SVM进行朝向分类对比。
AI.motivation: 6G网络期望以承载数据的同一波形进行环境感知，作者希望探明在没有专用感知硬件、仅依赖通信链路散射回波的情况下，能从太赫兹信号中获取多少目标几何信息。
AI.relevance_reason: 论文属太赫兹物理层感知与散射建模，与AI辅助物理层方向相邻，但聚焦目标几何/朝向推断而非CSI获取、反馈或压缩，与用户核心方向连接较弱。
relevance_topics: 太赫兹通信感知一体化
AI.result: 在未见过的朝向上准确率从单发射机的约70%提升至20个发射机的96–97%；CNN在不规则布置与有损目标两种情形下占优，而金属目标准均匀布置时SVM基线具竞争力；遮挡下性能渐变下降，75%表面被遮挡仍保持78%，完全未见遮挡目标时降至63%；多目标场景受重叠回波干扰限制而非角域覆盖，存在性检测约4个发射机后饱和。
AI.tldr: 该论文在300 GHz、50 GHz带宽下构建基于物理光学(PO)与物理绕射理论(PTD)的多基地前向模型，研究仅利用通信链路产生的太赫兹回波能否推断物体形状/朝向，并比较2D-CNN与物理信息RBF-SVM的性能。

item.comment: 6 pages, 5 figures, 2 tables. Accepted to IEEE GLOBECOM 2026 Workshops (Third Workshop on Positioning and Sensing Over Wireless Networks)
item.summary: 6G networks are expected to sense their surroundings using the same waveforms that carry data. We ask how much can be learned about the shape of an object from the terahertz echoes that user equipment transmissions produce as they scatter from that object on their way to a ceiling-mounted access point, with no sensing hardware beyond the communication link itself. We build a physics-based multistatic forward model at a 300 GHz carrier with 50 GHz of bandwidth, combining Physical Optics (PO) and Physical Theory of Diffraction (PTD) scattering with an image-source multipath lattice, molecular absorption and directional horn antennas. The model makes explicit a property of the PO mechanism hierarchy that is usually left implicit. Six physically distinct mechanisms share only three frequency exponents, so the spectral slope does not by itself determine which mechanisms a target presents and therefore cannot by itself determine its geometry. Angular diversity is accordingly a requirement for identifiability rather than an optional refinement. We compare a transmitter-count-invariant 2D-CNN with a physics-informed RBF-SVM on object orientations never seen in training. Accuracy climbs from roughly 70 percent with one transmitter to 96-97 percent with 20. The CNN gains in two regimes, irregular placement and lossy targets, while on metal under quasi-uniform placement the SVM baseline is fully competitive. Performance falls off gradually under occlusion, holding 78 percent with three quarters of the surface hidden and 63 percent when the classifier has never seen an occluded target. Multi-object scenes are limited by interference between overlapping returns rather than by angular coverage, so presence detection saturates after roughly four transmitters.
item.title: Multistatic Terahertz ISAC for Object Shape Identification

AI.conclusion: FM生成式框架可联合生成连续TM-IRS配置，在保证合法用户SINR的同时增强物理层安全扰乱，且训练效率与扩展性优于顺序离散生成方法。
AI.method: 提出基于Flow Matching（FM）的生成式框架，联合生成连续的TM-IRS时间调制参数；针对OFDM信号设计物理信息奖励，最大化合法用户响应零空间中的时间调制谐波能量，并以每子载波最小SINR为约束，无需已知窃听者方向。
AI.motivation: TM-IRS通过时间调制实现方向调制，为合法用户提供可靠接收同时对窃听者形成扰乱，但现有GFlowNet方法按离散参数顺序生成配置，训练慢且扩展性差。
AI.relevance_reason: 涉及RIS与生成式AI方法，但核心是TM-IRS方向调制与物理层安全，而非CSI获取、信道估计或CSI反馈压缩，仅方法层面可迁移。
AI.result: 与GFlowNet基线相比，训练损失接近饱和的时间平均减少99.4%（3×3至12×12表面），最终奖励更高，可扩展至80×80，低误符号区域更紧密地限制在合法用户周围。
AI.tldr: 提出基于Flow Matching的TM-IRS时间调制参数生成框架，联合生成连续配置，以物理信息奖励最大化零空间谐波能量并约束合法用户SINR，训练效率较GFlowNet提升99.4%且可扩展至80×80。

item.summary: Time-modulated intelligent reflecting surfaces (TM-IRS) achieve directional modulation by switching their elements on and off at designed instants and durations, so that an undistorted signal reaches the intended user while appearing scrambled elsewhere. We propose a Flow Matching (FM)-based generative framework that designs these parameters for strong scrambling and reliable reception simultaneously. For orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) signals, we introduce a physics-informed reward that maximizes the time-modulation harmonic energy radiated in the null space of the legitimate-user response, subject to a minimum per-subcarrier signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR), without requiring knowledge of adversary directions. Unlike prior generative flow network (GFlowNet) approaches, which assign discretized parameters sequentially, the FM model generates complete continuous configurations jointly, decoupling the generation depth from the number of elements and accelerating training. It also learns a distribution over configurations that can be resampled to vary the scrambling pattern. Numerical results show that, compared with a GFlowNet baseline, the proposed approach reduces the time to training loss near-saturation by $99.4\%$ on average for $3{\times}3$ to $12{\times}12$ surfaces, attains higher final rewards, scales to $80{\times}80$, and confines the low-symbol-error region more tightly around the legitimate user.
item.title: Generative Control of Time-Modulated Intelligent Reflecting Surfaces for Scalable Directional Modulation

AI.conclusion: 利用零填充诱导的Toeplitz Gram结构可实现闭式、低复杂度的精确SVD收发设计，在保持接近先进接收机性能的同时显著降低复杂度，为ISI信道下的预编码、均衡与编码调制联合设计提供了实用方案。

item.summary: We propose a low-complexity SVD-based transceiver for zero-padded memory-$1$ ISI channels. Appending a single zero-padding symbol to an $n$-symbol block yields an $n\times(n-1)$ channel matrix with an \emph{exact symmetric tridiagonal Toeplitz Gram matrix}. This structure provides closed-form singular values and vectors, enabling exact SVD precoding and equalization via FFTs without explicitly forming dense SVD matrices. The resulting implementation has $O(n\log n)$ complexity and incurs only a $1/n$ rate penalty. The resulting parallel scalar subchannels enable joint adaptive PAM and power allocation for SER minimization, followed by exact soft-information computation for LDPC decoding. At comparable code rates near $0.945$, simulations show that our proposed scheme outperforms a conventional TX-FFE/RX-DFE system with hard-decision Reed-Solomon (RS) decoding by approximately $5$ dB at FER $10^{-5}$. At high SNR, it achieves nearly the same FER performance as a SOVA-based receiver with LDPC decoding, while replacing trellis-based detection with fast SVD precoding and exact scalar soft-output computation.
item.title: Low-Complexity SVD-Based Precoding over Zero-Padded ISI Channels

item.summary: Moving dilated arrays (MDAs) can increase the uniform degrees of freedom (uDOFs) while alleviating mutual coupling, but their performance is susceptible to unknown gain and phase errors (GPEs). To deal with this problem, we investigate self-calibration direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation for MDAs with unknown GPEs. First, multi-position observations are phase aligned to construct an equivalent virtual array with an enlarged aperture. Next, the motion-induced relationships among the GPEs are exploited to establish explicit calibration constraints. By leveraging the orthogonality between the steering vectors and the noise subspace, the joint estimation of the DOAs and GPEs is formulated as a constrained optimization problem. To solve this problem, a two-stage alternating optimization (AO) algorithm is developed. In the first stage, the GPEs are estimated in closed form with the DOAs fixed. In the second stage, the estimated GPEs are used to calibrate the covariance matrix, after which the DOAs are refined using the multiple signal classification (MUSIC) algorithm. To obtain reliable initial estimates, a rotational invariance-like (RIL) initialization method is further developed by exploiting two translated virtual subarrays with identical GPEs. Furthermore, the Cramer-Rao bound (CRB) is derived to characterize the theoretical performance limit of the considered system. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method converges reliably and achieves accurate DOA estimation under different array apertures, numbers of snapshots, GPE levels, and numbers of sources.
item.title: Self-Calibration DOA Estimation for Moving Dilated Arrays with Gain and Phase Errors

item.summary: We study the relationship between strong data-processing inequalities for Rényi divergences and hypercontractivity. For Rényi divergences of order greater than one, we characterize the contraction of Rényi divergences through a property of the dual Markov operator that we name power contraction. Using the contraction coefficient, we derive an upper bound on rectangle probabilities in terms of their marginals that is at least as strong as the corresponding bound obtained via hypercontractivity. Combining this result with inversion of the binary Rényi divergence, we derive communication lower bounds for one-way communication-assisted agreement distillation. Examples involving binary symmetric and rare-event Z-channels illustrate the improvements over standard hypercontractive converses.
item.title: Beyond Hypercontractivity: Stronger Communication Converses via Rényi Contraction

item.summary: Consumer rotating devices, including washing machines, air conditioners, electric fans, robotic vacuum cleaners, and home fitness equipment, increasingly rely on vibration sensing for intelligent condition monitoring and predictive maintenance. Ensuring reliable operation in these resource-constrained appliances requires efficient, lightweight artificial intelligence (AI) solutions capable of processing non-stationary signals under real-world operational interference. This paper proposes a lightweight AI-assisted vibration sensing framework that employs continuous wavelet transform (CWT) and Hilbert-Huang transform (HHT) to convert one-dimensional (1-D) vibration time-series signals into two-dimensional (2-D) time-frequency representations. These representations are subsequently analyzed using lightweight deep learning architectures, specifically MobileNetV3-Small, ConvNeXt-Tiny, and the You Only Look Once version 11 classification model (YOLOv11-cls). Public bearing benchmark datasets, including Case Western Reserve University (CWRU), Paderborn University (PU), and Intelligent Maintenance Systems (IMS), are utilized as representative rotating components to investigate model generalization. The proposed framework is designed with eventual embedded deployment in consumer electronics in mind. Experimental results demonstrate that CWT combined with YOLOv11-cls achieves high diagnostic accuracy, while MobileNetV3-Small provides an attractive low-latency alternative for computationally constrained edge platforms. Conventional random splitting is also compared with dataset-specific structured isolation. The results highlight the importance of avoiding data leakage and quantify tradeoffs in classification accuracy, parameter count, floating-point operations (FLOPs), model footprint, preprocessing cost, and central processing unit (CPU) inference latency.
item.title: Lightweight Time-Frequency Vibration Sensing for Consumer Device Condition Monitoring

item.summary: We study the SNR, aperture, and port count needed to meet a target outage in a single-user downlink with a fixed transmit antenna and a single-RF fluid antenna receiver. For known spatially correlated Rayleigh channels and ideal port selection, a sampling-free residual certificate controls reduced-rank outage error over a continuous SNR interval. Positive Bessel features support large arrays, and bounded importance sampling converts the certificate into simultaneous design intervals. At 1 bit/s/Hz and outage $10^{-5}$, a four-wavelength, ten-port receiver requires 4.40--4.55 dB. Reducing its port count from 256 to ten costs 0.70--1.25 dB under a joint 95\% probability statement. At 3.5 wavelengths, ten ports require 4.90--5.05 dB. Integer-port screening across 3--8 dB shows how aperture and port requirements change with available SNR; an effective-SNR transformation extends these decisions to other rates. The reported intervals include model and sampling uncertainty under checked Gaussian covariance inputs. A constructive slow-growth rank bound and a 16--1024-port study support compact evaluation as port count grows.
item.title: Certified Outage Dimensioning of Fluid Antenna Receivers: Required SNR, Aperture, and Port Count

item.summary: Time-varying aggregate interference from low-Earth-orbit (LEO) satellites challenges terrestrial-network (TN) protection, whereas conservative control degrades LEO quality of service (QoS). This letter proposes a hierarchical framework combining geometry-based interference estimation, QoS-constrained power control, adaptive energy detection, large language model (LLM)-assisted candidate ranking, stay-or-switch decisions, and target-band selection, with deterministic verification. The current band is retained only when both spectrum-hole and power-feasibility conditions hold, with periodic reevaluation. Over a 300-s horizon with 0.5-s sampling, the proposed method keeps the aggregate INR from exceeding the $-12.2$~dB threshold and achieves a time-averaged mean LEO-link rate of $320.97$~Mbps with $100\%$ QoS satisfaction. It markedly outperforms power-only and satellite-muting in jointly protecting the TN and preserving LEO QoS.
item.title: LLM-Assisted Hierarchical Interference Control for Satellite-Terrestrial Integrated Networks

item.summary: Evaluating 5G positioning on a physical testbed ties every measurement to one propagation environment and one antenna layout, so any question about an alternative deployment requires a new field campaign. We present a ray-traced digital twin of the GEO-5G testbed at EURECOM that drives an unmodified OpenAirInterface (OAI) 5G stack with per-antenna channels computed by Sionna-RT over a 3D model of the site. The distributed gNB antennas are modelled as independent radio devices rather than as elements of a compact array, which preserves the per-antenna absolute delays on which time-difference-of-arrival (TDoA) positioning depends. With them preserved, the twin drives OAI's SRS-based UL-TDoA pipeline to metre-level accuracy consistent with that reported for the physical deployment. We then use the twin to answer a question the physical testbed cannot. Widening the carrier truncates the tail of the horizontal error distribution without improving a typical position, and leaves the vertical error untouched, because the latter is limited by the array geometry rather than by the measurement. That limit is predictable from the antenna coordinates alone, and a height-diverse layout reduces the RMS height error by a factor of four.
item.title: A Ray-Traced Digital Twin for 5G NR Positioning with OpenAirInterface

item.summary: Timely information dissemination is essential in modern communication systems, where low informational latency is critical for networked control, monitoring, and real-time decision-making. The Age of Information (AoI) has emerged as a fundamental metric for quantifying information freshness at the receiver. A key challenge in AoI optimization is selecting the update generation rate: infrequent updates lead to stale information, whereas overly frequent updates increase queueing delays. We develop a structure-aware, data-driven framework for adaptive AoI optimization modeled as single-server queues with unknown system statistics. Our key idea is to exploit analytical representations of the AoI gradient, which depend on a finite-dimensional collection of system quantities that can be estimated from observations collected during system operation. This reduces the online learning problem to estimating the quantities required by the gradient, rather than learning the AoI objective as a black box. We propose an online stochastic approximation algorithm that jointly estimates these quantities and optimizes the update generation rate. We prove almost sure convergence of the algorithm to the optimal update generation rate under mild regularity and moment conditions, despite the temporal dependence induced by the underlying queueing process. We demonstrate the framework in four representative incomplete-information settings, including FCFS queues with unknown service characteristics or hidden background traffic, a preemptive LCFS system with partial observations, and a generate-at-will system with threshold waiting.
item.title: Structure-Aware Online Optimization of the Age of Information with Unknown System Statistics

item.summary: This paper considers channel state information (CSI) prediction using neural networks for time-varying multi-antenna channels from noisy historical observations. The main challenge is to exploit temporal correlation while distinguishing channel evolution from observation noise. We propose JEPA-kMMVAE, which combines a joint-embedding predictive architecture with a k-memory Markov variational autoencoder to predict future CSI through temporally structured latent representations. The framework supports direct prediction and residual corrections relative to the latest latent state and noisy CSI observation. Simulation results show that the residual configuration outperforms the evaluated baselines at moderate and high input CSI signal-to-noise ratios, while sequence baselines remain more accurate under stronger noise.
item.title: JEPA-kMMVAE: CSI Prediction for Time-Varying Wireless Channels

item.summary: In this paper, we propose a signal processing concept, signal processing in networks (SPIN), that executes signal processing tasks directly on programmable switches. Traditionally, signal processing tasks, such as denoising, decomposition, and dimensionality reduction, are performed on edge or cloud servers, i.e., raw streams are transmitted from sensors. This imposes a heavy processing load on edge/cloud servers and requires substantial bandwidth. SPIN addresses this problem by performing signal processing on the forwarding path. As an initial realization of SPIN, we implement a DCT-based block transform on a programmable switch. We redesign its computation using a lifting-based lattice structure, multiplierless approximation, and pipeline partitioning across stages in a programmable switch. We verify at the compiler level that the proposed implementation satisfies the strict hardware constraints of the Intel Tofino2--specifically regarding pipeline stages, packet header vector, and ternary content-addressable memory usage--and therefore enables line-rate processing. We further quantify the per-packet latency of the ingress match-action pipeline. The SPIN-oriented preprocessing adds 46 cycles (approximately 31 ns at 1.5 GHz). The total ingress match-action unit latency is approximately 87 ns, which remains consistent with the low-latency operation targeted by SPIN. Furthermore, we implement the proposed block transform on a BMv2 switch using P4 and evaluate it as preprocessing for in-network machine learning. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method improves classification performance over unfiltered baselines.
item.title: Towards Signal Processing In Networks: Multiplierless Block Transforms in Data Plane

item.summary: Large-scale renewable energy profile clustering is a computationally challenging NP-hard problem. Recent quantum computing techniques offer a potential remedy, yet their scalability is severely constrained by the limited qubit count of current quantum hardware. To address this issue, we first cast the problem into a QUBO form and then we propose a consensus-based variable reduction (CBVR) method to drastically cut qubit usage. More specifically, we tailor the one-hot constraint to eliminate assignment variables and leverage consensus analysis to convert stable clustering relations from initial anneals into equality constraints for further reduction. Experiments on real quantum hardware confirm that CBVR compresses oversized QUBO models into feasible sizes while retaining high clustering quality and efficiency.
item.title: Scalable Quantum Clustering of Renewable Profiles via a Hybrid Qubit-efficient Strategy

AI.conclusion: 该工作表明无量化、全分辨率潜在空间的深度水印可在时移下保持较高的比特提取鲁棒性，并借助临床分类器引导的生理损失部分维持诊断语义；但诊断性能的类别级影响不一致，需谨慎评估。

item.summary: Secure transmission of electrocardiogram (ECG) signals remains a major challenge in telecardiology. While traditional mathematical watermarking can embed patient metadata directly into ECG signals, it is highly fragile against temporal desynchronization such as circular phase shifts. In contrast, existing deep watermarking approaches for temporal signals, such as audio, typically rely on lossy quantization, which compromises the high-frequency micro-morphological details critical for clinical diagnosis. To bridge this gap, we propose ECGWmark, a fully convolutional and quantization-free deep watermarking framework for medical time-series. ECGWmark operates in a continuous, full-resolution latent space and utilizes a localized frame-level mechanism to improve the robustness to severe desynchronization. Crucially, we introduce a differentiable Physiological Loss guided by a clinical classifier to preserve diagnostic semantics. Experiments on the benchmark MIT-BIH database show that ECGWmark maintains channel-bit extraction accuracy above 90% under the evaluated circular temporal shifts. Furthermore, under a rigorous inter-patient diagnostic evaluation, Class-V sensitivity changes from 71.97% to 76.50%, whereas Macro-F1 changes from 35.25% to 34.71% and Class-S sensitivity from 8.89% to 1.39%; these results indicate mixed class-level effects.
item.title: ECGWmark: Deep Watermarking for Electrocardiogram Signals

item.summary: We propose a coupling-aware tri-hybrid precoding architecture for simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT) using reconfigurable parasitic antennas. By integrating multiport network theory and information theory, we develop a third precoding layer that explicitly accounts for mutual coupling and reactive energy storage within the antenna domain. To efficiently optimize this architecture, we propose a low-complexity tri-hybrid solution comprising coordinate descent (CD) for parasitic reactive load optimization, a singular value decomposition (SVD)-based analog precoder, and a protective partial zero-forcing (PPZF) digital precoder. Numerical results demonstrate that the transmit array introduces impedance mismatch that reduces the real power accepted by the antenna array. Moreover, the proposed tri-hybrid architecture significantly outperforms hybrid precoding by constructively exploiting the coupling effects, yielding substantial gains in spectral efficiency (SE) and sum non-linear harvested energy (NLHE) at a fraction of the hardware cost.
item.title: Tri-Hybrid SWIPT with Reconfigurable Parasitic Antennas

item.summary: Goal-oriented communication often struggles to sustain downstream task performance under variable and unpredictable bandwidth. We address this problem by proposing GO-OAE (Goal-Oriented Ordered AutoEncoding), which learns a progressively refinable quantized latent sequence, optimized directly for task utility rather than source reconstruction. Each component of the sequence is represented for transmission by its code index, and the learned ordering enables inference from any received prefix of the index sequence, with performance improving as more indices arrive. We prove that optimizing the goal-oriented distortion objective is equivalent to solving a weighted conditional information bottleneck formulation, and introduce an unbiased multi-prefix importance sampling (MPIS) estimator, to reduce GO-OAE training computational cost from O(BK) to O(Bm) with m << K, and reduces the estimator variance by a factor of 1/m. Experiments show that, on MiniImageNet, GO-OAE achieves over 96% of the lossless upper-bound classification accuracy using 324 bits per image (683X compression vs. raw RGB), and already attains over 94% of the upper bound with only 70% of the transmitted indices. It consistently outperforms reconstruction-optimized codecs and ordered autoencoders trained with uniform prefix sampling across all transmission budgets, demonstrating effective communication at extreme compression rates.
item.title: Goal-Oriented Ordered Autoencoding for Successive Refinement in Progressive Communication

item.comment: 16 pages, 3 figures, accepted for publication in the IEEE Signal Processing Magazine
item.summary: Time series causal discovery --- the process of detecting causation between time series --- has its roots in signal processing research from over a half century ago. It has since received active and widespread interest, evolving into different forms across domains such as statistics, dynamical systems and machine learning. Entering this fragmented and constantly evolving research landscape can be daunting. This tutorial provides a unified overview of time series causal discovery across research communities. We introduce the key principles invoked by modern discovery methods, and we discuss their limitations and assumptions. We also discuss how discovery methods are evaluated, benchmarked and fine-tuned. We further discuss how causal discovery for time series is becoming crucial for downstream tasks in agriculture and Earth science, in healthcare, and in artificial intelligence systems. We believe that this tutorial will serve as a valuable resource in navigating the deluge of recent causality research, as well as an invitation to signal processing audiences to contribute to causal problems. To further help readers, we host a companion repository to link to useful code packages and resources at this https URL.
item.title: One Thing Leads to Another: The Essentials of Time Series Causal Discovery

item.summary: This paper addresses the grid quantization error of deep-learning (DL)-based direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation. Classification- based DOA methods discretize the continuous angular space into a grid, so that with a peak-based read-out, the accuracy and resolution are limited by the grid step and by the width of the label peak. To address this issue, we propose a sigmoid label that encodes the sources' DOAs as the sum of angle-shifted monotonic sigmoid functions. Differentiating the output of a CNN-Transformer network trained with the sigmoid label produces sharp spectral peaks at the source DOAs. Combined with a moderately refined grid step of 0.25 degrees, the CNN-Transformer with the proposed sigmoid label attains sub-degree accuracy and a 1-degree resolution, breaking the limit of the grid quantization error. Under the unified CNN-Transformer backbone, we compare the proposed Sigmoid label with the Gaussian label, the 0-1 hard label, and the binary cross-entropy (BCE) baseline. Numerical results demonstrate that the Sigmoid label attains the highest accuracy and superior resolution compared to other labels.
item.title: CNN-Transformer with Sigmoid Label for High-Resolution Sub-Degree DOA Estimation

item.summary: Building upon our preliminary study, this paper proposes a standalone beam-management framework for mobile MIMO-OFDM systems that integrates Blind Initial Beam Acquisition (BIBA) with Clock-Assisted Re-Acquisition (CARA). BIBA is a blind and asynchronous protocol that requires neither prior synchronization nor an out-of-band feedback channel, so the Base Station (BS) and User Equipment (UE) can independently identify the beam pair maximizing received signal strength. To handle subsequent link drops, the newly introduced CARA protocol exploits the clock synchronization established after BIBA to reduce the re-acquisition time by approximately 55% compared with BIBA. The operational reliability of both protocols is bounded by a probabilistic feasibility analysis under random UE mobility trajectories. Protocols are validated on a 28 GHz mmWave testbed under practical hardware constraints, including beam-switching and Time Division Duplex (TDD) latencies, and measured Software-Defined Radio (SDR) software processing delays. Finally, we formulate a unified Finite State Machine (FSM) model for both BIBA and CARA to ensure robust integration into practical wireless systems
item.title: Blind and Asynchronous Initial Beam Acquisition and Clock-Assisted Re-Acquisition in Standalone Mobile MIMO-OFDM Systems

item.summary: Adaptive notch filters (ANFs) based on the normalized least mean squares (NLMS) algorithm are an established technique for suppressing narrowband interference in GNSS receivers. The traditional solution for multiple interferers is simply cascading the NLMS-ANF into multiple stages but this solution degrades performance when multiple chirp jammers of similar power are present. We propose a low-complexity modification to the cascaded NLMS-ANF update rule to resolve this: a local gradient (LG) formulation: LG-ANF. The LG-ANF forms a locally bandlimited gradient signal by translating the input to baseband around the current frequency estimate, low-pass filtering it, and translating it back, thereby attenuating competing interferers before adaptation. The modification generalizes the traditional NLMS-ANF to handle the similar-power multiple interferer problem, using just one additional parameter. We characterize the gradient-averaging failure analytically and visually, demonstrate independent chirp tracking in the worst-case two-chirp scenarios, and evaluate statistical suppression performance by sweeping amplitude ratio against a standard NLMS-ANF, a frequency-locked-loop (FLL)-based ANF and a per-sample oracle upper bound. We further characterize the LG advantage over various ANF parameters and chirp conditions. Simulations show that the LG-ANF reduces to the standard NLMS-ANF outside the pathological multi-chirp regime, while recovering up to 4dB of in-band suppression around pathological amplitude ratios under per-condition optimization of the local bandwidth, and up to 13dB for selected edge-case parameter combinations. These optimized results represent an upper bound on the achievable LG gain. In a hardware experiment using a fixed alpha_lp=0.5, the LG-ANF extends position-lock survival by 24s relative to the standard ANF.
item.title: Suppressing Multiple GNSS Interferers with Local-Gradient Adaptive Notch Filtering

item.summary: The BROJA partial information decomposition provides an operationally motivated way to separate the information that two sources carry about a target into unique, redundant, and synergistic components. For continuous and high-dimensional variables, however, computing the BROJA decomposition requires solving a difficult optimization problem. Previous work showed that, when each source-target pair is jointly Gaussian, the problem can be reduced to finite-dimensional numerical optimization. Here, we derive a closed-form solution to this optimization problem, enabling direct computation of the BROJA decomposition in the general multivariate Gaussian setting. The resulting closed-form expression enables speedups exceeding two orders of magnitude for high-dimensional Gaussian BROJA PID. Code is available at this https URL.

item.summary: This paper presents a data-driven approach to lossless and lossy source compression using polar codes. Classical polar source coding achieves fundamental limits with low complexity for binary memoryless sources. However, for unknown q-ary sources with memory, successive-cancellation (SC) decoding requires an explicit source model and can be computationally prohibitive. We present analytical SC recursions and show that exact implementations scale quadratically with alphabet size and cubically with state-space size. To overcome these limitations, we develop neural polar decoders trained directly from data to approximate conditional distributions of synthetic polar coordinates without requiring an explicit source model. These learned distributions enable estimation of entropy rates, mutual information, and rate-distortion functions, and support explicit polar compression schemes. For lossless compression, we identify high-entropy polarized coordinates and reconstruct the remaining coordinates using the learned SC recursion. For lossy compression, we combine neural polar decoders with a neural test channel to estimate and optimize the mutual information-distortion tradeoff and construct an explicit lossy polar code. We also extend the framework to Wyner-Ziv compression with decoder side information by learning conditional polarized distributions and a reconstruction mapping. Experiments on memoryless sources, sources with memory, and real genomic data show that the learned decoders closely match analytical SC decoders when available and remain applicable when conventional methods are computationally infeasible or the source model is unavailable.
item.title: Neural Polar Codes for Source Coding

item.summary: High-frequency (HF) single-station localization estimates an emitter location from measured directions of arrival (DOAs) and an ionospheric propagation model. When the propagation mode composition cannot be identified from conventional direction-finding (DF) measurements, the same DF observation may produce multiple physically valid ground landing points under different propagation modes, making the location inversion ambiguous. This paper proposes a multimode time-frequency information fusion localization method (MTFIF-L).Rather than assuming a propagation mode a priori, MTFIF-L retains valid landing points generated under different propagation modes and uses repeated observations across time windows and, when available, multiple operating frequencies to progressively constrain the resulting candidate locations. Experiments on four measured HF links examine the respective roles of multimode candidate retention, cross-window processing, and cross-frequency processing. All four links yield unique location decisions. Links A--C achieve relative errors of $1.40\%$, $0.78\%$, and $3.41\%$, this http URL D, the only single-frequency case, also yields a unique decision from repeated temporal observations, although its post- localization error is substantially larger. Propagation-path analysis further reveals link-dependent differences in reflection layer, hop count, magnetoionic mode, and elevation angle among the ray-tracing paths associated with the measured this http URL, the results show that repeated temporal observations can support localization within an individual frequency, while multifrequency information provides additional robustness against unreliable frequency-specific outcomes, enabling HF single-station localization under unknown and potentially coexisting propagation modes while retaining interpretable propagation information for post-localization analysis.
item.title: HF Single-Station Localization via Multimode Ray Tracing and Time-Frequency Information Fusion

item.summary: Medical ultrasound is a widely accessible, real-time imaging modality, yet progress in data-driven ultrasound research is constrained by the scarcity of large, open collections of raw channel data. Existing public datasets are predominantly based on reconstructed images, while the smaller number of open raw channel datasets is generally specialized to individual reconstruction or imaging tasks, limiting the development of general-purpose methods and foundation models that operate directly on ultrasound signals. While interpretive tasks can be performed on reconstructed images, many of the key technical challenges in ultrasound imaging, such as aberration correction and reverberation reduction, require the raw channel data itself. We introduce OpenH-RF, a community-driven open dataset initiative comprising approximately 40 TB of medical ultrasound raw channel data in 19,332 acquisitions, contributed by 38 institutions across academia and industry, spanning in-vivo, phantom, and simulated data. Each dataset is annotated with a number of supported tasks, ranging from generalized reconstruction, speed-of-sound estimation, and aberration correction to blood flow imaging, motion estimation, quantitative ultrasound, and image interpretation. OpenH-RF provides a unified, self-contained data format that captures raw channel data together with the acquisition, probe, metadata, and reconstruction information required for reproducible processing across scanners and acquisition schemes. The corpus is publicly hosted under a permissive CC BY 4.0 license and can be streamed programmatically and selectively at scale. By bringing heterogeneous ultrasound data into a common representation, backed by modern data infrastructure, OpenH-RF lowers the barrier to working with raw channel data and aims to open medical ultrasound research to new communities. See this https URL.
item.title: OpenH-RF: A Large-Scale Ultrasound Raw Channel Dataset Initiative

item.summary: We study the design of a statistical privacy mechanism under a bounded $\alpha$-lift leakage constraint. An agent observes useful data $Y$, which is arbitrarily correlated with private data $X$, and releases $U$. The goal is to maximize Pearson $\chi^2$-information $\chi^2(Y;U)$ while satisfying the point-wise privacy constraint. This utility is an $f$-information that is nonnegative, obeys data processing, and measures the aggregate normalized change from the prior $P_Y$ to the posteriors $P_{Y|U=u}$. The main benefit of this choice is that $\chi^2(Y;U)$ is exactly quadratic in the posterior perturbations; hence, no local approximation of the utility is required. For the nonlinear $\alpha$-lift constraint, we derive a uniform Taylor-remainder bound that remains valid for the optimizing, $\epsilon$-dependent perturbation. When $P_{X|Y}$ is invertible, this yields a closed-form quadratic surrogate, an explicitly scaled binary mechanism that satisfies the original $\alpha$-lift constraint, a computable sufficient range for $\epsilon$, and an $O(\epsilon^{3/2})$ bound on the utility gap. For $\alpha=2$, the solution is exact over an explicit range. We transfer these results to point-wise Rényi-divergence privacy, including an exact-feasible mechanism, an explicit privacy-budget range, and matching gap bounds. We also give an exact formulation for arbitrary leakage matrices and evaluate exact-feasible mechanisms numerically.
item.title: On Privacy Mechanism Design Under a Bounded $α$-Lift Leakage Constraint with $χ^2$-Utility

item.summary: Consider a queueing system operated by Bob, which is intended to serve only jobs generated by a legitimate user, Willie. Willie's jobs arrive according to a Poisson process, and the service times are exponentially distributed. Bob seeks to covertly serve additional jobs arriving according to an independent Poisson process, without Willie detecting their presence. As the legitimate user, Willie is provided with certain statistics of each busy period by Bob. In particular, we consider two statistics: (i) the number of jobs served during each busy period and (ii) the duration of each busy period. We establish that, under either statistic, the maximum expected number of additional jobs that Bob can covertly serve obeys a square-root law. Specifically, over n busy periods, Bob can covertly serve additional jobs in the order of square root of n, whereas any scaling which is above square root of n enables Willie to asymptotically detect the presence of these additional jobs with vanishing error probability. Furthermore, we characterize the scaling constant associated with the square-root law, which we refer to as the covert queueing constant, for each of the two statistics. We compare the scaling constants corresponding to the two statistics and argue that the scaling constant under statistic (i) is no greater than that under statistic (ii).
item.title: Fundamental Limits of Covert queueing under Busy-Period Observations

item.summary: We consider the demand-private coded caching problem with heterogeneous file sizes and cache capacities, where each user must recover its requested file without learning any information about the demands of the other users. We first extend the virtual-user reduction technique to accommodate heterogeneous cache sizes, thereby enabling the construction of demand-private coded caching schemes from non-private schemes. Our main contribution is an exact characterization of the memory-rate trade-off for the fundamental setting of two users and two files with arbitrary file sizes and cache capacities. Specifically, we characterize the optimal trade-off through eight linear inequalities and establish achievability by constructing explicit coded caching schemes for the non-trivial corner points, followed by memory sharing. These constructions include novel asymmetric cache placement strategies tailored to heterogeneous file sizes and cache capacities. For the converse, we exploit the distributional equivalences induced by demand privacy to derive information-theoretic lower bounds that explicitly account for the underlying heterogeneity. Our results generalize the exact memory-rate trade-off characterization for the homogeneous demand-private coded caching setting with two users and two files, while quantifying the additional transmission cost imposed by demand privacy compared with the non-private heterogeneous setting.
item.title: Heterogeneous Demand-Private Coded Caching: Exact Characterization for Two Users and Two Files

2610.12588.summary: Near-field communication with large antenna arrays requires beamforming techniques that account for spherical wavefront effects. While predefined codebooks are widely used in multiple-antenna wireless systems, the performance of randomly generated codebooks in the near-field region has not been investigated. In this work, we study four randomly generated codebooks for near-field communications: random vector quantization (RVQ), random phase (RP), random far-field (RFF), and random near-field (RNF) codebooks. We use the known RVQ gain distribution as a benchmark. For RP, we derive a large-array bulk approximation and characterize the high-gain tail behavior of the gain distribution. For RNF, we characterize the high-gain tail behavior of the gain distribution. For RFF, we derive an analytical approximation for the maximum achievable beamforming gain when far-field beams are used to serve near-field users, along with the corresponding maximizing far-field direction. We also analyze the maximum-gain scaling with codebook size. Monte Carlo simulations verify the analytical results and show that RVQ and RP degrade significantly as the array size increases, while RNF achieves the most favorable high-gain scaling. RFF can outperform RVQ and RP for finite codebook sizes, but its maximum gain saturates below one due to the phase mismatch between the far-field beams and the near-field channel. These results show how codebook structure, array size, and codebook size affect random beamforming performance in the near-field.
2610.12588.title: On the Performance of Randomly Generated Codebooks in Near-Field Communications

2610.12592.summary: This paper introduces an enhanced channel estimation method for reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) communications. Considering the presence of both the direct link from the base station (BS) to the user equipment (UE) and the indirect link \textit{via} the RIS, we formulate a tensor-based receiver for joint direct and indirect channel estimation called the TenDICE algorithm. The proposed receiver relies on an extended parallel factor analysis (PARAFAC) tensor model for the received pilot signals, from which the involved (direct and indirect link) channels are estimated using a simple alternating least squares scheme. The proposed TenDICE method is compared with the state-of-the-art least squares (LS) method, Khatri-Rao factorization (KRF) method, enhanced trilinear alternating least squares (E-TALS), and the theoretical Cramér-Rao lower bound (CRLB) based on normalized mean square error (NMSE) and spectral efficiency (SE). The proposed TenDICE outperforms the LS and E-TALS methods and performs similarly to the KRF methods while estimating the direct channel.
2610.12592.title: Simultaneous Direct and Indirect Channel Estimation for RIS-Assisted MIMO Communications

2610.12604.summary: This paper presents a low-complexity tensor-based channel estimation framework for downlink mmWave massive MIMO systems using passive Butler-matrix beamforming. By modeling received signals as a third-order PARAFAC tensor, we exploit known pilot structures via bilinear alternating least-squares (BALS) optimization to reduce computational overhead. The decoupled spatial factors are then processed via 1D and 2D ESPRIT to extract angles of arrival and departure with automatic pairing. Additionally, we derive the Cramer--Rao lower bound (CRLB) for this architecture. Simulations confirm the proposed estimator outperforms conventional least-squares, achieving accurate channel reconstruction and approaching the CRLB at moderate-to-high signal-to-noise ratios.
2610.12604.title: Low-Complexity Tensor-Based Channel Parameter Estimation for mmWave MIMO-Assisted Systems

2610.12686.comment: 6 pages, 5 figures, 2 tables. Accepted to IEEE GLOBECOM 2026 Workshops (Third Workshop on Positioning and Sensing Over Wireless Networks)
2610.12686.summary: 6G networks are expected to sense their surroundings using the same waveforms that carry data. We ask how much can be learned about the shape of an object from the terahertz echoes that user equipment transmissions produce as they scatter from that object on their way to a ceiling-mounted access point, with no sensing hardware beyond the communication link itself. We build a physics-based multistatic forward model at a 300 GHz carrier with 50 GHz of bandwidth, combining Physical Optics (PO) and Physical Theory of Diffraction (PTD) scattering with an image-source multipath lattice, molecular absorption and directional horn antennas. The model makes explicit a property of the PO mechanism hierarchy that is usually left implicit. Six physically distinct mechanisms share only three frequency exponents, so the spectral slope does not by itself determine which mechanisms a target presents and therefore cannot by itself determine its geometry. Angular diversity is accordingly a requirement for identifiability rather than an optional refinement. We compare a transmitter-count-invariant 2D-CNN with a physics-informed RBF-SVM on object orientations never seen in training. Accuracy climbs from roughly 70 percent with one transmitter to 96-97 percent with 20. The CNN gains in two regimes, irregular placement and lossy targets, while on metal under quasi-uniform placement the SVM baseline is fully competitive. Performance falls off gradually under occlusion, holding 78 percent with three quarters of the surface hidden and 63 percent when the classifier has never seen an occluded target. Multi-object scenes are limited by interference between overlapping returns rather than by angular coverage, so presence detection saturates after roughly four transmitters.
2610.12686.title: Multistatic Terahertz ISAC for Object Shape Identification

2610.12773.summary: Time-modulated intelligent reflecting surfaces (TM-IRS) achieve directional modulation by switching their elements on and off at designed instants and durations, so that an undistorted signal reaches the intended user while appearing scrambled elsewhere. We propose a Flow Matching (FM)-based generative framework that designs these parameters for strong scrambling and reliable reception simultaneously. For orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) signals, we introduce a physics-informed reward that maximizes the time-modulation harmonic energy radiated in the null space of the legitimate-user response, subject to a minimum per-subcarrier signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR), without requiring knowledge of adversary directions. Unlike prior generative flow network (GFlowNet) approaches, which assign discretized parameters sequentially, the FM model generates complete continuous configurations jointly, decoupling the generation depth from the number of elements and accelerating training. It also learns a distribution over configurations that can be resampled to vary the scrambling pattern. Numerical results show that, compared with a GFlowNet baseline, the proposed approach reduces the time to training loss near-saturation by $99.4\%$ on average for $3{\times}3$ to $12{\times}12$ surfaces, attains higher final rewards, scales to $80{\times}80$, and confines the low-symbol-error region more tightly around the legitimate user.
2610.12773.title: Generative Control of Time-Modulated Intelligent Reflecting Surfaces for Scalable Directional Modulation

2610.12784.summary: We propose a low-complexity SVD-based transceiver for zero-padded memory-$1$ ISI channels. Appending a single zero-padding symbol to an $n$-symbol block yields an $n\times(n-1)$ channel matrix with an \emph{exact symmetric tridiagonal Toeplitz Gram matrix}. This structure provides closed-form singular values and vectors, enabling exact SVD precoding and equalization via FFTs without explicitly forming dense SVD matrices. The resulting implementation has $O(n\log n)$ complexity and incurs only a $1/n$ rate penalty. The resulting parallel scalar subchannels enable joint adaptive PAM and power allocation for SER minimization, followed by exact soft-information computation for LDPC decoding. At comparable code rates near $0.945$, simulations show that our proposed scheme outperforms a conventional TX-FFE/RX-DFE system with hard-decision Reed-Solomon (RS) decoding by approximately $5$ dB at FER $10^{-5}$. At high SNR, it achieves nearly the same FER performance as a SOVA-based receiver with LDPC decoding, while replacing trellis-based detection with fast SVD precoding and exact scalar soft-output computation.
2610.12784.title: Low-Complexity SVD-Based Precoding over Zero-Padded ISI Channels

2610.12934.summary: Moving dilated arrays (MDAs) can increase the uniform degrees of freedom (uDOFs) while alleviating mutual coupling, but their performance is susceptible to unknown gain and phase errors (GPEs). To deal with this problem, we investigate self-calibration direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation for MDAs with unknown GPEs. First, multi-position observations are phase aligned to construct an equivalent virtual array with an enlarged aperture. Next, the motion-induced relationships among the GPEs are exploited to establish explicit calibration constraints. By leveraging the orthogonality between the steering vectors and the noise subspace, the joint estimation of the DOAs and GPEs is formulated as a constrained optimization problem. To solve this problem, a two-stage alternating optimization (AO) algorithm is developed. In the first stage, the GPEs are estimated in closed form with the DOAs fixed. In the second stage, the estimated GPEs are used to calibrate the covariance matrix, after which the DOAs are refined using the multiple signal classification (MUSIC) algorithm. To obtain reliable initial estimates, a rotational invariance-like (RIL) initialization method is further developed by exploiting two translated virtual subarrays with identical GPEs. Furthermore, the Cramer-Rao bound (CRB) is derived to characterize the theoretical performance limit of the considered system. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method converges reliably and achieves accurate DOA estimation under different array apertures, numbers of snapshots, GPE levels, and numbers of sources.
2610.12934.title: Self-Calibration DOA Estimation for Moving Dilated Arrays with Gain and Phase Errors

2610.13030.summary: We study the relationship between strong data-processing inequalities for Rényi divergences and hypercontractivity. For Rényi divergences of order greater than one, we characterize the contraction of Rényi divergences through a property of the dual Markov operator that we name power contraction. Using the contraction coefficient, we derive an upper bound on rectangle probabilities in terms of their marginals that is at least as strong as the corresponding bound obtained via hypercontractivity. Combining this result with inversion of the binary Rényi divergence, we derive communication lower bounds for one-way communication-assisted agreement distillation. Examples involving binary symmetric and rare-event Z-channels illustrate the improvements over standard hypercontractive converses.
2610.13030.title: Beyond Hypercontractivity: Stronger Communication Converses via Rényi Contraction

2610.13040.comment: 6 pages, 3 figures, and 4 tables. Submitted to the 2027 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics (ICCE 2027)
2610.13040.summary: Consumer rotating devices, including washing machines, air conditioners, electric fans, robotic vacuum cleaners, and home fitness equipment, increasingly rely on vibration sensing for intelligent condition monitoring and predictive maintenance. Ensuring reliable operation in these resource-constrained appliances requires efficient, lightweight artificial intelligence (AI) solutions capable of processing non-stationary signals under real-world operational interference. This paper proposes a lightweight AI-assisted vibration sensing framework that employs continuous wavelet transform (CWT) and Hilbert-Huang transform (HHT) to convert one-dimensional (1-D) vibration time-series signals into two-dimensional (2-D) time-frequency representations. These representations are subsequently analyzed using lightweight deep learning architectures, specifically MobileNetV3-Small, ConvNeXt-Tiny, and the You Only Look Once version 11 classification model (YOLOv11-cls). Public bearing benchmark datasets, including Case Western Reserve University (CWRU), Paderborn University (PU), and Intelligent Maintenance Systems (IMS), are utilized as representative rotating components to investigate model generalization. The proposed framework is designed with eventual embedded deployment in consumer electronics in mind. Experimental results demonstrate that CWT combined with YOLOv11-cls achieves high diagnostic accuracy, while MobileNetV3-Small provides an attractive low-latency alternative for computationally constrained edge platforms. Conventional random splitting is also compared with dataset-specific structured isolation. The results highlight the importance of avoiding data leakage and quantify tradeoffs in classification accuracy, parameter count, floating-point operations (FLOPs), model footprint, preprocessing cost, and central processing unit (CPU) inference latency.
2610.13040.title: Lightweight Time-Frequency Vibration Sensing for Consumer Device Condition Monitoring

2610.13094.summary: We study the SNR, aperture, and port count needed to meet a target outage in a single-user downlink with a fixed transmit antenna and a single-RF fluid antenna receiver. For known spatially correlated Rayleigh channels and ideal port selection, a sampling-free residual certificate controls reduced-rank outage error over a continuous SNR interval. Positive Bessel features support large arrays, and bounded importance sampling converts the certificate into simultaneous design intervals. At 1 bit/s/Hz and outage $10^{-5}$, a four-wavelength, ten-port receiver requires 4.40--4.55 dB. Reducing its port count from 256 to ten costs 0.70--1.25 dB under a joint 95\% probability statement. At 3.5 wavelengths, ten ports require 4.90--5.05 dB. Integer-port screening across 3--8 dB shows how aperture and port requirements change with available SNR; an effective-SNR transformation extends these decisions to other rates. The reported intervals include model and sampling uncertainty under checked Gaussian covariance inputs. A constructive slow-growth rank bound and a 16--1024-port study support compact evaluation as port count grows.
2610.13094.title: Certified Outage Dimensioning of Fluid Antenna Receivers: Required SNR, Aperture, and Port Count

2610.13108.summary: Time-varying aggregate interference from low-Earth-orbit (LEO) satellites challenges terrestrial-network (TN) protection, whereas conservative control degrades LEO quality of service (QoS). This letter proposes a hierarchical framework combining geometry-based interference estimation, QoS-constrained power control, adaptive energy detection, large language model (LLM)-assisted candidate ranking, stay-or-switch decisions, and target-band selection, with deterministic verification. The current band is retained only when both spectrum-hole and power-feasibility conditions hold, with periodic reevaluation. Over a 300-s horizon with 0.5-s sampling, the proposed method keeps the aggregate INR from exceeding the $-12.2$~dB threshold and achieves a time-averaged mean LEO-link rate of $320.97$~Mbps with $100\%$ QoS satisfaction. It markedly outperforms power-only and satellite-muting in jointly protecting the TN and preserving LEO QoS.
2610.13108.title: LLM-Assisted Hierarchical Interference Control for Satellite-Terrestrial Integrated Networks

2610.13138.comment: submitted at 22nd Wireless On-demand Network systems and Services Conference
2610.13138.summary: Evaluating 5G positioning on a physical testbed ties every measurement to one propagation environment and one antenna layout, so any question about an alternative deployment requires a new field campaign. We present a ray-traced digital twin of the GEO-5G testbed at EURECOM that drives an unmodified OpenAirInterface (OAI) 5G stack with per-antenna channels computed by Sionna-RT over a 3D model of the site. The distributed gNB antennas are modelled as independent radio devices rather than as elements of a compact array, which preserves the per-antenna absolute delays on which time-difference-of-arrival (TDoA) positioning depends. With them preserved, the twin drives OAI's SRS-based UL-TDoA pipeline to metre-level accuracy consistent with that reported for the physical deployment. We then use the twin to answer a question the physical testbed cannot. Widening the carrier truncates the tail of the horizontal error distribution without improving a typical position, and leaves the vertical error untouched, because the latter is limited by the array geometry rather than by the measurement. That limit is predictable from the antenna coordinates alone, and a height-diverse layout reduces the RMS height error by a factor of four.
2610.13138.title: A Ray-Traced Digital Twin for 5G NR Positioning with OpenAirInterface

2610.13142.summary: Timely information dissemination is essential in modern communication systems, where low informational latency is critical for networked control, monitoring, and real-time decision-making. The Age of Information (AoI) has emerged as a fundamental metric for quantifying information freshness at the receiver. A key challenge in AoI optimization is selecting the update generation rate: infrequent updates lead to stale information, whereas overly frequent updates increase queueing delays. We develop a structure-aware, data-driven framework for adaptive AoI optimization modeled as single-server queues with unknown system statistics. Our key idea is to exploit analytical representations of the AoI gradient, which depend on a finite-dimensional collection of system quantities that can be estimated from observations collected during system operation. This reduces the online learning problem to estimating the quantities required by the gradient, rather than learning the AoI objective as a black box. We propose an online stochastic approximation algorithm that jointly estimates these quantities and optimizes the update generation rate. We prove almost sure convergence of the algorithm to the optimal update generation rate under mild regularity and moment conditions, despite the temporal dependence induced by the underlying queueing process. We demonstrate the framework in four representative incomplete-information settings, including FCFS queues with unknown service characteristics or hidden background traffic, a preemptive LCFS system with partial observations, and a generate-at-will system with threshold waiting.
2610.13142.title: Structure-Aware Online Optimization of the Age of Information with Unknown System Statistics

2610.13315.summary: This paper considers channel state information (CSI) prediction using neural networks for time-varying multi-antenna channels from noisy historical observations. The main challenge is to exploit temporal correlation while distinguishing channel evolution from observation noise. We propose JEPA-kMMVAE, which combines a joint-embedding predictive architecture with a k-memory Markov variational autoencoder to predict future CSI through temporally structured latent representations. The framework supports direct prediction and residual corrections relative to the latest latent state and noisy CSI observation. Simulation results show that the residual configuration outperforms the evaluated baselines at moderate and high input CSI signal-to-noise ratios, while sequence baselines remain more accurate under stronger noise.
2610.13315.title: JEPA-kMMVAE: CSI Prediction for Time-Varying Wireless Channels

2610.13324.comment: Submitted to the 2027 ICASSP-OJSP track, 9 pages, 4 figures
2610.13324.summary: In this paper, we propose a signal processing concept, signal processing in networks (SPIN), that executes signal processing tasks directly on programmable switches. Traditionally, signal processing tasks, such as denoising, decomposition, and dimensionality reduction, are performed on edge or cloud servers, i.e., raw streams are transmitted from sensors. This imposes a heavy processing load on edge/cloud servers and requires substantial bandwidth. SPIN addresses this problem by performing signal processing on the forwarding path. As an initial realization of SPIN, we implement a DCT-based block transform on a programmable switch. We redesign its computation using a lifting-based lattice structure, multiplierless approximation, and pipeline partitioning across stages in a programmable switch. We verify at the compiler level that the proposed implementation satisfies the strict hardware constraints of the Intel Tofino2--specifically regarding pipeline stages, packet header vector, and ternary content-addressable memory usage--and therefore enables line-rate processing. We further quantify the per-packet latency of the ingress match-action pipeline. The SPIN-oriented preprocessing adds 46 cycles (approximately 31 ns at 1.5 GHz). The total ingress match-action unit latency is approximately 87 ns, which remains consistent with the low-latency operation targeted by SPIN. Furthermore, we implement the proposed block transform on a BMv2 switch using P4 and evaluate it as preprocessing for in-network machine learning. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method improves classification performance over unfiltered baselines.
2610.13324.title: Towards Signal Processing In Networks: Multiplierless Block Transforms in Data Plane

2610.13336.summary: Large-scale renewable energy profile clustering is a computationally challenging NP-hard problem. Recent quantum computing techniques offer a potential remedy, yet their scalability is severely constrained by the limited qubit count of current quantum hardware. To address this issue, we first cast the problem into a QUBO form and then we propose a consensus-based variable reduction (CBVR) method to drastically cut qubit usage. More specifically, we tailor the one-hot constraint to eliminate assignment variables and leverage consensus analysis to convert stable clustering relations from initial anneals into equality constraints for further reduction. Experiments on real quantum hardware confirm that CBVR compresses oversized QUBO models into feasible sizes while retaining high clustering quality and efficiency.
2610.13336.title: Scalable Quantum Clustering of Renewable Profiles via a Hybrid Qubit-efficient Strategy

2610.13357.summary: Secure transmission of electrocardiogram (ECG) signals remains a major challenge in telecardiology. While traditional mathematical watermarking can embed patient metadata directly into ECG signals, it is highly fragile against temporal desynchronization such as circular phase shifts. In contrast, existing deep watermarking approaches for temporal signals, such as audio, typically rely on lossy quantization, which compromises the high-frequency micro-morphological details critical for clinical diagnosis. To bridge this gap, we propose ECGWmark, a fully convolutional and quantization-free deep watermarking framework for medical time-series. ECGWmark operates in a continuous, full-resolution latent space and utilizes a localized frame-level mechanism to improve the robustness to severe desynchronization. Crucially, we introduce a differentiable Physiological Loss guided by a clinical classifier to preserve diagnostic semantics. Experiments on the benchmark MIT-BIH database show that ECGWmark maintains channel-bit extraction accuracy above 90% under the evaluated circular temporal shifts. Furthermore, under a rigorous inter-patient diagnostic evaluation, Class-V sensitivity changes from 71.97% to 76.50%, whereas Macro-F1 changes from 35.25% to 34.71% and Class-S sensitivity from 8.89% to 1.39%; these results indicate mixed class-level effects.
2610.13357.title: ECGWmark: Deep Watermarking for Electrocardiogram Signals

2610.13402.summary: We propose a coupling-aware tri-hybrid precoding architecture for simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT) using reconfigurable parasitic antennas. By integrating multiport network theory and information theory, we develop a third precoding layer that explicitly accounts for mutual coupling and reactive energy storage within the antenna domain. To efficiently optimize this architecture, we propose a low-complexity tri-hybrid solution comprising coordinate descent (CD) for parasitic reactive load optimization, a singular value decomposition (SVD)-based analog precoder, and a protective partial zero-forcing (PPZF) digital precoder. Numerical results demonstrate that the transmit array introduces impedance mismatch that reduces the real power accepted by the antenna array. Moreover, the proposed tri-hybrid architecture significantly outperforms hybrid precoding by constructively exploiting the coupling effects, yielding substantial gains in spectral efficiency (SE) and sum non-linear harvested energy (NLHE) at a fraction of the hardware cost.
2610.13402.title: Tri-Hybrid SWIPT with Reconfigurable Parasitic Antennas

2610.13426.summary: Goal-oriented communication often struggles to sustain downstream task performance under variable and unpredictable bandwidth. We address this problem by proposing GO-OAE (Goal-Oriented Ordered AutoEncoding), which learns a progressively refinable quantized latent sequence, optimized directly for task utility rather than source reconstruction. Each component of the sequence is represented for transmission by its code index, and the learned ordering enables inference from any received prefix of the index sequence, with performance improving as more indices arrive. We prove that optimizing the goal-oriented distortion objective is equivalent to solving a weighted conditional information bottleneck formulation, and introduce an unbiased multi-prefix importance sampling (MPIS) estimator, to reduce GO-OAE training computational cost from O(BK) to O(Bm) with m << K, and reduces the estimator variance by a factor of 1/m. Experiments show that, on MiniImageNet, GO-OAE achieves over 96% of the lossless upper-bound classification accuracy using 324 bits per image (683X compression vs. raw RGB), and already attains over 94% of the upper bound with only 70% of the transmitted indices. It consistently outperforms reconstruction-optimized codecs and ordered autoencoders trained with uniform prefix sampling across all transmission budgets, demonstrating effective communication at extreme compression rates.
2610.13426.title: Goal-Oriented Ordered Autoencoding for Successive Refinement in Progressive Communication

2610.13430.comment: 16 pages, 3 figures, accepted for publication in the IEEE Signal Processing Magazine
2610.13430.summary: Time series causal discovery --- the process of detecting causation between time series --- has its roots in signal processing research from over a half century ago. It has since received active and widespread interest, evolving into different forms across domains such as statistics, dynamical systems and machine learning. Entering this fragmented and constantly evolving research landscape can be daunting. This tutorial provides a unified overview of time series causal discovery across research communities. We introduce the key principles invoked by modern discovery methods, and we discuss their limitations and assumptions. We also discuss how discovery methods are evaluated, benchmarked and fine-tuned. We further discuss how causal discovery for time series is becoming crucial for downstream tasks in agriculture and Earth science, in healthcare, and in artificial intelligence systems. We believe that this tutorial will serve as a valuable resource in navigating the deluge of recent causality research, as well as an invitation to signal processing audiences to contribute to causal problems. To further help readers, we host a companion repository to link to useful code packages and resources at this https URL.
2610.13430.title: One Thing Leads to Another: The Essentials of Time Series Causal Discovery

2610.13433.summary: This paper addresses the grid quantization error of deep-learning (DL)-based direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation. Classification- based DOA methods discretize the continuous angular space into a grid, so that with a peak-based read-out, the accuracy and resolution are limited by the grid step and by the width of the label peak. To address this issue, we propose a sigmoid label that encodes the sources' DOAs as the sum of angle-shifted monotonic sigmoid functions. Differentiating the output of a CNN-Transformer network trained with the sigmoid label produces sharp spectral peaks at the source DOAs. Combined with a moderately refined grid step of 0.25 degrees, the CNN-Transformer with the proposed sigmoid label attains sub-degree accuracy and a 1-degree resolution, breaking the limit of the grid quantization error. Under the unified CNN-Transformer backbone, we compare the proposed Sigmoid label with the Gaussian label, the 0-1 hard label, and the binary cross-entropy (BCE) baseline. Numerical results demonstrate that the Sigmoid label attains the highest accuracy and superior resolution compared to other labels.
2610.13433.title: CNN-Transformer with Sigmoid Label for High-Resolution Sub-Degree DOA Estimation

2610.13436.summary: Building upon our preliminary study, this paper proposes a standalone beam-management framework for mobile MIMO-OFDM systems that integrates Blind Initial Beam Acquisition (BIBA) with Clock-Assisted Re-Acquisition (CARA).
