DeepTelecom refines coarse indoor/outdoor reconstructions and uses a large language model to map segmented surfaces to frequency-dependent electromagnetic parameters, yielding material-aware Level of Detail 3 digital twins. Then, a differentiable GPU-accelerated Sionna ray tracer simulates propagation across the sub-6 GHz/millimeter-wave/sub-terahertz bands, and specifically captures rotor-induced micro-Doppler signatures of stationary or moving UAVs at different pitch angles and translational velocities. The framework synchronously produces channel tensors, coverage maps, transmission videos, multi-view images, and weather-conditioned renderings, and supports differentiable material calibration from sparse channel anchors. The released dataset contains 10 material-aware indoor/outdoor scenes and 50,000 synchronized UAV samples; the framework supports scalable generation of additional data for user-defined scenes and system configurations. In 3D UAV localization, DeepTelecom reduces the 90th-percentile error from 31.05 m to 2.43 m compared with schemes considering only channel state information, demonstrating its significance for artificial-intelligence-enabled wireless systems.
2610.14545.title: DeepTelecom: A Differentiable Multimodal Framework for Channel Twinning in Dynamic Heterogeneous Wireless Environments

2610.14593.summary: Camera-based beam selection can reduce the need for exhaustive channel measurement in highly mobile millimeter-wave UAV links, but the complementary value of visual and position-derived representations and their behavior under modality degradation require further investigation. This paper develops a staged multimodal framework for current-beam prediction using real-world UAV measurements. The proposed 32-beam classifier combines an ImageNet-pretrained EfficientNet-B3 visual encoder with two deterministic position-derived representations: an explicit Geometric-Kinematic vector and a nonlinear synthetic feature basis constructed from position. The image and synthetic representations are fused first, followed by late fusion with the geometry representation. Experiments on DeepSense 6G Scenario 23 show that Image-Synthetic fusion achieves 86.92% Top-1, 99.03% Top-3, and 99.56% Top-5 accuracy, improving Top-1 performance by 2.64 percentage points over image-only inference and outperforming the 60.71% Top-1 accuracy of synthetic-only inference. Adding the Geometric-Kinematic branch yields the highest measured performance, reaching 87.14% Top-1, 99.12% Top-3, and 99.60% Top-5 accuracy. Controlled input interventions further demonstrate complementary behavior under visual degradation and strong sensitivity to severe synthetic-input corruption. Position-derived nonlinear features provide complementary information to visual context and improve current-beam prediction in the evaluated real-world UAV setting.
2610.14593.title: Efficient Multimodal Beam Prediction for Real-World 6G UAV Communications via Image-Position-Synthetic Fusion

2610.14615.summary: We study autoregressive token generation through the notion of sequential samplers: A circuit that samples the next symbol only given the previous ones and possibly a small amount of state. We show that (1) a sequential sampler with $k$ bits of state can be simulated by a stateless one at a roughly $O(2^{k})$ size overhead; (2) efficient insertional sampling (Stern, Chan, Kiros, Uszkoreit, ICML 2019) is more powerful than efficient sequential sampling in any fixed order; (3) sequential samplers with small state cannot establish certain forms of covert cryptographic channels. Result (1), together with the pseudoentropy vs. sequential sampleability duality of Vadhan and Zheng (STOC 2012), characterizes efficient sequential sampleability with small state. Result (3) provides a potential safety mechanism against subliminal coordination among malicious LLM agents.
2610.14615.title: Limitations on Autoregressive Token Generation via Sequential Sampling

2610.14623.summary: Direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation can degrade markedly in impulsive noise, where methods relying on Gaussian or second-order statistical assumptions are particularly susceptible to large-amplitude outliers. This paper develops an adaptive DOA estimator that employs Gaussian kernel weighting to attenuate the influence of large prediction errors while adjusting the kernel bandwidth online according to a Kullback--Leibler (KL) divergence criterion. A sample-based approximation of the KL criterion yields a recursive bandwidth update that adapts the degree of outlier suppression to the observed error statistics rather than prescribing a fixed bandwidth a priori. The spatial-filter coefficients and kernel bandwidth are updated recursively, and the DOAs are recovered from the resulting spatial spectrum. Mean and mean-square analyses are developed under standard adaptive-filtering approximations to characterize the coefficient convergence and steady-state behavior. Simulation results under Gaussian-mixture impulsive noise demonstrate stable coefficient adaptation and improved DOA estimation accuracy over representative competing methods in several challenging operating regimes, with the most pronounced gains occurring at low-to-moderate signal-to-noise ratios. The results also indicate reduced sensitivity to the initial kernel bandwidth through online bandwidth adaptation.
2610.14623.title: Adaptive DOA Estimation With KL-Based Kernel Bandwidth Adaptation Under Impulsive Noise

2610.14641.summary: A receiver can change its observation state while the physical signal remains the same. In rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) downlinks, this distinction separates receive-beam design and phase-reference transport from the motion of the satellite--UAV line of sight. We formulate receive optimization within the physical--observation dual-axis (PODA) structure and obtain three complementary results. For a known line-of-sight response and positive-definite receiver-noise covariance, a noise-weighted matched combiner simultaneously maximizes every decoding SINR and the minimum user rate. Under directional uncertainty, the principal eigenvector of the conditional response covariance globally maximizes mean array gain; for a Gaussian directional model, an equal-amplitude receiver is optimized by steering towards the conditional mean. Mean rate requires a different objective. We prove that the RSMA common-rate water level is jointly concave in the users' receive gains and derive a semidefinite relaxation with a computable global upper bound. A feasible rank-one beam can therefore be compared directly with the optimum of the finite-scenario problem. We also derive a precision-weighted linear predictor that suppresses uncertain physical-velocity estimates after observation-frame transport. Paired dynamic simulations reduce direction-cosine RMSE by 51.29\% relative to unrestricted nine-point extrapolation. In a separate uncertainty experiment, direct rate optimization increases mean minimum spectral efficiency from 0.32425 to 0.41712 bit/s/Hz, an improvement of 28.64\%; the corresponding design objective is within $2.28\times10^{-4}$ bit/s/Hz of a global upper bound. The phase-transport equation fixes a coherent representative of each optimal beam without changing its gain.
2610.14641.title: Optimal Receive Design on the Observation Axis for RSMA Satellite-UAV Downlinks

2610.14649.comment: The paper is accepeted in GlobeCom 2026
2610.14649.summary: In frequency-division duplex (FDD) systems, the uplink (UL) and downlink (DL) channels are not fully reciprocal. Therefore, DL channel state information (CSI) estimated by each user equipment (UE) must be fed back to the base station (BS). However, because the channel varies between CSI acquisition and utilization, the feedback CSI may become outdated before it is used at the BS. To address this challenge, this paper proposes an UL-assisted parametric CSI feedback and prediction scheme for multi-user FDD systems with time-varying channel parameters. By exploiting the partial reciprocity between the UL and DL channel parameters, the BS first estimates the UL channel parameters from the sounding reference signals (SRSs) transmitted by the UEs. The BS then broadcasts DL pilots, allowing each UE to obtain observations containing information about its current DL channel. Instead of explicitly estimating the DL channel from these observations, each UE directly encodes them into feedback symbols and transmits the symbols to the BS. The BS decoder combines the feedback symbols with the partially reciprocal UL parameters to predict the future DL channel parameters. Finally, the corresponding DL channel matrix is synthesized from the predicted parameters using an explicit physical channel model. Simulation results on Sionna ray tracing (RT) dataset show that the proposed scheme outperforms the considered baselines in terms of channel prediction performance over different signal-to-noise ratios and prediction lengths.
2610.14649.title: UL-Assisted Parametric CSI Feedback and Prediction for FDD Systems

2610.14765.summary: Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) combined with rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) provide a promising solution for improving the spectral efficiency (SE) of sixth-generation (6G) communication systems. However, most existing studies neglect the practical coupling between the RIS phase shift and amplitude, which may cause phase-shift mismatch and significant performance loss. In this paper, we investigate the multiuser sum-rate maximization problem for practical RIS-enhanced RSMA systems considering amplitude-phase coupling. To address the resulting non-convex problem, an effective variable separation algorithm is proposed. The proposed algorithm is compatible with RIS reflecting optimization under the continuous phase shift or any amplitude-phase coupling relationship and can also be directly extended to practical RIS-enhanced NOMA and OMA systems. Simulation results demonstrate performance gain of over 190\% compared with the ideal-RIS-based benchmark, while the proposed RSMA scheme significantly outperforms the corresponding NOMA and OMA schemes.
2610.14765.title: Sum Rate Maximization for Practical RIS-Enhanced Rate-Splitting Multiple Access Systems

2610.14771.summary: Virtual Reality (VR) requires strict Quality-of-Experience (QoE) guarantees, making radio resource management harder. Static slice allocations are wasteful, while dynamic approaches often rely on heuristic penalty functions lacking an empirical basis. We introduce a QoE-driven network-slicing framework for Open RAN in which resource allocation is guided by empirically derived multi-user VR traffic statistics. Closed-form n-fold convolutions model the aggregate data rate and inter-arrival time of n concurrent users, validated empirically for up to four. The fitted data-rate cumulative distribution function is checked against the measured throughput to give a percentile-based satisfaction indicator; the inter-arrival law sets the slice targets. A near-real-time RIC xApp closes a loop over the E2SM-KPM and E2SM-RC interfaces to apply slice-level Physical Resource Block (PRB) quotas. On an over-the-air testbed it reclaims up to 41% of the cell's committed PRBs from a greedy neighbouring slice while never reducing the protected VR slice. An analytical study then estimates the PRB demand and per-user QoE across user counts and channel qualities, giving the admission boundary beyond which the target QoE is unattainable. A controlled comparison further shows that a fixed-rate synthetic load overstates the VR slice's PRB footprint by 68%, showing the necessity of data-driven slice dimensioning.
2610.14771.title: A QoE-Driven Framework for O-RAN Network Slicing Based on Empirical Multi-User VR Traffic Modelling

2610.14822.summary: Multipath and non-line-of-sight (NLOS) propagation degrade global navigation satellite system (GNSS) positioning accuracy in urban environments. Although fisheye sky segmentation identifies obstructions along satellite directions, binary visibility does not fully characterize observation quality. This study proposes a point-supervised visual framework that predicts GNSS observation faults from fisheye images using supervision derived from GNSS observations. During offline labeling, a vision-assisted differential GNSS procedure selects multiple reference satellites based on sky visibility and elevation constraints. Double-difference pseudorange residuals automatically generate fault labels and sample importance weights at satellite projection locations. A residual-weighted loss is computed only at valid labeled points, enabling learning from sparse supervision without manual pixelwise fault annotations. The trained network generates dense fault probability maps, which are sampled at satellite projection locations to weight observations in weighted least squares positioning, reducing the influence of potentially faulty observations. The framework is evaluated using U-Net, DeepLabv3+, DINOv3, and SAM3 on urban vehicle data collected on a different day from the training data. All four models reduce horizontal root mean square error (RMSE) by 29.51% to 36.07% compared with SAM binary sky segmentation, with U-Net achieving the lowest RMSE of 0.78 m. The framework also provides positioning solutions during some intervals when the segmentation baseline fails. These results demonstrate the framework's generalization ability and show that GNSS-derived point supervision enables fisheye images to provide observation quality information beyond binary sky visibility, supporting GNSS fault detection.
2610.14822.title: Point-Supervised Visual Learning for GNSS Measurement Quality Assessment

2610.14882.summary: This paper develops adaptive movable-antenna (MA) array structures to enhance wireless sensing performance under arbitrary SNR conditions, using the AoA estimation MSE as the sensing metric. Due to the presence of strong sidelobes in the ambiguity function of sparse MA arrays, the classical CRB of AoA estimation MSE fails to characterize the true MSE in the low and medium SNR regimes, rendering CRB-optimized antenna position vector designs suboptimal for MA-enabled sensing. We derive a deterministic MSE approximation that captures the local estimation error within the mainlobe of the ambiguity function and the outlier error induced by sidelobes, providing a tractable and accurate optimization objective. We then propose three adaptive MA structures that are tailored to different hardware and computational requirements. For systems with fully independent motors, a movable free array is optimized by a two-stage greedy algorithm, which approaches the performance of the globally optimal exhaustive search but with lower computational complexity. Halving the required motors, a movable nested array fixes the dense inner subarray and adjusts only the outer-subarray spacing, reducing the optimization to a one-dimensional search. As the most hardware-efficient design, a movable twin array is proposed to adjust the inter-subarray spacing only with a single motor, while still achieving significant MSE reduction over fixed array geometries. Numerical results show that the derived approximation closely matches the true MSE compared with existing performance bounds, and that the proposed structures outperform the CRB-optimized designs by orders of magnitude in MSE across the tested low-to-medium SNR range. Moreover, it reveals that in the low-SNR regime, APV reconfiguration is more effective for improving estimation accuracy than simply increasing the number of fixed antennas.
2610.14882.title: MSE Minimization for Movable Antenna Enhanced Wireless Sensing via Array Geometry Optimization

2610.14995.summary: Oscillation monitors have root-mean-square (RMS) energy detectors at their core. These detect oscillation in a predefined frequency band by comparing the signal power in that band with a threshold (usually set empirically). A key design decision is the choice of frequency bands. Traditionally, for monitoring the stability of wide-area electromechanical modes, finer bands were set below 1 Hz, while higher frequencies were covered by wider bands. However, this approach can yield poor detection in modern power systems with fast and largely unknown local dynamics. This letter proposes an algorithm to set frequency bands from the ambient noise spectrum to maximize the average detection performance.
2610.14995.title: Optimally Setting RMS Energy Bands for Detecting Oscillations

2610.15070.summary: This paper proposes a channel-knowledge-map (CKM)-based predictive beamforming framework for integrated sensing, communication, and powering (ISCAP) of a mobile energy-constrained node in non-line-of-sight (NLoS) multipath environments. The CKM provides location-dependent channel information for both predictive beamforming and EKF-based tracking, while resolved path parameters estimated from the sensing echoes are used as observations. Based on the predicted node location, the transmit covariance and power-splitting ratio are jointly optimized to maximize wireless power-transfer efficiency subject to communication, sensing, transmit-power, and tracking-quality constraints. A finite-battery model and an adaptive inter-frame energy-management policy are further introduced to balance decoding energy consumption and battery preservation. The resulting non-convex fractional problem is solved using Dinkelbach's method, alternating optimization, and semidefinite relaxation. Numerical results show that the proposed framework maintains reliable tracking, satisfies the prescribed position-uncertainty requirement, achieves near-oracle wireless power-transfer performance after the initial tracking transient, and preserves more battery energy while meeting the required communication quality of service.
2610.15070.title: CKM-Based Predictive Beamforming for Energy-Efficient Mobile Tracking in ISCAP System

2610.15072.summary: In integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems, strict sensing requirements can substantially constrain the transmit power available for communication. A hybrid reconfigurable intelligent surface (HRIS) with passive reflection and active amplification capabilities mounted on an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) can enhance coverage and strengthen communication links in such power-limited regimes. Meanwhile, rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) provides an effective transmission strategy for managing inter-user interference, particularly in dense multiuser wireless scenarios. Motivated by this, we analyze the performance of a UAV-mounted HRIS-assisted monostatic ISAC system employing RSMA scheme. We consider the imperfections in the channel state information and successive interference cancellation in the RSMA, which are inevitable in practical system implementations. We then derive highly accurate expressions for outage probability, ergodic rate, and throughput to evaluate communication performance over Nakagami-$m$ fading channels. These expressions reveal key insights into the diversity order and coding gain of the system in the high signal-to-noise ratio regime. To characterize the sensing performance, we derive expressions for the probability of detection, the probability of false alarm, and the Cramér-Rao lower bound. Numerical results validate the theoretical findings and highlight the performance gains of the proposed system over conventional multiple-access schemes and RIS-based systems.
2610.15072.title: UAV-Mounted Hybrid RIS-Assisted ISAC-RSMA: Performance Analysis with Imperfect CSI and SIC

2610.15170.summary: In this paper, we consider joint beamforming and power allocation for a mobile multiuser MIMO integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) network with clutter, residual self-interference, and outdated channel state information, under per-user rate and sensing signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) constraints that must hold on every realization. The design must be recomputed every block, and distant or weak targets can make the sensing constraint unmeetable. We propose a physics-informed unsupervised learning (PI-UnSL) network that corrects the analytical design, meets the power and norm constraints exactly by construction, and is conditioned on closed-form interference statistics, spanning the whole tradeoff in one pass. We derive a closed-form sensing SINR at the interference-aware combiner, yielding a necessary range-radar-cross-section-power condition and a priority-independent analytic violation floor, so the problem is intermittently infeasible. We then show that a dual targeting below the attainable floor has no fixed point, and calibrate the label-free objective against the measured floor. Numerical results confirm the floor and the bounded calibrated dual, and show that PI-UnSL substantially raises per-realization joint quality of service over the closed-form baseline, delivers more rate than time-division ISAC at matched detection over most of the tradeoff, and exceeds the reliability of an uncalibrated alternating-optimization solver at a fraction of its latency. More broadly, the physical knowledge given to the network, not its architecture, makes such problems learnable without labels: five architectures fail alike from scratch and perform alike when started from the closed-form design and conditioned on its interference statistics.
2610.15170.title: Physics-Informed Unsupervised Learning for Reliable Beamforming in Cluttered MIMO-ISAC

2610.15178.summary: In this paper, we study functional-split selection for an Open radio access network (RAN) deployed as a non-terrestrial network (NTN), in which a low-Earth-orbit (LEO) satellite hosts the radio unit, so that each candidate split (7.2x, 6, 2) places the RAN at a distinct point of the transparent-to-regenerative axis. We capture the space-ground geometry exactly through an instantaneous link plane, which yields closed-form slant range, elevation, delay, and Doppler for an inclined orbit and a rotating Earth. On this geometry we derive the received-SNR density of the elevation-driven LOS/NLOS mixture channel and, through a split-dependent channel state information (CSI) aging mechanism, an uncoded bit-error-rate (BER) law for each split, establishing that what separates the splits is the freshness of the CSI each brings to its adaptation loops: a loop closed on the ground pays the feeder round-trip and incurs an aging-induced error floor. We formulate split selection as a prefer-centralized feasibility problem over reliability, aging, and fronthaul-capacity constraints, and we show that its exact solution is a closed-form region rule in four state coordinates, validated against exhaustive enumeration without a single mismatch. Because this solution is reactive whereas a split change must be initiated ahead of time, we propose a compact Kolmogorov-Arnold network (KAN)-LSTM, sized for an edge xApp/rApp, that predicts the split schedule seconds ahead; we show that it attains high schedule accuracy at a sub-percent BER-violation probability and delivers nearly all of the ground-truth policy's goodput, outperforming naive and reactive baselines.
2610.15178.title: CSI-Aging-Aware Functional Split Optimization and KAN-LSTM Prediction for Open-RAN NTN

2610.15184.comment: This paper(2-column version) has been accept for publish in IEEE wireless communication letter(WCL)
2610.15184.summary: Sparse near-field arrays phase-cohere $M$ widely separated sub-arrays of $N$ elements and underpin distributed MIMO, satellite formations, and integrated sensing and communication. We show that their interference suppression over a protected region is set by coherence within a single sub-array rather than by the span of the formation: the effective rank of the region covariance can collapse from $MN$ to $M$. Two independent arguments establish this. For canonical line and disk regions each diagonal covariance block is exactly a classical concentration operator, which supplies sharp per-block rank thresholds and makes fewer than one spatial degree of freedom per sub-array a conservative design rule; an orthogonal decomposition with eigenvalue interlacing gives a nonasymptotic sufficient condition that assumes nothing about the coupling between platforms. The consequences are covariance-side and beamformer-independent: the unloaded Capon functional upper-bounds worst-case signal-to-interference ratio, while its regularized counterpart scales very differently for angularly separated and for in-cone targets. An eight-satellite LEO study validates the theory, including realized worst-case SIR.
2610.15184.title: Effective DoF Collapse in Sparse Near-Field Beamforming: A Block-Rank-1 Mechanism

2610.15247.summary: An incomplete inventory creates a specific attribution ambiguity in load disaggregation: unclaimed demand can offset changes in claimed loads without altering meter reconstruction. We study how the allowed target and nuisance trajectories govern this ambiguity. A bounded ordered Markov chain represents unclaimed demand, while an unweighted acceptor removes commissioning-inconsistent paths from one target without reweighting surviving paths; exact factorial MAP jointly decodes all paths. At two fully instrumented commercial buildings, restricting exterior-lighting support improves agreement on the count of rooftop compressors although no compressor chain is constrained; the gain depends on the nuisance representation. A synthetic experiment identifies the boundary: the effect persists under support-preserving changes but reverses when the true path violates commissioned support or the commissioned level is miscalibrated. Attribution therefore depends on joint target-nuisance path geometry, not reconstruction error alone.
2610.15247.title: Load Disaggregation under Incomplete Inventory with Structured Unclaimed Demand

2610.15252.summary: Code conversion changes the parameters of encoded data while avoiding complete decoding and re-encoding. Existing general bounds largely rely on the algebraic structure of linear codes. This paper develops an information-theoretic framework for nonlinear code conversion in the merge regime. Using the entropy/length profile (ELP), we derive upper bounds on the number of unchanged symbols and lower bounds on the number of read symbols for arbitrary $(n,M)_q$ codes, without assuming linearity or requiring $\log_q M$ to be an integer. We also obtain joint bounds for multiple initial codes and consequences involving minimum distance. For linear codes, the proposed bounds reduce to the corresponding generalized Hamming weight (GHW) bounds. The construction based on Hamming codes converts Hamming codes of redundancy two into a Hamming code of any larger redundancy and simultaneously attains the general bounds on unchanged and read symbols. The construction based on quasigroups shows that new bounds remain tight for genuinely nonlinear codes of nonintegral dimension and at a nonintegral entropy threshold, which, to the best of our knowledge, is the first construction of convertible codes for nonlinear codes.
2610.15252.title: Entropy/Length Profile Bounds for the Conversion of (Non)linear Codes in the Merge Regime

2610.15300.summary: Ultra-reliable and low-latency communication (URLLC) is essential for mission-critical cellular Internet of Things (IoT) applications requiring reliable short-packet transmission and efficient radio-resource allocation. However, finite-blocklength (FBL)-aware beamforming becomes computationally demanding as the numbers of users and antennas increase. Existing successive convex approximation (SCA) methods typically rely on general-purpose convex solvers without exploiting the structure of the resulting beamforming problem. This paper develops a structure-exploiting consensus alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) framework for low-complexity FBL-aware beamforming in downlink multi-user multiple-input single-output (MU-MISO) cellular IoT networks. The FBL sum rate is maximized subject to transmit-power and per-user minimum-rate constraints. Each SCA iteration yields a convex quadratically constrained quadratic program (QCQP), reformulated into an equivalent consensus problem. For an M-antenna base station serving N IoT nodes, the global update exploits Kronecker structure to replace an MN-by-MN factorization with a shared M-by-M factorization, while rank-one channel matrices enable low-complexity local projections. CVX-SCA serves as a general-purpose benchmark, whereas standard ADMM-SCA isolates the gains from structural exploitation. Numerical results demonstrate close agreement with CVX-SCA in objective value, feasibility, and convergence. Under user scaling, the proposed method achieves more than 4-fold end-to-end speedup over CVX-SCA and approximately 6-fold per-iteration speedup over standard ADMM-SCA, demonstrating its computational efficiency for cellular IoT resource allocation.
2610.15300.title: Structure-Exploiting ADMM for Low-Complexity Finite-Blocklength Beamforming in Cellular IoT Networks

2610.15302.summary: Continuous-aperture arrays (CAPAs) provide a new electromagnetic transmission paradigm by directly controlling the source-current distribution over a continuous radiating aperture. This paper studies CAPA-enabled integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) with spatially extended sensing targets, for which the electromagnetic response over each target region is characterized by an aperture-to-region operator. Unlike point-target models, the resulting illumination operator may have infinite rank, precluding a priori finite-dimensional reduction of the transmit design. We formulate the joint communication and target-illumination beamforming problem in the continuous electromagnetic domain and develop an operator semidefinite relaxation (SDR). A key structural result is that the optimal transmit covariance operators remain finite rank even when the aggregate illumination operator has infinite rank. We further establish the tightness of the operator SDR and provide a constructive rank-one recovery of the information beamformers. Since the finite electromagnetic subspace supporting the optimum is generally unknown, we develop a dual-slack-driven adaptive mode-enrichment method that discovers the required modes from the full-space optimality conditions. The dual-slack violation simultaneously identifies missing modes and yields a computable certificate of the remaining full-space optimality gap. Global convergence of the enrichment sequence to the full-space optimum is established. Numerical results validate the finite-rank optimal structure and show that the proposed method approaches the full-space optimum with substantially fewer electromagnetic modes than truncated-SVD and spatial-Fourier representations.
2610.15302.title: CAPA Beamforming for Extended-Target ISAC: Finite-Rank Solution Structure and Adaptive Electromagnetic-Mode Enrichment

2610.15306.comment: This manuscript has been submitted to IEEE journal
2610.15306.summary: Rydberg atomic quantum receivers (RAQR) exhibit exceptional sensitivity to radio-frequency (RF) signals, positioning them as promising candidates for next-generation wireless systems. Extending their capabilities to orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM), however, requires atomic responses that go beyond broadband reception and are tailored to the structured interference of multicarrier signals. To bridge this gap, we develop an atomic-comb Rydberg receiver based on six-wave mixing (SWM) transduction. In particular, injecting a multi-tone local oscillator (LO) into the RAQR generates frequency-shifted replicas of the intrinsic SWM response. By subtly tuning the amplitude and phase of each LO tone, constructive and destructive interference can be selectively induced to preserve desired response components while attenuating harmful frequency offsets. Furthermore, we harness the response-reshaping capability of the proposed atomic comb to proactively mitigate OFDM interference. More explicitly, by exploiting the discrete difference-frequency structure of both carrier-frequency-offset (CFO)-induced and phase-noise (PN)-induced inter-carrier interference (ICI), we optimize the atomic-comb response to suppress dominant ICI components directly. We further reveal an intrinsic coupling between spectral shaping and the time-domain effective channel memory, motivating a joint optimization of both ICI and inter-symbol interference (ISI), which simultaneously suppresses inter-carrier leakage and post-cyclic-prefix (CP) tail energy. Extensive simulation results validate our atomic-comb design, unveiling that the proposed atomic comb can effectively reshape the receiver response over the OFDM, while mitigating ICI, shortening the effective channel memory, and substantially lowering CP overhead.
2610.15306.title: Rydberg Atomic Quantum Receivers for OFDM Systems: An Atomic-Comb Design

2610.15329.summary: In this paper, {we propose a new family of $(n, k)$ Minimum Storage Regenerating (MSR) codes} for distributed storage systems. By structuring the parity-check matrix as a block Vandermonde matrix composed of diagonal matrices and generalized permutation matrices, the proposed code achieves a sub-packetization level of $N = (d-k+1)^{\lceil\frac{n}{2}\rceil}$ and supports any repair degree $k+1\le d<n$. A key innovation of the new construction lies in relaxing the strict commutativity condition previously required for the building blocks in the parity-check matrices of Ye-Barg codes. We introduce a novel proof technique to establish the MDS property without relying on full commutativity, thereby generalizing the applicability of block Vandermonde matrices and enriching the family of Ye-Barg codes. Additionally, the sparsity of the parity-check matrix enhances encoding and decoding efficiency by reducing computational complexity. This work provides new insights into the construction of MSR codes.
2610.15329.title: New Minimum Storage Regenerating Codes With Small Sub-packetization Levels for All Admissible Repair Degrees

2610.15338.comment: This paper has been submitted to the IEEE trans journals
2610.15338.summary: Semantic sensing extends integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) beyond physical parameter estimation by exploiting task-oriented representations from radio echoes. Nevertheless, existing multimodal sensing remains largely limited to vision-assisted radio physical parameter estimation or typically processes the visual and radio modalities separately, leaving radio representations underutilized for visual task enhancement. Feature-level fusion enables closer cross-modal interaction, while echo interference complicates the learning of user-specific radio representations and its semantic consistency with the visual entities. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a multimodal semantic sensing framework for orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM)-ISAC systems. We propose a radio encoder to learn radio representations oriented toward visual localization from superimposed pilot echoes, together with Variational Radio-Visual Grounding (VRVG) to promote semantic consistency between the learned radio representations and visual spatial features. The radio representations are then formulated as semantic probes to highlight the corresponding entities in the visual scene through cross-modal fusion. Experiments using real-world RCooper dataset show that the resulting synergistic radio-visual embeddings enable accurate radio-visual user matching and significantly improve both user-specific visual localization and physical parameter estimation performance. The results substantiate the benefits of radio representation learning and semantically consistent fusion for multimodal semantic sensing.
2610.15338.title: Radio Echo Representation Learning for Semantic Sensing in Multi-Modal ISAC Systems

2610.15355.summary: Multi-frequency electrical impedance tomography (EIT) often requires specialized hardware. This challenge is especially pronounced in biomedical applications. We developed a 16-electrode EIT system using an Arduino GIGA R1 WiFi for generation and acquisition, with a discrete current source, three analog multiplexers, and basic signal conditioning. Dual cores separate waveform timing from switching and acquisition. A 3D-printed tank with silver-wire electrodes was tested at 11 frequencies (1-180 kHz). Across the 10-180 kHz analysis band, median repeat-frame signal-to-noise ratio was 48 dB, acquisition rate was ~0.18 frames/s per frequency (~60 s per sweep), and cross-session baseline drift was ~6%. KCl phantoms contained an insulating ABS cylinder or KCl-filled dialysis bags (0.001-1.0 M) spanning positive and negative conductivity contrasts. Boundary voltages were analyzed without reconstruction to estimate inclusion position, contrast polarity, and relative magnitude. Leave-one-session-out matching located ABS inclusions in 29/30 runs at 160 kHz (87-97% across the band; chance 33%). For dialysis bags, polarity was correctly identified in all 36 nonzero-contrast runs. Signed voltage projections correlated with the cylindrical contrast factor (R^2=0.68 across runs; R^2=0.89 for the aggregate fit). Concentration was ordered (Spearman rho=0.85), despite saturation above ~10-fold contrast. Bag position accuracy ranged from 6/6 at the highest contrasts to 2/6 at matched conductivity. The matched-conductivity bag produced a ~1.7% RMS perturbation against 0.4-0.6% repeat-frame variability. These results demonstrate that microcontroller-based multi-frequency EIT can support selected detection and identification tasks through direct boundary-voltage analysis, supporting future studies of muscle electrochemistry.
2610.15355.title: An Arduino Giga-Based Multi-Frequency Electrical Impedance Tomography System for Electrolyte Media: Hardware Design, Statistical Voltage Analysis, and System Performance Evaluation

2610.15402.comment: A preliminary version of the manuscript
2610.15402.summary: Wyner's common information $J(p)$ and the common entropy $G(p)$ of a pair of random variables $(X,Y)$ with finite ranges and joint distribution $p$ are both defined by an optimization over the auxiliary random variables $W$ that make $X$ and $Y$ conditionally independent: $J(p)$ is the infimum of the mutual information $I(X,Y;W)$, and $G(p)$ is the infimum of the entropy $H(W)$. We prove that both quantities are NP-hard to compute. For Wyner's common information, deciding whether $J(p)$ is strictly smaller than a given integer $r$ is NP-hard, and the problem is NP-complete on tables that are uniform on their support and have the same number of positive entries in every row. The reduction is from Maximum Edge Biclique and rests on an exact criterion, in terms of rectangles in the support of $p$, for improving on the auxiliary $W=X$; every yes-instance satisfies $J(p)<r-1/(4N^2)$ and every no-instance satisfies $J(p)=r$, where $N$ is the number of positive entries of $p$. For the common entropy, deciding whether $G(p)\le r$ for a rational number $r$ is NP-hard, even for tables with at most four nonzero entries in each row, all taking one of two values. The reduction is from exact cover by $3$-sets and rests on a majorization property of the masses of the nonnegative rank-one decompositions of $p$, combined with a quantitative form of the Schur concavity of entropy. In both cases the separation between yes- and no-instances is inverse-polynomial in the size of $p$, so that approximating $J(p)$ or $G(p)$ within a suitable inverse-polynomial additive error is also NP-hard. The two mechanisms are genuinely different: we exhibit a table on which a large rectangle in the support lowers $J$ below the threshold of our first reduction while leaving $G$ on it.
2610.15402.title: Wyner's Common Information and the Common Entropy are NP-Hard to Compute

2610.15404.summary: The AI-RAN paradigm makes the next-generation cellular network more versatile by co-locating AI and RAN workloads on the same commodity hardware. While the GPU is a promising platform for AI-RAN realization, a generic concurrent AI application interferes with the latency-sensitive RAN on GPU compute resources. In this paper, we propose Eunoia, a dynamic real-time AI-RAN GPU scheduler that is transparent to both AI applications and the RAN workload and operates at the granularity level of the RAN slot. We deploy Eunoia onto NVIDIA Aerial AI-RAN and evaluate Eunoia on both an over-the-air 5G private network and an emulated multi-cell network. We demonstrate that in a 27-cell AI-RAN, Eunoia keeps the RAN uplink P99 latency under 3 ms while delivering higher AI performance than other RAN-safe static partitioning methods.
2610.15404.title: Eunoia: Toward Application-Transparent, Scalable GPU Sharing in AI-RAN

2610.15413.summary: In this paper, we focus on decoding optimal Reed-Solomon codes of dimension two for insdel errors up to the half-Singleton bound. We present a decoding algorithm for the general insertion-and-deletion scenario with a time complexity smaller than brute-force decoding. Our algorithm corrects insdel errors up to the half-Singleton bound, which exceeds the scope of existing methods. Additionally, for the special cases of insertion-only and deletion-only insdel error patterns, we present two different algorithms with a time complexity smaller than our general algorithm.
2610.15413.title: Insdel Reed-Solomon Decoding Algorithms up to the Half-Singleton Bound

2610.15420.summary: We study the undetected-error exponent of discrete memoryless channels with erasure decoding. Assuming that the undetected-error and erasure probabilities vanish, we derive an upper bound on the undetected-error exponent at positive rates. The bound uses Somekh-Baruch's genie-aided argument where an auxiliary output provides the decoder with a list of codewords. It recovers Telatar's tight rate-zero converse and is at least as tight as the straight-line bound. A numerical example shows that the improvement over the straight-line bound can be strict.
2610.15420.title: An Upper Bound to the Undetected Error Exponent with Erasure Decoding at Positive Rates

2610.15423.summary: We study universal unequal error protection of a single special message over discrete memoryless channels. We construct a sequence of codes with a decoding rule that does not depend on the channel transition law. We derive an achievable error exponent for the special message while ensuring reliable decoding of the ordinary messages. The resulting exponent strictly improves on the natural equal-error-protection random-coding baseline and remains positive as the rate approaches capacity. For symmetric channels, it converges to the optimal red-alert exponent at capacity.
2610.15423.title: Universal Decoding for Unequal Error Protection

2610.15446.summary: Due to the directional antenna pattern, the received signal power decreases when the target deviates from the array boresight, degrading direction-sensing accuracy. Although rotatable arrays can alleviate this problem, repeated array rotations will induce an incremental long sensing latency. To break the dilemma of harvesting the directive gain from element and making a low-latency sensing, a multi-armed array comprising multiple subarrays with different orientations is proposed to provide wide spatial coverage encompassing low-altitude and terrestrial regions while enabling multi-view direction sensing. However, the different views lead to different direction-sensing accuracies. To fully exploit the complementary information from multiple views, two fusion methods, called SNR-weighted fusion and logistic-weighted fusion, are developed. The former directly assigns fusion weights according to the estimated received SNRs, whereas the latter employs an exponential SNR mapping to further emphasize high-SNR subarrays. Furthermore, the Cramer-Rao lower bound (CRLB) is derived to provide a theoretical benchmark for the proposed multi-view direction-sensing system. Simulation results show that logistic-weighted fusion achieves better accuracy in the very low-SNR regime, while both proposed methods approach the CRLB at medium and high SNRs and maintain stable sensing performance.
2610.15446.title: A Multi-View Low-Latency Direction-Sensing for Low-Altitude Network via a Multi-Armed Array

2610.15455.summary: In multiple-input multiple-output orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (MIMO-OFDM) systems, conventional receivers based on linear channel estimation and subband-averaged interference covariance reconstruction suffer serious performance degradation under strong interference. To address this issue, we propose a probabilistic framework for joint channel estimation and interference suppression using score-based prior learning. Specifically, we formulate a variational inference problem that exploits the bilinear structure of the interference by explicitly separating the interference channels from the interference symbols. To solve the resulting highly nonconvex bilinear inference problem, we develop a score-based variational inference algorithm that combines score-based turbo message passing for target-channel estimation with a reverse mean propagation framework for interference-channel inference, while the interference symbols are updated via linear minimum mean square error (LMMSE) estimation. We further design an interference rejection combining (IRC) detector with subcarrier-level covariance reconstruction based on the estimated interference channels, thereby avoiding the performance loss caused by conventional subband averaging. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm is able to effectively suppress the interference in channel estimation, as well as to accurately reconstruct the interference subspace for interference rejection in data detection, and thus significantly outperforms existing baselines.
2610.15455.title: Inter-Cell Interference Suppression for Channel Estimation and Data Detection in MIMO-OFDM Systems via Score-Based Variational Inference

2610.15490.comment: This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication. Copyright may be transferred without notice, after which this version may no longer be accessible
2610.15490.summary: Designing a massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) detector that is tailored to each specific deployment site can improve detection performance, yet most existing detectors, including deep-unfolding methods, adapt mainly within human-prescribed algorithmic structures. This letter proposes SiteEvo, a site-adaptive agentic discovery framework that extends adaptation from parameter tuning to detector-algorithm discovery. Rather than selecting or recombining predefined architectures, the large language model (LLM) agent synthesizes complete executable detector programs under a common design contract by combining its pretrained communication knowledge, site-specific wireless evidence, and experience accumulated during the search. Each proposal defines its own processing structure and trainable parameterization, and the parameters are optimized by a communication-system backend. The resulting high-performance detector is further structurally refined to reduce block-level computational cost under a bit error rate (BER)-preservation constraint and is finally frozen for deployment without online LLM inference. Simulations across three sites demonstrate BER reductions by factors of 2.6 to 6.0 over the best-performing competing detector at each site at 6 dB, while structural refinement reduces block-level computational cost by 16.7-34.1% under a validation-BER constraint.
2610.15490.title: SiteEvo: An LLM Agent for Autonomous Discovery of Site-Adaptive Massive MIMO Detectors

2610.15494.summary: Radio frequency fingerprinting aims to identify transmitters by exploiting small differences in the emitted signal waveform. Common approaches exploit hardware-dependent imperfections for that purpose. This work instead investigates whether differences between digital signal processing implementations of a transmitter can be identified from their radiated signals. As a practical case study, five different software-based DSP implementations for generating a 2-FSK RTTY communication waveform are considered. In a monitoring receiver, a classifier can identify these DSP implementations using convolutional neural networks that are trained on augmented software-generated signals represented as raw IQ, power spectrum or instantaneous frequency. The trained networks are evaluated on over-the-air recordings obtained using a shortwave transceiver and a software-defined radio receiver. The best neural network combines IQ and the power spectrum representation and achieves an accuracy of up to 90%. The study further examines the influence of the signal SNR and the observation bandwidth on the classification accuracy. The results demonstrate that DSP implementations leave distinguishable characteristics in the transmitted signals and suggest that DSP-dependent fingerprinting can provide complementary information for specific emitter identification systems.
2610.15494.title: RF Fingerprinting of DSP Implementations using Machine Learning: An Over-the-Air Case Study

2610.15549.summary: We study the mean-squared error (MSE) rate-distortion function (RDF) of finite Gaussian mixture models (GMMs) in $\mathbb{R}^d$, for which neither the RDF nor an optimal test channel is known in closed form. It can be sandwiched between the genie-aided conditional RDF $R_{\mathbf{X} | T}(D)$, which can be characterized in closed-form for a GMM, and $R_{\mathbf{X} | T}(D)+I(\mathbf{X};T)$, where $T$ denotes the latent component label. We show that the upper bound can be achieved operationally by the proposed Gibbs-relabelling method (GRM), which conveys a label from the posterior $P_{T|\mathbf{X}}$ through \textit{channel simulation} at rate $I(\mathbf{X};T)$, followed by vector quantization of the resulting exactly Gaussian conditional sources by reverse water-filling. Using the Shannon lower bound (SLB), we prove that GRM attains the SLB, and hence the RDF, of a general finite mixture if and only if every component attains its own SLB. For a GMM this holds throughout the fully active interval $D/d<\min_{k,m}\lambda_{k,m}$, where $\lambda_{k,m}$ are the eigenvalues of the component covariances, and for scalar GMMs the condition is also necessary. Since GRM cannot operate below the label cost $I(\mathbf{X};T)$, we propose a complementary stochastic scalar quantization (SSQ) scheme for low rates, which simulates an $M$-ary reconstruction index. We show that at low rates SSQ with $M\geq 2$ matches the Shannon RDF to first order: $R(D_{\max}-\delta)=\delta/(2\tau^2)+o(\delta)$, where $\tau^2$ is a directional sub-Gaussian proxy of the mixture, and quantify the price of a finite codebook through a strict rate gap at high rates and a distortion floor whose joint scaling in $M$ and number of mixture components is characterized. Numerical results illustrate both regimes and the finite-blocklength cost of channel simulation.
2610.15549.title: Rate-Distortion Theory of Gaussian Mixtures via Posterior Label Sampling

2610.15611.comment: 13 pages, 10 figures, 3 tables. Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Communications
2610.15611.summary: Movable antenna (MA) can enhance the physical layer security (PLS) performance of integrated sensing and communications (ISAC). However, most existing works assume either near-field (NF) or far-field (FF) propagation models for both communication users (CUs) and targets. This paper considers a more practical scenario where multiple CUs, an eavesdropper (Eve), and multiple targets are in a mixed near- and far-field environment due to the changes in the propagation field caused by antenna position updates in MA with a unified array response and continuous NF/FF weights. To evaluate the PLS performance of MA-aided ISAC in mixed-field environments, we formulate an optimization problem to maximize the sum secrecy rate (SSR) of CUs by jointly designing the transmit beamforming and antenna positions at the transmitter. The problem is highly non-convex, so a two-layer algorithm is proposed to iteratively solve the problem using the projected gradient ascent (PGA) method and the Lagrangian dual transform. Since the abrupt switch between the NF and the FF models during antenna movement can cause the objective function to oscillate during iteration, the unified array response is combined with the Barzilai-Borwein step, Armijo line search, and precise projection to ensure that the SSR does not decrease during the iteration and the objective function is differentiable on the Rayleigh boundary. Numerical results show that the MA-ISAC using the mixed-field model achieves almost identical PLS performance to that of using the full NF model in terms of SSR, and both outperform the FF model. Using the mismatched FF model during antenna position updates results in a loss of MA gain, potentially making MA inferior to the FA-based system using the correct model.
2610.15611.title: Physical Layer Security for Movable Antenna-Aided Mixed-Field ISAC

2610.15631.summary: Codes in the Levenshtein metric that can correct multiple edits (including deletions, insertions, and substitutions) have attracted a lot of attention recently owing to their application in DNA-based storage and racetrack memories. In this work, we present new techniques for designing explicit binary codes of length $n$ that correct $t$ edits with at most $(2t+1)\log n+O_t(\log\log n)$ bits of redundancy. We first propose to use a polynomial hash to construct a systematic code that corrects $t$ edits with $(4t+2)\log n+O_t(\log\log n)$ bits of redundancy. Then we observe that there are many polynomial hashes like this, some are good, some are bad. So, we propose the second technique, called entropy recycling, to use the indices of good hashes to carry information. As a consequence, we obtain a partial-systematic code of length $n$ that corrects $t$ edits with at most $(2t+1)\log n+O_t(\log\log n)$ bits of redundancy. Finally, we provide deterministic polynomial-time encoding and decoding algorithms for our code.
2610.15631.title: Binary Codes Correcting Multiple Edits via Polynomial Hashing and Entropy Recycling

2610.15641.comment: 6 pages, 6 figures, 2 tables. Accepted for presentation at the 1st IEEE Conference on Integrated Sensing and Communications (ISAC), Lisbon, Portugal, November 2026
2610.15641.summary: This paper investigates how bistatic delay information improves the observability and localization performance of 3D moving targets in distributed Wi-Fi sensing. Motivated by emerging IEEE 802.11bf WLAN sensing, we consider one transmitter, multiple distributed receivers, and a single target with unknown position and velocity. We compare Doppler-only sensing with delay-Doppler sensing, in which delay-capable receivers provide additional bistatic path-length information for target localization. We derive the Fisher information matrix (FIM) and the position equivalent FIM (EFIM) for both sensing formulations. The resulting observability analysis shows that Doppler-only localization generically requires six receivers, whereas delay-Doppler localization can become locally identifiable with three receivers under non-degenerate geometry. We further study mixed receiver architectures in which only a subset of receivers provides delay estimates. Simulations with Wi-Fi-like bandwidths confirm the transition and quantify the roles of bandwidth, Doppler noise, receiver geometry, and delay-capable receiver availability.
2610.15641.title: Bistatic Delay-Doppler Sensing for 3D Target Localization in Distributed Wi-Fi Systems

2610.15652.summary: A quantum-dot array prepared in a timed Dicke state exhibits directional radiation asymmetry, which has often been interpreted as evidence of reciprocity breaking through quantum-state preparation. We show that this interpretation is incorrect: reciprocity concerns transmit-receive response, not necessarily pattern symmetry. Moreover, the first-order coherence of any single-excitation state is exactly equivalent to the power pattern of a classical phased array driven by conjugate weights, making the observed asymmetry classically reproducible. The genuine quantum signature instead appears in second-order correlations, where a single-excitation state violates the classical lower bound on photon coincidences. We therefore propose a quantum-antenna certificate combining nonzero directional asymmetry with photon antibunching at the beam peak. We further derive a tight asymmetry bound, establish the correct mirror operation for planar arrays, correct the collective decay rate with dipole-dipole coupling, and derive a saturation law for direction-finding precision. All theoretical results are validated through independent numerical implementations.
2610.15652.title: Theoretical Investigation of Nonclassical Directional Emission in 1D and 2D Quantum-Dot Antenna Arrays and Quantum DoA Estimation

2610.15656.summary: We study the communication cost of exact sampling under Campbell's exponential coding criterion. Given a target distribution $P$ and a proposal distribution $Q$, the sender and receiver share i.i.d. $Q$-distributed samples, and the sender communicates an index so that the selected sample has distribution exactly $P$. We introduce a new information measure Rényi channel simulation divergence $R_\alpha(P\Vert Q)$, a Rényi generalization of the channel simulation divergence. We then show that it lower bounds the Campbell cost of every exact sampler and is achievable, via a new layered sampling scheme, within an additive constant depending only on the Campbell parameter. This yields a tighter one-shot characterization than previous bounds based on Rényi divergences of different orders. For i.i.d. product distributions, under suitable non-degeneracy and moment conditions, we further show that the gap beyond the leading Rényi-divergence term is $\frac{1}{2}\log n+O(1)$.
2610.15656.title: Exact Sampling Under Campbell Cost via Rényi Channel Simulation Divergence

2610.15701.summary: We introduce the problem of permutation burst error-correction, motivated by applications in molecular data storage with nanopore sequencing read platforms. A permutation burst of length $k$ is an error that affects a substring of length $k$ of a string of length $n$ by permuting its entries. Permutation burst errors can be corrected using classical burst error-correcting codes, such as Fire and Reed-Solomon codes. Here, we study how to reduce the redundancy of these classical codes by taking into account that the burst error preserves the weight of the substring. In addition, we further restrict our model to handle cyclic permutation bursts only, which are of independent practical and mathematical interest. Our main results include proving/establishing the following: a) for $k=o(\sqrt{n}),$ the redundancy of any permutation burst error correcting code is at least $\log n-k+\log \binom{2k-2}{k-2}+o(1).$ This result follows from McDiarmid's concentration bound; b) for $k \geq 9$ and $k=o\left(\sqrt{\frac{n}{\log n}}\right)$, the redundancy of any cyclic permutation burst error correcting code is at least $\log n +\log (k(k-1)-56)-\log\,80+o(1).$ c) the asymptotic redundancy upper bounds for the two types of substring errors that are twice the lower bound; d) constructions for both permutation burst and cyclic permutation burst errors that involve Varshamov-Tenegoltz type constraints or represent generalizations and extensions of Fire and other codes. In particular, we exhibit polynomially encodable and decodable codes that can correct cyclic bursts of length $\leq k$ using $\log n + k + 49\log k + O(\log \log k)$ redundant bits.
2610.15701.title: Correcting Burst Errors with Applications to DNA-Based Data Storage

2610.15767.summary: Levenshtein's classical theorem shows that any code that can uniquely decode from \(t\) deletions can also uniquely decode from \(t\) insertions. This symmetry, however, does not generally hold in the list-decoding regime. Several prior results on the capacity and radii of list-decoding from insertions and deletions suggest that insertions are easier to handle than deletions. In an effort to better understand this asymmetry between insertions and deletions under list-decoding, we study an analogous version of McEliece's \emph{average list size problem}. More precisely, given a binary code \(\mathcal{C}\) of length \(n\) that uniquely corrects \(t'\) insertions (or deletions), we are interested in the average number of codewords returned by a \(t\)-insertion (or deletion) list decoder, where \(t' < t\). Focusing on the case of \(t'=1\) and \(t=2\), we find that under two insertions, this quantity is at most \((n+12)/4\) for any VT code of length \(n\), whereas under two deletions it is at least \(n/2 - 10\) when averaged over all length-\(n\) VT codes. The nearly factor-of-two gap between these upper and lower bounds serves to confirm the relative ease of list-decoding of insertions compared to deletions from an average-case perspective.
2610.15767.title: On the Average List Size of VT Codes under Two Insertions or Two Deletions

2610.15815.summary: Recent work shows that ordinary Reed--Solomon codes over prime fields admit polynomial-size lists up to list-decoding capacity on every evaluation set. We show a contrasting phenomenon over binary extension fields. For every fixed rate $0<R<1$, there exists $\varepsilon_R>0$ such that, for all sufficiently large $h$, the full-field Reed--Solomon code over $\mathbb{F}_{2^h}$ has a received word with $n^{\Omega_R(\log n)}$ codewords within relative distance $1-R-\varepsilon_R$. To our knowledge, these are the first superpolynomial ordinary Reed--Solomon list-size lower bounds at fixed positive rate and a fixed positive agreement gap above the rate. Thus capacity-approaching polynomial list size for Reed--Solomon codes is not uniform over the underlying field, and the obstruction occurs at every fixed rate. As a puncturing consequence, the same holds for primitive Reed--Solomon codes; the obstruction is also robust under controlled dense puncturing. The proof begins with an exact correspondence that turns certain binary Bose--Chaudhuri--Hocquenghem weight-enumerator coefficients into sizes of single Reed--Solomon lists. A classical binary weight family gives the initial quarter-rate construction, while a quadratic-form enumeration supplies its superpolynomial multiplicity. A common-kernel quotient/descent argument and common-root padding then extend the construction to all rates. We also determine the optimized agreement envelope achieved by the construction.
2610.15815.title: Superpolynomial Lists for Reed-Solomon Codes over Binary Extension Fields

2610.15847.summary: Information-theoretic generalization bounds usually control dependence on the task sample, whereas selective privacy may constrain only a different, private coordinate. We study i.i.d. pairs $(X,Y)$, where a learner observes $(X^n,Y^n)$, leaks at most $\epsilon_n$ nats about $X^n$, and incurs loss on $Y$. A chain-rule transfer converts this mismatched constraint into the closed-form universal certificate $I(W;Y^n)\leq\min\{nH(Y),nH(Y\mid X)+\epsilon_n\}$. Combining the certificate with mutual-information generalization yields a bound governed by residual task uncertainty and normalized privacy leakage. We derive complementary task-compression and individual-sample refinements, identify a sharp obstruction showing why selective privacy alone need not give a vanishing certificate, and invert the bound to obtain the exact leakage allowance for a prescribed generalization tolerance. We prove exact information-level achievability for deterministic-task and independent-residual source families and show that the resulting $\sqrt{\epsilon_n/n}$ generalization rate is tight up to a universal constant. We also give a fixed-horizon adaptive application in which conditional leakage costs add.
2610.15847.title: Residual-Information Generalization Bounds Under Selective Privacy: Extended Version

2610.15857.summary: Belief propagation (BP) is attractive for quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) decoding because of its low complexity and low latency, but short cycles and degeneracy can limit its error-correction performance. Reinforcement-learned sequential scheduling (RL-S) substantially improves this performance by adapting the variable node (VN) update order, although Q-table storage and heap-based selection introduce additional overhead. We propose bucket RL-S (B-RL-S), which quantizes learned Q-values into integer priorities and schedules VN updates using dynamically maintained first-in, first-out buckets. Without retraining or changing the BP message updates, B-RL-S reduces policy storage and refreshes only priorities affected by local residual syndrome changes. A fixed number of priority levels enables constant-time VN selection and queue relocation. For the $[[288,12,18]]$ bivariate bicycle code over the depolarizing channel at $p=0.05$, B-RL-S with eight priority levels achieves approximately one fifth the block error rate (BLER) of flooding BP followed by order-10 ordered-statistics decoding. The respective caps are $1000$ sequential iterations for B-RL-S and $1000$ flooding iterations for the BP stage of the reference decoder. These results highlight strong error correction with inexpensive scheduling and no additional post-processing stage.
2610.15857.title: Low-Latency Belief-Propagation Decoding of Quantum LDPC Codes with Reinforcement-Learned Scheduling

2610.15868.summary: We study the behavior of the $k$-th-order nonhomomorphicity of Boolean functions under restriction to affine subspaces. For odd $k\ge3$ and $0\le t<n$, we introduce the $t$-restriction $k$-th-order nonhomomorphicity $P_{k,t}(f)$, defined as the minimum of $P_k(f_{\mid A})$ over affine spaces of codimension at most $t$. For a direct sum of $m$ monomials of degrees at least two, we determine $P_{k,t}$ exactly. When $t<m$, a minimum is obtained by setting one variable equal to zero in each of the $t$ monomials of lowest degree. When $m\le t<n$, the minimum is zero. The proof combines multiplicativity of even Walsh moments with a contraction argument for affine restrictions. We establish a general formula for the Walsh transform of a Boolean function restricted to an affine subspace of arbitrary codimension, yielding an exact spectral characterization of the $t$-restriction normalized nonlinearity $\rnnl_t(f)$. As odd $k$ tends to infinity, $(1-2P_{k,t}(f))^{1/(k+1)}$ converges to $1-2\rnnl_t(f)$. We further prove that every non-affine function has a hyperplane restriction with strictly smaller odd-order nonhomomorphicity. Finally, we determine $\rnnl_1(T_{d,n})$ exactly for all threshold functions with $n\ge3$. This proves the two threshold-function conjectures left open in~\cite{SergeAnaPante2025}, including the previously unresolved odd-majority case, where a minimizing hyperplane is $x_1+x_2=0$.
2610.15868.title: Higher-order nonhomomorphicity under affine restrictions

2610.15872.comment: This paper has been pubblished in 2025 IEEE International Conference on Omni-layer Intelligent Systems (COINS)
2610.15872.summary: Open Radio Access Networks (O-RAN) empower operators with choice and customization through their disaggregated and interoperable architecture. However, ensuring interoperability in O-RAN presents challenges due to complex testing environments and evolving specifications. This paper addresses these challenges by proposing the Generative AI and Graph Neural Network-based Open RAN Testing and Automation (GNG-OTA) framework. GNG-OTA utilizes state-of-the-art AI techniques including generative AI, natural language processing, and graph neural networks to enable accurate, reliable, efficient, and automatic O-RAN interoperability and performance testing.
2610.15872.title: The Role of Generative Artificial Intelligence in Testing and Automation of Open RAN Systems: GNG-OTA Framework

2610.15877.summary: We study the approximate channel simulation problem in the normal approximation regime. Our starting point is the fact established by Cao et al.~\cite{Cao_channel_simulation}, that the minimal codebook size $M_\epsilon^*(W)$ for a fixed error tolerance $\epsilon>0$ is closely related to the $\epsilon$-smooth channel max-information, $I_{\max}^\epsilon(W)$. Using this, we refine earlier large-blocklength approximations to $M_\epsilon^*(W^{\otimes n})$ for discrete memoryless channels. Specifically, we provide tight third-order expansions for Gallager-symmetric channels and demonstrate that the third-order term is channel-dependent. As in corresponding channel coding expansions, we identify a substantial rate gap between singular and nonsingular channels. Notably, the direction of this gap is reversed relative to channel coding: The third-order term is $-\frac{1}{2}\log n$ for singular channels but $O(\log\log n)$ for nonsingular channels.
2610.15877.title: Fine asymptotics for approximate simulation of symmetric channels

2610.15972.summary: Full-support local randomizers can incur unnecessary reporting distortion on ordered alphabets. We study randomized response whose output is restricted to a radius-$t$ neighborhood of the private input. Input-dependent supports create privacy leakage at their boundaries, so ordinary likelihood-ratio calibration is no longer sufficient. Under approximate local privacy restricted to input pairs at distance at most $H$, we derive the exact hockey-stick defect of the mechanism. We then solve the joint design of the truthful probability, off-truth probability, and support radius. The fixed-radius optimum is available in closed form, while the global optimum requires only a one-dimensional integer search. We characterize both the privacy floor and its inverse, namely the smallest defect attainable under a reporting-distortion budget. We further prove that stringent approximate privacy forces the support size to scale as $\Omega(H/\delta)$. Deterministic evaluations illustrate the resulting tradeoff.
2610.15972.title: Exact Privacy--Distortion Design of Support-Constrained Randomized Response

2610.15976.summary: This paper investigates a new role of randomness in stochastic policies--as a medium for embedding and communicating information. Specifically, we consider an agent interacting with an environment according to a prescribed stochastic policy. By carefully modulating the random action realizations of the policy, information can be embedded into the agent's behavior without altering the prescribed action distribution. We cast this problem as a channel coding problem, in which the controlled system implicitly serves as a communication channel. We then propose a coding scheme, termed posterior-matching randomness modulation (PRAM), that selects actions according to the message to be transmitted. With the aid of common randomness independent of the control system, PRAM preserves the prescribed action distribution for every state and every message. We further prove that PRAM is asymptotically reliable: the message can be decoded with arbitrarily small error probability as the observed state trajectory becomes sufficiently long. Experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in applications including multi-bit policy watermarking and trajectory provenance.
2610.15976.title: Embedding Information in Policy Randomness: Distribution-Preserving Implicit Communication in MDPs

2610.15980.comment: 19 pages (14 pages of main text and 5 pages of appendix)
2610.15980.summary: Radio map estimation (RME), also known as spectrum cartography, aims to recover radio signal strength across multiple domains (e.g., spatial and spectral domains) from sparse measurements, naturally leading to a tensor completion problem. Recent advances show that deep learning-based generative models can provide data-driven structural constraints for RME, yielding substantial performance improvements over traditional model-based approaches. Diffusion models (DMs) represent the current state of the art in generative modeling and hold strong promise for advancing RME. However, existing diffusion-based RME methods often require extensive training data, necessitate retraining when scenarios or measurement formats change, and lack recoverability guarantees. This paper proposes a latent factor diffusion framework for spatio-spectral radio map tensor completion. By training two independent DMs on single-emitter's spatial loss field and spectral signature and embedding them into the factors of the radio map tensor, the proposed approach enables diffusion posterior sampling-based recovery with reduced training complexity as well as enhanced measurement format/sensing pattern flexibility. Recoverability and sample complexity guarantees under the proposed approach are also established. Numerical experiments validate the effectiveness of the proposed method, showing strong generalization across city environments unseen in training data.
2610.15980.title: Completing Radio Map Tensors via Factor Diffusion Posterior Sampling

2610.16026.summary: A printed tapered-slot coupling probe with a partially inserted 12-mm wire element is characterized for short-range microwave coupling through a brain-mimicking agar--gelatin--saline phantom and \textit{ex vivo} brain. Simulated and measured free-space $S_{11}$ responses agree over a measured $-10$-dB band spanning 5.78 to 6.86~GHz, corresponding to a 1.08-GHz bandwidth and approximately 17.1~percent fractional bandwidth. In a controlled two-probe experiment, the phantom was introduced and removed while the probe arrangement and measurement conditions were retained. This comparison was repeated under the same retained arrangement, with the same general $S_{21}$ differential behavior observed across repetitions. Near 6.3~GHz, measured $S_{21}$ was approximately $-25$~dB with the phantom present and approximately $-40$~dB in air, corresponding to an $\approx 16~\mathrm dB$. \textit{Ex vivo} goat brain measurements repeated more than five times showed reproducible behavior. Across 5.78--6.86~GHz, the \textit{ex vivo} goat-brain $S_{21}$ response closely followed that of the phantom, with an approximately figure-derived maximum operating-band difference of about 1.5~dB. The observed increase in $|S_{21}|$ is interpreted as a property of the complete probe--medium--probe system, including loading, mutual coupling, interfaces, geometry, propagation, and material loss. The measurement does not uniquely identify a tissue-intrinsic mechanism.
2610.16026.title: Short-Range Microwave Interprobe Coupling in a Brain-Mimicking Phantom and Ex-Vivo Brain

2610.16033.summary: The Zak-OTFS carrier waveform is a pulse in the delay-Doppler (DD) domain, and given the input-output (I/O) relation at one DD point in a frame, we can predict the I/O relation at all other points. While it is simple to acquire the effective wireless channel with Zak-OTFS, the cost of embracing inter-carrier interference is equalization complexity. The cost of linear minimum mean-square error (LMMSE) equalization grows cubically with the frame size. We describe how to use channel knowledge to reduce equalization complexity. For any pulse shaping filter, and for fractional delays and Dopplers, we show that the DD channel matrix is unitarily similar, through the discrete Zak transform, to a time-domain (TD) matrix that is a weighted sum of cyclic delay and Doppler operators, where the weights are the taps of the effective channel. We also obtain a dual frequency-domain (FD) form through an additional Fourier transform. The TD matrix is banded with a width set by the delay spread that is independent of the Doppler spread, whereas the FD matrix is banded with a width set only by the Doppler spread. We design a receiver that reads off the two widths from the channel estimate, selects the cheaper domain, and solves the banded system exactly, using a bordered Cholesky factorization that treats the quasi-periodic wrap-around without sacrificing degrees of freedom. Filters that decay slowly need a few preconditioned conjugate gradient steps. We show that the complexity of equalization becomes linear in the frame size. Simulations match direct DD-LMMSE error rates with three to four orders of magnitude fewer multiplications. A single receiver handles channels with very different delay and Doppler characteristics.
2610.16033.title: Delay-Doppler Duality: Simplifying Exact Equalization of Zak-OTFS in Time or in Frequency

2610.16055.summary: A quickest change detection problem is studied where the decision-maker has access to multiple experiments, but can choose only one experiment at a time to detect the change. The true post-change distribution under each experiment is unknown, but known to belong to a family of distributions. It is assumed that each of these families of distributions has an element that is least favorable in a well-defined sense. An algorithm is proposed that is designed using the least favorable distributions. It is shown that the algorithm is first-order asymptotically optimal, as the rate of false alarms goes to zero. This algorithm minimizes the worst-case average detection delay over all post-change distributions within the assumed families, subject to a constraint on the average run length to false alarm and constraints on the average fraction of time each experiment is performed before change.
2610.16055.title: Robust Quickest Change Detection with Cost-Efficient Experiment Design and Unknown Post-Change Model

2610.16069.summary: We prove the Fourier entropy--influence inequality for every linear threshold function, with a constant below $8.937$ and no restrictions on its weights or threshold. The argument applies to regular Boolean functions and gives logarithmic bounds for their Boolean combinations and for unions with bounded variable overlap. Character multiplication preserves the estimates and yields bounds by influence minus variance. Under arbitrary product measures, symmetric thresholds satisfy the strengthened inequality needed for read-once composition, uniformly in depth and fan-in. A joint description of each Fourier set refines the overlap estimate and recovers constant bounds for addressing. Exact selector identities extend the bound to orthogonal multiplexers with shared data. Rare activation preserves the optimal constant of unrestricted FEI. The proofs combine pivotal antichains, spectral reference measures, and product-measure composition.
2610.16069.title: Fourier entropy of threshold functions and their compositions

2610.16121.summary: Linear complementary dual (LCD) codes are linear codes that intersect their dual trivially. We study double circulant (Euclidean) LCD codes over the finite chain ring $R=\mathbb F_2+u\mathbb F_2$, where $u^2=0$. Using the Chinese Remainder Theorem and the factorization of $x^n-1$, we derive an explicit enumeration formula, with a separate treatment of the constituent corresponding to $x-1$, which is not obtained by a formal specialization of the previously known counting formula over $\mathbb F_q[u]/(u^k)$. Assuming Artin's primitive root conjecture for $2$, we show that the binary Gray images contain an asymptotically good family of rate $1/2$ whose relative distance can approach $H_2^{-1}(1/4)$ from below.
