item.summary: We study cache-aided linear computation in distributed systems where each source generates and stores its own data. An external receiver requests a linear combination of these data, and the sources use information cached before the request is known to reduce the communication needed to recover the requested result. In our model, each of the $N$ sources stores its own independent file over a finite field and has an additional cache of normalized size $M$. The receiver must recover any requested linear combination with zero error from the messages sent by the sources over separate noiseless links. We establish a lower bound on the worst-case communication rate over any finite field by analyzing several requests under the same cache placement. This bound determines the optimal rate when no additional cache is available. For binary files, we propose parity-aided placement (PAP), a coded-placement scheme that combines cached parities with uncoded symbols. For every $N\geq3$, we characterize its communication rate for each request and optimize its placement parameters to obtain a closed-form worst-case rate. The resulting achievable rate meets the lower bound for $0\leq M\leq1/(2N-1)$ and $M\geq(N-1)/N$, establishing the optimal memory--rate tradeoff in these two ranges.
item.title: Cache-Aided Linear Function Computation

AI.conclusion: 该工作验证了双极化RSMA在毫米波频段的可行性与实用性，提供了首个相关原型验证，极化分集带来灵活性且非SIC接收机可降低硬件复杂度，为未来FR2/FR3多用户接入设计提供参考。
AI.method: 构建双极化RSMA系统模型（发射机与每个接收机各配备一对双极化天线），推导离散星座下的可达速率表达式；提出并评估基于SIC的接收机架构与非SIC解码器；搭建25 GHz载频的原型系统，在不同SNR与极化分集条件下测量各数据流的符号错误率（SER），并与软件仿真对比。
AI.motivation: 毫米波/FR2频段通信需要在高频段实现多用户接入并提升频谱效率，同时实际硬件实现需兼顾复杂度。作者希望利用极化分集与RSMA的结合，为服务两个用户提供适应不同信道条件的灵活性，并验证其可行性与实际性能。
AI.relevance_reason: 论文属于毫米波多址接入与极化分集的物理层/原型设计，与无线通信相关，但不涉及CSI获取、信道估计、CSI反馈/压缩或AI辅助信道建模等核心方向。
AI.result: 两种接收架构性能相当；极化分集与RSMA结合使系统在服务两用户时具有显著的信道适应灵活性，非SIC解码器可实现更简单的硬件实现。原型测量结果与软件仿真吻合良好，验证了系统实现。作者称这是文献中首个毫米波RSMA原型，也是首个利用极化分集的方案，并可能适用于FR3频段（7-24 GHz）上部。
AI.tldr: 该论文提出一种用于毫米波（FR2）的双极化速率分离多址（RSMA）设计方案，面向单发射机服务两用户的场景，推导离散星座下的可达速率，设计SIC与非SIC两种接收机架构，并搭建25 GHz原型系统通过SER测量验证其性能。

item.summary: This work presents a dual-polarized rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) design for millimeter-wave (mmWave) or frequency range 2 (FR2) communications. Focusing on a practical implementation, we consider the specific scenario of a single transmitter serving two receivers (users) within the same time, frequency, and code resource block. The transmitter and each receiver are equipped with a pair of dual-polarized antennas. We first present the system formulation and compute the achievable rate expressions for discrete constellations. Based on these expressions, we propose and evaluate two receiver architectures: one based on successive interference cancellation (SIC) and a non-SIC decoder. Both designs exhibit comparable performance, and the combination of polarization diversity and RSMA provides the system with significant flexibility to adapt to different channel conditions when serving both users, while the non-SIC decoder enables a simpler hardware implementation. We then present a prototype implementation of the proposed design, operating at a carrier frequency of 25 GHz, and evaluate it by measuring the symbol error rate (SER) of the different data streams under various signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and polarization diversity conditions. The obtained measurements show good agreement with software simulations, thereby validating the system implementation. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first mmWave RSMA prototype reported in the literature and the first to exploit polarization diversity. Furthermore, given the selected carrier frequency, the proposed design may also find applicability in the upper portion of the envisioned FR3 band (7-24 GHz).
item.title: Dual-Polarized Rate-Splitting Multiple Access for mmWave Communications: A Practical Design and Prototype Implementation

AI.conclusion: 层互补性与Jacobian条件是SIM架构设计的有效判据，解释了深度增益的来源。
AI.method: 对级联模型做逐层解析，分析Jacobian秩、灵敏度方向强度与均衡性及层间传播生成互补灵敏度方向的机制；采用包含电磁耦合与多次散射的S参数多端口模型评估该机制。
AI.motivation: 探究为何以及何时将可编程超表面堆叠为SIM能在固定相位控制预算下提升线性变换合成能力，为SIM架构设计提供判据。
AI.relevance_reason: 该文研究可编程超表面/SIM的电磁建模与变换合成条件，属于RIS相关物理层方向，但聚焦波域线性变换与Jacobian条件分析，未涉及CSI获取、信道估计或AI方法。
AI.result: 近场与远场感知场景的数值结果显示，将相同控制资源分散到多层可增强弱变换方向、改善Jacobian条件数并显著提升合成精度；增加深度带来的增益无法通过扩大单层可编程表面获得。
AI.tldr: 该文分析堆叠式智能超表面（SIM）在固定相位控制预算下改进线性变换合成的机理，指出仅靠Jacobian代数秩不足以刻画实际合成效果，还取决于灵敏度方向的强度与均衡性，并用含电磁耦合的S参数多端口模型验证分层互补机制。

item.summary: This paper investigates when and why stacking programmable metasurfaces into Stacked Intelligent Metasurfaces (SIMs) improves linear transformation synthesis at a fixed phase-control budget. The analysis shows that algebraic Jacobian rank alone is insufficient to characterize practical synthesis, which also depends on the strength and balance of the sensitivity directions generated by the available controls. A layer-resolved analysis of the cascade model explains how inter-layer propagation can generate complementary sensitivity directions. The relevance of this mechanism is then assessed using an S-parameter multiport model that includes electromagnetic coupling and multiple scattering. Numerical results in near- and far-field sensing scenarios show that distributing the same control resources across multiple layers can strengthen weak transformation directions, improve Jacobian conditioning, and substantially enhance synthesis accuracy. These findings explain why increasing depth can offer benefits that are not obtained by simply enlarging a single programmable surface, and identify layer complementarity and Jacobian conditioning as useful criteria for SIM architecture design.
item.title: To Stack or Not to Stack? Jacobian Conditioning and the Benefits of Depth in Metasurface-Based Linear Transformation Synthesis

AI.conclusion: 持久表面关联散射点可有效改善射线追踪对非平稳移动信道漫散射时间演化的表征能力，提升站点特定信道建模精度。
AI.method: 在 Sionna RT 中扩展漫散射模型，采用与表面关联的持久散射点：散射点位置固定，其贡献随传播几何与可见性变化而演化；随后在城市车载场景 5.9 GHz 下利用实测信道冲激响应进行验证。
AI.motivation: 在站点特定的非平稳移动场景中，重复执行射线追踪会生成互不对应的漫散射路径，破坏了漫散射分量时间演化的连贯表示，因此需要一个能保持路径对应关系的漫散射传播建模方法。
AI.relevance_reason: 该文涉及射线追踪信道建模与多普勒/时延域验证，与无线信道传播建模相关，但未涉及 CSI 获取、反馈压缩或 AI 方法，故关联度中等偏低。
AI.result: 与标准 Sionna RT 基线相比，所提模型在时延域和多普勒域与实测结果的一致性均有提升。
AI.tldr: 该论文扩展了开源射线追踪框架 Sionna RT 的漫散射建模，引入与表面绑定的持久散射点，使非平稳移动场景下多次 RT 评估的漫散射路径保持时间对应关系，并用 5.9 GHz 城市车载信道的实测信道冲激响应在时延与多普勒域验证了改进效果。

item.summary: Open-source ray tracing (RT) frameworks are increasingly used for site-specific channel modeling due to their reproducibility and extensibility. In non-stationary mobility scenarios, repeated RT evaluations can generate different diffuse propagation paths without preserving their correspondence, limiting a consistent representation of their temporal evolution. To address this limitation, we extend diffuse scattering modeling in Sionna RT using persistent surface-associated scattering points. Their positions remain fixed, while their contributions evolve according to changes in the propagation geometry and visibility. The proposed approach is validated using empirical radio channel impulse response measurements in an urban vehicular scenario at 5.9 GHz. Compared with the standard Sionna RT baseline, the proposed model shows improved agreement with measurements in the delay and Doppler domains.
item.title: Modeling Diffuse Scattering in Mobility Scenarios: Ray Tracing Model and Measurement Validation

2610.18904.comment: 10 pages, 2 figures, 7 tables. Code and data: this https URL
2610.18904.summary: A reading departs from what a monitoring system expects for one of three reasons: the physical process changed, the instrument is failing, or the value was corrupted between the instrument and the software. The three call for different responses and look alike in a single sample. We state the three-cause problem, prove which pairs of causes one channel cannot separate, and propose a bank of online detectors - a Kalman tracker with CUSUM and EWMA charts on its innovation, a Hampel median with generalized-ESD confirmation, a robust noise statistic with ADWIN, exact-value checks and an optional two-channel complementary filter - combined by a deterministic, inspectable attribution rule. The detectors were merged into a public algorithm library. On 2,942 injected events of thirteen fault types the method detects 96.3% (95% interval 95.7-97.0) at 0.22 false alarms per hour and attributes 91.2% (90.6-91.8) of detected events correctly from one channel and 99.0% (98.6-99.4) with a second, rate channel; from one channel only 2 of 207 detected sensor drifts are attributed to the instrument, as the problem statement predicts. Injected into recorded industrial signals, the same catalogue is detected at 80.8% and attributed correctly at 84.5%, at 3.6 false alarms per hour. On the Skoltech Anomaly Benchmark the method detects 32 of 33 experiments with a median delay of 15 s, at 46 false alarms per hour against 11 for a rolling z-score.
2610.18904.title: Distinguishing Process Change, Instrument Fault and Data-Path Corruption in Streaming Telemetry: A Reference Implementation and Benchmark

2610.18905.comment: 29 pages, 4 figures, 6 tables. Data, certificates and code: doi:https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23303466. Submitted to PRX Quantum
2610.18905.summary: Entanglement entropies of multipartite pure states satisfy linear inequalities; for stabilizer states, the backbone of quantum error correction, the achievable entropy vectors generate a convex cone. We show that, after a linear lift, the closure of this cone is exactly the self-dual slice of a classical object on one more element than there are parties: the closed cone generated by the rank functions of arrangements of subspaces over $\mathrm{GF}(d)$ for a prime local dimension $d$, and of subgroups of abelian groups of exponent dividing $d$ in general. This correspondence brings two features of rank inequalities into play. First, the purifier acts as an extra variable: already for five parties the stabilizer cone is strictly smaller than the quantum linear rank cone, with which earlier evidence suggested it might coincide; an explicit six-variable inequality witnesses the gap. Second, the characteristic of the field enters, so the cone depends on the local dimension. It does not for up to four parties. With enough parties, the cone of $\mathbb{Z}_d$ qudits is contained in that of $\mathbb{Z}_{d'}$ qudits if and only if $d$ divides $d'$, and already for six parties the logical zero state of Steane's code lies outside the stabilizer cone of every odd local dimension. For this last result we show that the seven-variable characteristic-dependent inequalities we checked all follow from Shannon inequalities on the self-dual slice, and instead transfer one of them through a family of subgroups derived from the Fano plane.
2610.18905.title: Stabilizer entropy cones as self-dual slices of linear rank cones: a five-party gap and dependence on the local dimension

2610.18930.summary: In this paper, we investigate the impact of antenna beam pattern models on the beam placement problem in Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite networks. Unlike conventional beam placement studies that often rely on a fixed antenna pattern or a predefined half-power beamwidth, this work compares four representative gain models, namely the Bessel $J_1$ model, the combined Bessel $J_1+J_3$ model, the Gaussian model, and a 3GPP-TR 37.842 model. For each antenna pattern, the corresponding half-power angle is obtained and used to construct a user compatibility graph. The beam placement problem is then transformed into a Minimum Clique Cover problem and solved using a graph coloring-based algorithm. Numerical results compare the considered antenna models in terms of the number of active beams, load balancing, statistical channel gain-to-noise ratio (SCGNR), and signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR). We analyze the impact of increasing the number of active beams on SINR-based spectral efficiency to explain the importance of carefully controlling the number of active beams. The results show that antenna beam pattern models affect both beam resource usage and link quality, highlighting the need for antenna-pattern-aware beam placement in LEO satellite networks.
2610.18930.title: On the Investigation of Antenna Beam Pattern Models for Fast Beam Placement in LEO Satellite Networks

2610.19040.summary: Simultaneously transmitting and reflecting reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (STAR-RIS) enable programmable wave control on both sides of a surface, extending wireless coverage beyond single-sided operation. However, practical STAR-RIS demonstrations in literature have narrow bandwidths, because it is challenging to achieve wideband reflection and transmission simultaneously from the same aperture. To overcome this limitation, a wideband STAR-RIS architecture is proposed based on shared-aperture polarization conversion and diagonal switching topology. Here, multiple resonances enable wideband magnitude responses and mirror-symmetric current reversal maintains $180^{\circ}$ phase difference in both reflection and transmission modes. Accordingly, a diagonal four-branch unit cell configuration is developed, where the tailored top patch directs the received wave either through a pair of blind vias connected by a buried strip to the shared top aperture for reflection, or to the bottom ring patch using a through via for transmission. Based on the proposed design, a 10 by 10 STAR-RIS prototype is fabricated and experimentally characterized. The measured 3-dB bandwidths reach 19.8% in reflection mode and 21.9% in transmission mode. Near-field measurements show average signal enhancements of 19.8 and 22.6 dB for reflection and transmission, respectively, over the wide frequency range of 6.8-8.4 GHz. Far-field measurements further demonstrate average received-power enhancements of 11.2 dB in reflection and 11.9 dB in transmission. To the best of the authors' knowledge, this work presents the first experimentally demonstrated wideband STAR-RIS covering the 7.125-8.4 GHz band within the emerging 6G FR3 spectrum.
2610.19040.title: A Wideband STAR-RIS Employing Shared-Aperture Polarization Conversion and Diagonal Switching Topology for 6G Applications

2610.19115.summary: Any AIS transmitter can claim any vessel's identity (MMSI), because nothing in the protocol authenticates it; only the transmitter's analog hardware reveals who is really sending. We treat AIS traffic as streams of bursts keyed by claimed MMSI and accumulate physical-layer evidence with a sequential test. Each burst is scored by its k-nearest-neighbor distance to enrolled fingerprints in the feature space of a classifier whose weights are fixed after training, calibrated into a tail probability, and accumulated by a geometric-entropy-minimization cumulative-sum (GEM-CUSUM) statistic. The same test rejects unknown transmitters when scored against all enrolled vessels, and exposes insider spoofs when scored against the claimed vessel. A threshold refreshed from genuine traffic alone keeps it at a stated false-alarm rate as fingerprints drift. On AIS in-phase/quadrature (I/Q) recordings captured over 13 days at the Istanbul Strait (Bosphorus), the detector rejects unseen vessels at least 10 days after enrollment. Evaluated over 50-burst trials with every vessel weighted equally, it reaches an area under the ROC curve (AUROC) of 0.956 (95% confidence interval 0.913-0.989), where the best score computed from one burst at a time reaches 0.899. A threshold refreshed from the first quarter of the enrolled vessels' traffic holds 5.3% false alarms (3.0-9.2% across five independently trained encoders) at 88.8% detection. Scored against the claimed MMSI, enrolled transmitters spoofing another vessel are rejected at 0.991, a threat that open-set tests cannot see (AUROC 0.500, chance level). The lightweight Transformer GLFormer, reimplemented from its paper (no code is public) and retrained on the same data, reaches 0.652 in the same detector with its published in-phase input and 0.849 when given the same I/Q input as our encoder.
2610.19115.title: Sequential RF Fingerprinting for AIS: Rejecting Unknown Vessels and Insider MMSI Spoofs Days After Enrollment

2610.19137.summary: Decarbonizing cellular networks requires coordinating communication-resource and battery operation with time-varying electricity prices and carbon intensity. We jointly optimize base station and battery operation under a carbon-adjusted electricity price and traffic-demand constraints, and solve the mixed-integer nonconvex problem through a two-stage decomposition exact under a minimum-power rule. Using California price and carbon-intensity data, we show that carbon-aware scheduling reduces emissions most when low-price and low-carbon periods are misaligned. Above a carbon price of roughly 100-300 USD/ton, battery operation shifts from cost-driven to carbon-driven, cutting emissions by up to 57.8% relative to a cost-only schedule.
2610.19137.title: Carbon-Aware Joint Resource and Energy Scheduling for Cellular Base Stations

2610.19265.summary: The scarcity of real-world ground penetrating radar (RealGPR) data is a major barrier to the development of deep learning (DL) methods for GPR data processing. Although simulated GPR (SimGPR) datasets can be used to train DL models, differences in hardware configuration and system parameters between SimGPR and RealGPR create a sim-to-real domain gap that leads to poor generalization of DL models to RealGPR measurements. To address this gap, we present a physics-based far-field GPR domain transfer (FFDT) method to transfer far-field SimGPR data to the corresponding RealGPR-domain data in the same scenario. In FFDT, SimGPR and RealGPR are modeled using angle-dependent transfer functions that capture three-dimensional antenna radiation characteristics. These transfer functions are then combined with ray tracing to enable the sim-to-real data transfer. Extensive studies across diverse objects and soil conditions demonstrate that FFDT-transferred data closely match RealGPR ground truth. To further demonstrate its value for RealGPR-domain dataset generation, FFDT is implemented to build a RealGPR-domain dataset for training a DL model for clutter removal. The model achieves robust performance on RealGPR measurements. With one-time SimGPR and RealGPR system calibration, FFDT enables RealGPR-domain dataset generation without requiring task-specific RealGPR field measurements for DL model training or fine-tuning, thereby addressing the RealGPR data scarcity bottleneck and supporting reliable development and deployment of DL methods for real-world GPR applications.
2610.19265.title: FFDT: Sim-to-Real Domain Transfer Method for Far-Field Ground Penetrating Radar

2610.19300.summary: The torn paper channel breaks a codeword into fragments and returns all fragments without their original order. The noisy torn paper channel additionally introduces bit substitution errors to each fragment. Recovering the message therefore requires accounting for both bit errors and uncertainty about the fragment order. We establish a capacity upper bound for the noisy torn paper channel that matches the achievable rate of Ravi, Vahid, and Shomorony and resolves their conjecture. Our results also determine the capacity of the noisy shuffling channel of Shomorony and Heckel, in which all fragments have the same length, and resolve their open question.
2610.19300.title: The Capacity of the Noisy Torn Paper Channel and the Noisy Shuffling Channel

2610.19451.summary: We study two explicit constructions of binary Calderbank--Shor--Steane quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) codes with check weight six. The first uses a fixed circulant shift pattern and yields parameters $\code{6N}{2N+2}{6}$ with Tanner graph girth twelve for $N=31$ and every $N\ge37$. A graph incidence interpretation gives the ranks and girths, and a uniform weight six logical operator establishes the exact distance. The second construction uses fixed matrix polynomials with circulant and affine permutation coefficients. Here, a polynomial commutation identity guarantees orthogonality for every cyclic lift. Four realizations give $[[192,16,8]]$, $[[288,16,12]]$, $[[384,16,14]]$, and $[[576,32,20]]$, with Tanner girth eight and computationally certified distances. We give reproducible construction data, distinguish classical cycle distance from quantum distance, and identify the limitations of both families.
2610.19451.title: High-Girth QLDPC Codes from Circulant and Affine Permutation Matrices

2610.19456.summary: The problem of Private Information Retrieval (PIR) across graph-based replicated systems has seen a surge of interest in recent literature. In such systems, servers are modeled as the vertices of a graph, and each file is represented by an edge connecting the pair of servers that store it. While previous research on Graph-PIR (G-PIR) has focused mostly on perfect information-theoretic privacy, relaxing this constraint has the potential for significantly higher retrieval rates. In this work, we consider the setting of Graph-based Weak Private Information Retrieval (G-WPIR), under an $\epsilon$-privacy metric. We adapt an existing G-WPIR scheme for arbitrary graphs to analyze its performance under the $\epsilon$-privacy metric. Additionally, we establish a lower bound on the expected download cost for arbitrary graphs under the $\epsilon$-privacy metric and derive from it an explicit rate upper bound for complete graphs. Finally, we show the achievable rate-privacy trade-offs for two specific graph classes---complete graphs and complete bipartite graphs.
2610.19456.title: Weak Private Information Retrieval for Graph-based Storage under $ε$-privacy

2610.19490.summary: Digital-domain self-interference cancellation is essential in in-band full-duplex radios after passive suppression and analog cancellation. It is particularly challenging when the desired signal is strong relative to the residual self-interference. In this regime, conventional iterative digital cancellers update their coefficients from desired-signal-contaminated received samples and may suffer substantial performance degradation. This paper reformulates digital-domain self-interference cancellation as an operator-learning problem. The proposed framework learns the temporal evolution of the residual self-interference channel from historical observations and uses the learned operator together with the known local transmit signal to reconstruct the current residual self-interference. A Transformer neural operator is used to realize this framework. The resulting method is trained in a desired-signal-free setting and then applied in the presence of a desired signal. A continuity-based analysis characterizes the sensitivity of the learned operator to the resulting input perturbation. Numerical experiments in static and time-varying channels, including time-varying SIR conditions, demonstrate stable cancellation performance over a wide range of interference levels. At 30 dB SIR, the proposed method improves the cancellation performance by 5--15 dB over the considered conventional methods.
2610.19490.title: Digital Self-Interference Cancellation for In-Band Full-Duplex Systems Based on Transformer Neural Operators

2610.19612.comment: 16 pages, 5 figures, and 7 tables. Published in IEEE IOTJ
2610.19612.summary: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) with cloud radio access networks (C-RAN) unifies two foundational technologies for the Internet of Things (IoT), enabling both high-data-rate transmission and accurate environmental awareness. This paper investigates an uplink C-RAN system where multiple remote radio units (RRUs) jointly serve user equipment devices (UEs) and sense a target. We demonstrate that only a subset of RRUs is typically needed to meet sensing requirements, while energy is potentially conserved by deactivating redundant sensing RRUs. Motivated by this, we aim to improve the system's energy efficiency (EE) by jointly optimizing RRU activation, user association, and power allocation, while ensuring localization accuracy through the Cramér-Rao lower bound (CRLB). To address this problem, we propose a model-based iterative algorithm that integrates optimal user association, decision tree-based selection of sensing RRUs, and fixed-point power allocation. This algorithm is further used to train a graph neural network (GNN) framework, ISAC-GNN, to overcome scalability and computational complexity limitations. Our theoretical analysis ensures performance guarantees, while a semi-supervised training strategy enhances stability and generalization. Simulation results demonstrate that ISAC-GNN reduces inference time by 67% relative to the model-based approach, enabling real-time implementation for ISAC system resource management. In addition, ISAC-GNN allows scalable deployment across various system scenarios without retraining the model.
2610.19612.title: Energy Efficiency Maximization for Integrated Sensing and Communication in IoT C-RAN

2610.19639.summary: High-frequency and broadband line-of-sight multiple-input multiple-output (LoS-MIMO) is a key solution for massive space-to-Earth data downlinks. However, in low Earth orbit (LEO) scenarios, it faces spatial rank deficiency from time-frequency coupling correlation and clock deviations from distributed oscillators. This paper establishes a dynamic effective channel throughput (ECT) framework incorporating waterfall characteristics of forward error correction. A hardware-friendly OFDM-based transceiver architecture with subband-adaptive truncation and dynamic timing recovery to achieve robust spatial decoupling is proposed. Through rigorous closed-form derivations, the equivalent signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) under joint errors is quantified, and an optimal scheduling algorithm combining truncation with variable coding and modulation is proposed to maximize ECT. Simulations confirm that the design circumvents outages caused by spatial notches with low complexity, stably enhancing the potential average throughput of a single dual-polarized beam to over 100 Gbps, providing a reliable theoretical foundation and baseband solution for next-generation high-throughput satellites.
2610.19639.title: Hardware-friendly Baseband Design and Performance Analysis for LEO Broadband LoS-MIMO Systems

2610.19691.summary: Subspace-design codes form a central unifying framework in coding theory, connecting probabilistic existence results and explicit algebraically structured constructions. The two core families are folded Reed-Solomon codes and univariate multiplicity codes, both possessing the subspace-design property. These codes reach list-decoding capacity with polynomial-size lists, but their alphabet size grows with code length and hurts practical efficiency. Goyal, Guruswami, and Hsieh achieved a major breakthrough: they constructed the first explicit subspace-design codes over constant-size alphabets via the Alon-Edmonds-Luby expander framework, settling an open problem and showing subspace-design properties can hold without large alphabets. Despite recent progress, constructing subspace-design codes with low-complexity efficient encoding remains a critical open challenge. This work gives an explicit construction of r-dimensional subspace-design codes over a constant alphabet whose size grows exponentially with r. By comparison, Goyal et al. (FOCS 2026) built r-dimensional subspace-design codes with alphabet size doubly exponential in r squared. Our construction is computationally efficient: encoding scales quadratically with block length and linearly with dimension r in field operations. We use modified algebraic geometry codes, replacing rational evaluation points with higher-degree places to obtain a valid additive code. To confirm parameter bounds, we use Moore matrices to analyze determinants with many zero entries. We also generalize univariate multiplicity codes, originally built from Reed-Solomon codes, to algebraic geometry codes, and prove these AG-multiplicity codes achieve optimal parameters.
2610.19691.title: Efficient construction of subspace design codes over constant alphabet

2610.19715.summary: Accurate information-theoretic analysis of multiuser wavelength-division multiplexed (WDM) optical links is complicated by Kerr nonlinearity and chromatic dispersion. Existing capacity bounds for first-order regular perturbative (RP) channel models have relied on per-symbol peak power constraints to simplify the underlying extremal analysis. In this paper, we replace these peak constraints with the more practically relevant average input power constraints and study the resulting RP WDM interference channel. Unlike the peak-constrained formulation, an exact finite signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) analysis under average power leads in general to a nonconvex, high-dimensional optimization problem with no closed-form solution. We show that the problem admits a tractable characterization in the high-SNR regime. Using a genie-aided argument, we derive closed-form single-user high-SNR capacity bounds for the RP interference channel and identify constant-amplitude interferer signaling as extremal. Furthermore, under an empirically validated non-negativity condition on the dominant RP kernels and within a truncated first-order RP model, we establish a finite-SNR extremality result, yielding a single-user capacity characterization within the RP model under average power constraints. Building on these single-user corner points, we construct an all-helpsone achievable region via time sharing, which strictly improves upon treating nonlinear interference as noise. Numerical results and split-step Fourier simulations of the nonlinear Schrodinger equation channel confirm that the qualitative conclusions persist over practical launch powers. The results provide new insight into extremal signaling and multiuser trade-offs for nonlinear WDM systems within the RP approximation.
2610.19715.title: Capacity Bounds for Optical Interference Channels Subject to Average Power Constraints

2610.19784.summary: We consider a discrete memoryless state-dependent channel with noiseless feedback, where the transmitter uses randomized encoding to jointly perform message transmission, identification, and state sensing. In this setting, the transmitter sends a conventional transmission message and an identification message while estimating the unknown channel state sequence under an average distortion constraint. We establish a single-letter characterization of the randomized identification-transmission-sensing capacity-distortion region. The result reveals a single-letter separation structure: the communication rates are determined by the averaged channel, subject to the sensing-induced constraint on admissible input distributions. Specifically, the transmission rate is characterized by mutual information, while the identification rate is characterized by output entropy under the same distortion constraint. The achievability proof combines constant-composition transmission coding, output partitioning, and combinatorial identification coding, while the converse follows from an averaged-channel reduction, distortion lower bounds, and feedback-identification converse arguments.
2610.19784.title: Joint Identification, Transmission, and Sensing over State-Dependent Channels with Noiseless Feedback

2610.19826.summary: This paper proposes a Full Duplex (FD) framework for safeguarding Integrated Sensing and Communications (ISAC) against a passive multi-antenna Eavesdropper (Eve). The adversary is modeled as both a communication and sensing threat, seeking to decode uplink data streams and estimate the surrounding scene. Eve's threat is quantified through two worst-case requirements over a location uncertainty region: a minimum secrecy rate for data confidentiality and a minimum eavesdropping Cramer-Rao Bound (CRB) for sensing privacy. We derive the eavesdropping information measures governing both data interception and scene inference, showcasing that transmitting Artificial Noise (AN) can degrade Eve's capabilities through the inverse interference-plus-noise covariance. Exploiting the underlying structure of the problem, we characterize finite-power local and robust feasibility conditions for target secrecy-privacy pairs. The analysis showcases that AN is fundamentally subspace-limited: increasing power is beneficial only along Eve's communication channel and sensing-derivative directions illuminated by the effective AN subspace. Finally, we formulate an AN power allocation problem that is solved via monotone branch-and-bound, and numerical evaluations quantify the AN power required to guarantee joint secrecy and sensing privacy.
2610.19826.title: Simultaneous Secure Communications and Sensing Privacy with Full Duplex MIMO Radios

2610.19852.summary: Shannon entropy is a standard measure of ciphertext randomness, evaluated either globally over the byte histogram of the entire ciphertext or locally as the average over non-overlapping blocks of ?xed size. While the global statistic captures only the overall byte distribution, the local statistic is also sensitive to non-randomness that is con?ned to parts of the ciphertext. Both measures are commonly assessed against reference values derived under the assumption of independent uniform bytes. However, STL encodes most numerical data as single-precision IEEE-754 ?oats, and format validity requires them to be ?nite, causing nonuniform byte probabilities and dependence between the two bytes of each exponent pair. We derive the exact mean and variance of entropy under the valid-STL (VSTL) distribution, which assigns equal probability to every admissible sequence of triangle records, and provide second-order expansions that keep the global reference values practical to compute at large ?le sizes. Using these expansions, we establish a two-sided hypothesis test for the global entropy statistic, whose limiting value is lowered from 8 to 7.99991479609 bits. The format constraints also change the local entropy reference: applying the capacity energy criterion to triangle records selects a block size of 1950 bytes instead of 1936 bytes, with an exact reference mean of 7.903106732975 rather than 7.902469316647 bits. Although small, these shifts are su?cient to place the VSTL reference means outside the conventional 95% acceptance intervals at practical ?le sizes, making unadjusted entropy tests prone to falsely rejecting ideal VSTL ciphertexts. Monte-Carlo simulations con?rm all reference values within sampling error. We therefore recommend using the format-speci?c reference values derived here to evaluate STL ciphers.
2610.19852.title: Global and Local Entropy Tests for STL Files Under IEEE-754 Validity Constraints

2610.19889.comment: Accepted at 2026 IEEE 1st Annual Integrated Sensing and Communication Conference (ISAC)
2610.19889.summary: Power amplifier (PA) nonlinearity is a critical transmitter impairment in the upper mid-band (7 GHz to 24 GHz), designated as Frequency Range 3 (FR3) in emerging 6G standardisation. The 3GPP PA model baseline, TR 38.803 Annex A, was derived from 2.1 GHz and 28 GHz measurements and has not been revisited yet for FR3 standards work. This paper addresses that gap with characterisation measurements of multiple PA devices-under-test (DUTs), driven into gain compression in the 7 GHz and 15 GHz bands with 100 MHz and 200 MHz bandwidth. Memoryless polynomial and Generalized Memory Polynomial (GMP) behavioral models are extracted by least-squares regression and compared with 3GPP models spanning FR1 and FR2. The GaN PA DUT is modelled best at a higher nonlinear order and shows markedly stronger phase distortion than the wideband PA. The memory terms of the GMP model measurably improve the Normalized Mean Square Error (NMSE) at all operating points. An orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) ambiguity function analysis from the Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) literature, using the extracted models, illustrates how PA compression raises the sidelobe floor of the sensing response. These results provide a reference for PA impairment modelling in FR3, directly applicable to ISAC system design. All model coefficients and measurement data are publicly available [1].
2610.19889.title: Comparative Analysis and Behavioral Modelling of Power Amplifiers in FR3

2610.19894.summary: Background: Estimating subvoxel tissue fractions from magnetic resonance fingerprinting (MRF) is challenging. Conventional dictionary matching and segmentation pipelines can propagate errors from intermediate parametric maps into tissue fraction estimates. Purpose: We introduce DeepPV-MRF, a deep learning framework that directly estimates voxel-wise tissue fractions from raw MRF signals. Methods: A cascaded spatial-temporal network was trained on subject-derived Bloch simulations with radial k-space undersampling. The network combines temporal encoding and spatial U-Net refinement to estimate cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), gray matter (GM), and white matter (WM) fractions without intermediate T1/T2 maps. We compared DeepPV-MRF with partial-volume dictionary matching (PV-DM) and pseudoinverse estimation (PV-Pinv) using simulated and in vivo data. Results: DeepPV-MRF outperformed both methods across acquisition settings. In single-shot simulations, CSF/WM/GM mean absolute errors were 0.0418/0.0744/0.0757, versus 0.1281/0.2443/0.2958 for PV-DM and 0.2021/0.2793/0.2630 for PV-Pinv. Corresponding structural similarity values were 0.960/0.916/0.922. In vivo results showed sharper anatomical boundaries and smoother tissue transitions, while cross-shot analysis indicated improved consistency across volunteers. Conclusions: DeepPV-MRF enables accurate and efficient direct tissue fraction estimation from MRF signals, particularly with limited shots. Further validation is needed before clinical deployment.
2610.19894.title: DeepPV-MRF: End-to-End Partial-Volume Fraction Estimation from MR Fingerprinting Time Series

2610.19960.summary: Let $A_q(n,d)$ denote the largest size of a code of length $n$ and minimum Hamming distance $d$ over an alphabet of $q$ symbols. For fixed $q\ge2$ and $d\ge4$ we construct codes with redundancy $n-\log_q A_q(n,d)\le(d-3)\log_q n+O(\sqrt{\log n})$ for all large $n$. No algebraic structure is imposed on the alphabet, and the codes are not linear. For $d=4$ and $d=5$ the coefficient of $\log_q n$ matches the Hamming bound, so the redundancy is determined up to lower-order terms. At distance four the codes are provably better than every linear code: by the polynomial-method bound for cap sets, $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear codes with $q>2$ require a strictly larger coefficient in front of $\log_q n$. The construction imposes moment checksums over an auxiliary finite field, as BCH codes do, but one fewer than the distance would normally require. The affine-line theorem from prior work describes the dependencies left by these checks. We exclude them by placing the code positions inside a specially structured subset of the field, built from Behrend's sphere construction with the help of algebraic number theory.
2610.19960.title: Nonlinear fixed-distance codes via real lifts of moment configurations

2610.19969.comment: 4 pages, 4 figures, 1 table. Accepted for publication in IEEE Sensors Letters
2610.19969.summary: Motion capture is increasingly important in healthcare, rehabilitation, and sports applications. However, conventional vision-based systems require camera infrastructure and line-of-sight conditions, limiting their use in daily environments. This paper proposes a location-independent platform for motion capture, based on an array of IMU (inertial measurement unit) sensor nodes without individual wiring or onboard batteries, enabled by two-dimensional communication and power delivery over conductive fabric. Pipeline processing in each sensor node, combined with a token-passing protocol, enables collision-free and stable data acquisition at 50 Hz. Real-time three-dimensional reconstruction of flexible objects is further demonstrated by applying Hermite spline interpolation to orientation data from grid-aligned IMUs. Against a cylinder of known radius, the reconstructed surface deviates by 2.60 mm RMS over the 225 mm span of the array. The reconstruction is formulated for the quasi-static regime, and this letter empirically validates it in that regime. The hardware platform and communication protocol implemented in this work enable further investigation toward dynamic motion capture textiles.
2610.19969.title: Toward Motion Capture Textiles: A Batteryless IMU Array Powered and Networked Through a Conductive-Fabric Bus

2610.19987.comment: Accepted at IEEE GLOBECOM 2026 Workshop on Positioning and Sensing Over Wireless Networks
2610.19987.summary: In hybrid monostatic-bistatic orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) sensing, each sensing node receives a superposition of monostatic and bistatic target returns, whose phase-noise (PN) characteristics differ fundamentally due to oscillator sharing. While monostatic sensing benefits from partial PN cancellation through the common transmit-receive oscillator, bistatic sensing involves independent oscillators and is therefore more strongly affected by PN. In this paper, we characterize the joint residual differential PN statistics of these superimposed components in a centralized two-node sensing system and quantify their impact on target localization via theoretical lower bounds considering three different receivers: (i) PN-free ideal receiver, (ii) PN-aware receiver that exploits the joint PN statistics, and (iii) PN-ignorant receiver that neglects PN.
2610.19987.title: Hybrid Monostatic and Bistatic Sensing for Target Localization in OFDM Systems under Phase Noise

2610.20018.summary: Training hardware by gradient descent requires a gradient to be computed using a separate backwards pass. If a circuit is reciprocal, meaning every connection is symmetric, the backward pass is the same network run a second time with the error as its input. The reciprocal tau-cell, a weak-inversion log-domain circuit, makes this practical in standard CMOS. Each cell is a current-mode leaky integrator with a built-in ReLU; each connection is two transistors whose signed strength is a ratio of bias currents. The equilibrium of the network is the solution to a convex program, and latching the cells that are off will hardware linearise the circuit, making its second run exactly linear. Transistor-level SKY130 simulations show that the second run gives the gradient within 1.9%; that hardware linearisation permits large, noise-robust error signals; that a 13-cell network learns the Iris data set; and that learning in situ restores mismatched circuits on which software-trained weights fail, from 53-63% to 88-96% test accuracy.
2610.20018.title: The Reciprocal tau-Cell: A Log-Domain Circuit for On-Chip Learning

2610.20076.summary: Accurate bistatic radar cross-section (RCS) characterization requires near-field measurements over multiple dimensions, which, under typical near-field sampling requirements, can lead to long measurement durations for electrically large radar targets. This paper presents a near-field-to-far-field transformation based on an equivalent surface-current reconstruction using a-priori information about the target to reduce the number of newly acquired near-field samples. It is assumed that the prior target and the target under test (TUT) differ by localized geometrical modifications. Their complex differential near field is reconstructed using Tikhonov-regularized least squares QR factorization (LSQR) method. The reconstructed differential far- field contribution is coherently combined with the prior far-field contribution to estimate the bi-static RCS of the TUT. The method is preliminarily evaluated using simulations of a complex target at 6 GHz. The results indicate that, for the investigated simulation case, prior information can be used to thin out the sampling grid by 90% while maintaining close agreement with the simulation baseline.
2610.20076.title: Sampling Reduction for Near-Field to Far-Field Transformation of Bistatic Radar Target Measurements

2610.20087.summary: We introduce binary cyclic gradient coding (BCGC), an exact gradient coding scheme for $n$ workers and up to $s$ stragglers. Its encoding matrix is binary, circulant when $(s+1)\mid n$ and nearly circulant otherwise, and the master decodes by a single summation. Like the fractional repetition coding scheme (FRC) and its generalized version (GFRC), BCGC splits the workers into $s+1$ classes that each cover the whole dataset, but it assigns the data through cyclic supports. Its encoding matrix has rank $n-s$, and $n-s-1$ workers keep the balanced load $s+1$, which is the largest possible number. We prove that encoding matrix of BCGC is not permutation-equivalent to those of FRC and GFRC schemes. Moreover, We also prove that a binary coded scheme with compression is equivalent to an uncoded compressed scheme on a coarser partition of the data. This explains why binary schemes remain stable under compression, whereas the large decoding coefficients of MDS codes amplify the compression error and lead to divergence in our experiments. For every contractive compressor, the standard convergence guarantee of compressed gradient descent holds on each coarse partition. FRC, GFRC and BCGC therefore share the same convergence guarantee and differ only in their partitions, with one partition for FRC, two for GFRC and $s+1$ distinct partitions for BCGC. Choosing among these partitions can recover the exact gradient in cases where FRC and GFRC cannot. Experiments on four datasets confirm the theory. BCGC matches GFRC, keeps its accuracy under top $\kappa$ sparsification while the MDS codes diverge, and on heterogeneous data its partition diversity reduces the compression error and improves the accuracy.
2610.20087.title: Binary Cyclic Gradient Coding: Exact Recovery and Robustness to Compression

2610.20092.summary: Near-field beamfocusing confines radiated power into a localized three-dimensional focal spot, making the analytical characterization of radial and angular resolution critical for sixth-generation (6G) multi-user systems, yet existing models treat the focal resolution as a fixed geometric outcome rather than a tunable design variable. Based on the Angular Representation (ASR) approach, this paper presents a resolution framework to design contiguous focal regions across both the radial and angular domain for steered multi-user systems. By extending the definition of a tunable inter-beam overlap $\rho$, we derive closed-form expressions for the radial and angular focal boundaries and extents, alongside the steering-dependent minimum focal distance $d_{0,\text{min}}$ and maximum steering angle $\theta_{\text{max}}$. Using these boundaries, iterative synthesis algorithms are developed to construct uniform and non-uniform radial and angular beam arrangements. Finally, by analyzing both isolated and joint radial-angular configurations, we quantify the fundamental trade-offs between $\rho$, achievable user capacity, inter-user interference, and system sum-rate across varying steering angles.
2610.20092.title: Radial-Angular Resolution Framework for Near-Field Communications

2610.20142.comment: Submitted to an IEEE Journal for possible publication
2610.20142.summary: Movable antenna (MA) has emerged as a promising technology for enhancing wireless communication performance by flexibly reconfiguring wireless channels via antenna movement. In this paper, we propose an MA relay-enhanced multiuser communication system that adopts a half-duplex decode-and-forward (DF) relay scheme. The relay node is equipped with an MA array, and a buffer is employed to enhance the end-to-end transmission performance. Specifically, we formulate an optimization problem to maximize the minimum average achievable rate among multiple users over a given transmission period by dynamically optimizing the positions of MAs, transmit power, and beamforming matrices, subject to the constraints on antenna movement, inter-antenna spacing, and total energy budget for antenna movement and transmission. To address this non-convex problem with highly coupled variables, we propose a reinforcement learning (RL)-based algorithm, where a twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient (TD3) algorithm is utilized to optimize the antenna positions and power allocation, while the transmit and receive beamforming solutions are obtained through closed-form expressions in each time slot. Numerical results validate the efficacy of the proposed RL-based algorithm and demonstrate the superiority of the proposed MA relay-enhanced multiuser communication system over the conventional fixed-position antenna (FPA)-based relay system and other MA-based benchmarks.
2610.20142.title: Movable-Antenna Relay Enhanced Multiuser Communications: Reinforcement Learning-Based Antenna Positioning and Power Allocation

2610.20185.comment: 13 pages, 6 figures, 3 tables; supplementary material (11 pages) as an ancillary file. This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication. Copyright may be transferred without notice, after which this version may no longer be accessible
2610.20185.summary: Sensing-aided beam prediction could cut the beam-training overhead of millimeter-wave vehicular links, and two design choices could strengthen a radar-only predictor: a Doppler-resolved input and knowledge distilled from a camera during training. We measure what each is worth in received power rather than in top-1 accuracy, whose differences of a few points amount to only tenths of a decibel. We use real DeepSense 6G measurements, mainly at one roadside site, and one convolutional-recurrent predictor family evaluated open-loop up to 0.67 s ahead. Adding a range-Doppler map to the range-angle map lowers the mean beam-selection loss by 0.28 dB (95% bootstrap interval [0.14, 0.41]). The gain comes from the Doppler content, not from the extra input, and replicates, as pre-specified, at a second base station, although holding the last measured beam beats both predictors there. Cross-modal knowledge distillation from a motion-mask vision-radar teacher, by contrast, changes received power by -0.01 dB ([-0.07, +0.06]). The tested teacher, student, fusion and distillation variants show the same null in the metric each was scored on. Where distillation helps, in an exploratory run with few training passes, a radar-only teacher trained on all training passes reproduces most of the gain. For this predictor family and the full training set, the measurable gain at the link comes from Doppler-resolved radar content; no tested route for transferring training-only visual information adds a resolved gain.
2610.20185.title: Radar-Only Long-Term Beam Prediction in mmWave Vehicular Networks: An Empirical Study of Doppler Input and Cross-Modal Distillation

2610.20196.comment: 14 pages, 6 figures, 4 tables; supplementary material (17 pages) as an ancillary file. This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication. Copyright may be transferred without notice, after which this version may no longer be accessible
2610.20196.summary: Sensor-based beam prediction is usually evaluated against exhaustive beam training, leaving open when sensing adds useful information beyond a deployed tracker's link feedback and when it should be withheld. We separate system gain from the marginal value of sensing in action-restricted causal replay of recorded 64-beam sweeps from four vehicular DeepSense 6G scenarios. The replay exposes only serving-beam and explicitly probed candidate powers and counts probes and model invocations separately. The proposed controller combines a scheduled post-setup re-sweep with probe-verified sensing admission and blacklist backoff. In three scenarios where feedback-only tracking is within 0.25 dB of the recorded-sweep oracle, the controller stays close to feedback-only in mean loss while rarely invoking the model, whereas always-on sensing performs worse. In the sole high-innovation scenario, the controller's system gain is 0.82 dB (95% confidence interval [0.30, 1.40]) over the plain feedback-only tracker and 0.15 dB over a probe-limited re-sweeping reference, with fewer probes than either. Sensing and the re-sweep both correct setup lock loss. At the native decision interval, enabling sensing in the same controller yields no statistically resolved loss reduction but cuts probing by 21%. In this scenario, accurate sensing reduces loss relative to the sensor-disabled controller under emulated link noise, staleness or longer decision intervals. Weak or delayed sensing can instead increase loss despite probe verification. These exploratory results characterize sensing as a conditional substitute for RF probing or a source of loss reduction, depending on the limitations of link feedback and on the accuracy and timeliness of sensing.
2610.20196.title: Sensing-Aided Vehicular Beam Tracking: System Gain Over Link Feedback and Probe-Verified Sensing Invocation

2610.20219.summary: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) equips cellular networks with the dual capability of data transmission and environmental sensing by sharing spectrum, waveforms, and radio hardware. While network-side sensing via transmission-reception points (TRPs) has been widely investigated, the use of user equipment (UEs) as sensing receivers introduces additional bistatic viewpoints and can improve target observability. UE-assisted operation is nevertheless constrained by small UE apertures and by waveform processing, especially when data-bearing communication signals are reused for sensing. The present paper investigates theoretical limits and operating conditions for UE-assisted passive target positioning, with emphasis on hybrid operation that fuses TRP--TRP and TRP--UE measurements. A unified OFDM-based signal-and-noise model is developed to cover both positioning reference signals (PRS) and communication waveform reuse with modulation-dependent noise enhancement. Based on this model, closed-form Fisher-information expressions and Cramer-Rao lower bounds are derived for delay and angular parameters and are mapped to positioning error bounds (PEBs) for two estimator classes: time-angle positioning based on TDOA + DoA and delay-only 3D ellipsoid positioning based on excess-delay/TDOA measurements. Monte-Carlo simulations across reference SNR, subcarrier spacing and occupied bandwidth, modulation order, radar cross section (RCS), sensing mode, and positioning algorithm identify regimes where UE participation and hybrid sensing provide significant gains and quantify the associated estimator-to-bound trade-offs.
2610.20219.title: TRP-UE Bistatic Sensing for 6G Performance Analysis and Insights

2610.20233.comment: 7 pages, 3 figures, 2 tables. Full version including two appendices. A shortened version omitting Appendix A is being prepared for submission to IEEE ICC 2027
2610.20233.summary: Spatial reception under directed molecule transport requires balancing useful molecule capture against intersymbol interference (ISI). To characterize this balance, we study a fully absorbing spherical receiver that counts absorption events only within a prescribed cap. Using the known joint first-hitting law under aligned drift, we derive exact cap impulse, cumulative, and eventual responses. We perform stable cumulative evaluation. We then assess the derived responses through particle simulations and time-step comparisons, and demonstrate that our conditional-timing analysis explains when opposite drifts of equal magnitude can favor the same wider aperture. We also show that for the studied geometry and a symbol duration of $0.15$ s, the aperture that maximizes the signal-to-interference difference (SID) increases from $29.13^\circ$ at zero drift to $61.86^\circ$ at a drift magnitude of $40$ $\mu$m/s. These results (i) connect joint arrival-time and location statistics to spatial reception design, (ii) characterize the tradeoff between useful molecule capture and ISI, (iii) support SID-based aperture selection for a given drift and symbol duration, and (iv) quantify the SID loss incurred by retaining the zero-drift optimal aperture for the same symbol duration.
2610.20233.title: Exact Cap Response and Aperture Selection for Molecular Communication under Aligned Drift

2610.20269.summary: Single-channel radio-frequency (RF) signal separation is important for interference mitigation when a signal of interest overlaps with a co-channel interferer in time and frequency. Classical matched filtering and LMMSE receivers are limited under structured non-Gaussian interference, while diffusion and score-based methods often require iterative sampling or optimization. We propose FlowSep-RF, a rectified flow matching framework that learns a clean-endpoint transport from the received mixture to the signal of interest. The model combines time-domain IQ samples with frequency-domain features and recovers the separated waveform using one endpoint velocity evaluation. We evaluate FlowSep-RF on QPSK mixtures with OFDM-BPSK, OFDM-QPSK, and RFChallenge CommSignal2 interference against classical, discriminative, and generative baselines. FlowSep-RF achieves the lowest average BER and MSE among evaluated baselines across all three settings with one-step inference.
2610.20269.title: FlowSep-RF: Rectified Flow Matching for Single-Channel Radio-Frequency Signal Separation

2610.20282.summary: A generative site-specific beam prediction (Beam-STeP) method is proposed. Spatial priors from site-specific propagation and mobility information are jointly exploited with temporal priors from historical beam observations for beam prediction. To address the beam prediction ambiguity from multimodal spatio-temporal priors, the generative model is adopted, where a history-conditioned diffusion model is proposed to learn the multimodal conditional distribution of future beamforming vectors. Multiple beam candidates are sampled from the distribution using a denoising diffusion implicit model (DDIM). The candidate with the highest received power is then selected for transmission. Simulation results across three urban scenarios demonstrate that: i) Beam-STeP generally achieves higher normalized beamforming gains than the baselines under the same probing budget, particularly as beam prediction progresses; ii) site-specific propagation and mobility priors improve recursive beam prediction performance; and iii) DDIM sampling enables a flexible gain-latency trade-off.
2610.20282.title: Beam-STeP: Generative Site-Specific Beam Prediction with Spatio-Temporal Priors

2610.20296.summary: A single low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite offers almost no spatial degrees of freedom. Its two polarizations, however, can be exploited to carry a second layer to a handset, which 5G New Radio (NR) non-terrestrial networks do not use yet. The gain of this layer in downlink spectral efficiency (SE) is mapped over the footprint of a satellite at 330 km altitude above Munich transmitting at 2 GHz. The channel is modeled as a cascade of Jones factors for the phased-array payload, Faraday rotation, a dual-polarized land mobile satellite (LMS) channel with a line of sight, and a standardized handset antenna element at three attitudes. For a handset with boresight pointing to zenith, ideal precoding selects rank 2 with a probability of at least 0.95 within about 340 km of the nadir point at a reference signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of 6 dB. With closed-loop precoding, such a handset on the nadir track is in rank 2 during 99% of a pass. At 13 dB, rank selection with closed-loop precoding raises the mean SE over the footprint by 49%, and upright handsets gain about 31%. Their gain is limited to the positions where they face the satellite, since the element gain is low behind the handset. At 3 dB, these gains fall to 15% and 7%.
2610.20296.title: Opportunities for Direct-to-Cell Polarization MIMO in the S-band Downlink of a LEO Satellite Footprint

2610.20323.comment: 11 pages, 2 figures. A shorter version has been submitted to the 2027 IEEE Information Theory Workshop (ITW)
2610.20323.summary: We study cache-aided linear computation in distributed systems where each source generates and stores its own data. An external receiver requests a linear combination of these data, and the sources use information cached before the request is known to reduce the communication needed to recover the requested result. In our model, each of the $N$ sources stores its own independent file over a finite field and has an additional cache of normalized size $M$. The receiver must recover any requested linear combination with zero error from the messages sent by the sources over separate noiseless links. We establish a lower bound on the worst-case communication rate over any finite field by analyzing several requests under the same cache placement. This bound determines the optimal rate when no additional cache is available. For binary files, we propose parity-aided placement (PAP), a coded-placement scheme that combines cached parities with uncoded symbols. For every $N\geq3$, we characterize its communication rate for each request and optimize its placement parameters to obtain a closed-form worst-case rate. The resulting achievable rate meets the lower bound for $0\leq M\leq1/(2N-1)$ and $M\geq(N-1)/N$, establishing the optimal memory--rate tradeoff in these two ranges.
2610.20323.title: Cache-Aided Linear Function Computation

2610.20338.summary: This work presents a dual-polarized rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) design for millimeter-wave (mmWave) or frequency range 2 (FR2) communications. Focusing on a practical implementation, we consider the specific scenario of a single transmitter serving two receivers (users) within the same time, frequency, and code resource block. The transmitter and each receiver are equipped with a pair of dual-polarized antennas. We first present the system formulation and compute the achievable rate expressions for discrete constellations. Based on these expressions, we propose and evaluate two receiver architectures: one based on successive interference cancellation (SIC) and a non-SIC decoder. Both designs exhibit comparable performance, and the combination of polarization diversity and RSMA provides the system with significant flexibility to adapt to different channel conditions when serving both users, while the non-SIC decoder enables a simpler hardware implementation. We then present a prototype implementation of the proposed design, operating at a carrier frequency of 25 GHz, and evaluate it by measuring the symbol error rate (SER) of the different data streams under various signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and polarization diversity conditions. The obtained measurements show good agreement with software simulations, thereby validating the system implementation. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first mmWave RSMA prototype reported in the literature and the first to exploit polarization diversity. Furthermore, given the selected carrier frequency, the proposed design may also find applicability in the upper portion of the envisioned FR3 band (7-24 GHz).
2610.20338.title: Dual-Polarized Rate-Splitting Multiple Access for mmWave Communications: A Practical Design and Prototype Implementation

2610.20377.summary: This paper investigates when and why stacking programmable metasurfaces into Stacked Intelligent Metasurfaces (SIMs) improves linear transformation synthesis at a fixed phase-control budget. The analysis shows that algebraic Jacobian rank alone is insufficient to characterize practical synthesis, which also depends on the strength and balance of the sensitivity directions generated by the available controls. A layer-resolved analysis of the cascade model explains how inter-layer propagation can generate complementary sensitivity directions. The relevance of this mechanism is then assessed using an S-parameter multiport model that includes electromagnetic coupling and multiple scattering. Numerical results in near- and far-field sensing scenarios show that distributing the same control resources across multiple layers can strengthen weak transformation directions, improve Jacobian conditioning, and substantially enhance synthesis accuracy. These findings explain why increasing depth can offer benefits that are not obtained by simply enlarging a single programmable surface, and identify layer complementarity and Jacobian conditioning as useful criteria for SIM architecture design.
2610.20377.title: To Stack or Not to Stack? Jacobian Conditioning and the Benefits of Depth in Metasurface-Based Linear Transformation Synthesis

2610.20387.summary: Open-source ray tracing (RT) frameworks are increasingly used for site-specific channel modeling due to their reproducibility and extensibility. In non-stationary mobility scenarios, repeated RT evaluations can generate different diffuse propagation paths without preserving their correspondence, limiting a consistent representation of their temporal evolution. To address this limitation, we extend diffuse scattering modeling in Sionna RT using persistent surface-associated scattering points. Their positions remain fixed, while their contributions evolve according to changes in the propagation geometry and visibility. The proposed approach is validated using empirical radio channel impulse response measurements in an urban vehicular scenario at 5.9 GHz. Compared with the standard Sionna RT baseline, the proposed model shows improved agreement with measurements in the delay and Doppler domains.
2610.20387.title: Modeling Diffuse Scattering in Mobility Scenarios: Ray Tracing Model and Measurement Validation

AI.conclusion: 显著提升了Fisher信息对数凸性常数的下界并缩小了尖锐值区间，但二维尖锐常数仍未确定。
AI.method: 在二维指标记号下构造精确的有理多项式恒等式与SOS证书（含11个正定Gram矩阵、491个严格正的主子式），结合独立的精确Fourier/高斯包络构造给出上界。
AI.motivation: 确定二维概率归一化热流下Fisher信息对数凸性不等式的最优常数，改进已知的 c=1/2 界并逼近尖锐值。

item.summary: We study the sharp constant in the differential inequality \[ I(t)I''(t)\geq c\,[I'(t)]^2 \] for Fisher information along the probability-normalized heat flow on $\mathbb R^2$. The unrestricted log-convexity value $c=1$ is false in two dimensions, whereas the known square-root convexity theorem gives the universal value $c=1/2$. We construct an exact, machine-verifiable sum-of-squares certificate proving the stronger universal bound \[ c\geq \frac{231691}{250000}=0.926764. \] Together with an independent exact Fourier/Gaussian-envelope construction, this gives \[ 0.926764\leq c_*<0.94176665012062, \] where $c_*$ is the sharp constant for positive-time Gaussian convolutions of arbitrary probability measures on $\mathbb R^2$. We formulate the proof in explicit two-dimensional index notation. The lower bound follows from an exact rational polynomial identity involving a strictly positive denominator, a weighted total derivative, and eleven positive rational Gram matrices. All $491$ recorded leading principal minors are strictly positive and the complete polynomial identity has zero residual. No symmetry, log-concavity, finite-variance, or finite-entropy assumption is imposed on the initial measure. The sharp value remains open.
item.title: An exact computer-assisted lower bound for Fisher-information convexity along the two-dimensional heat flow

item.comment: We take a step toward wireless networks that can compute as well as communicate, using analog RF computing to deliver AI inference to resource-constrained edge devices while simultaneously serving conventional data transmission. This is a follow-up to our analog RF computing framework: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.14331. To be presented at IEEE Globecom 2026
item.summary: Many resource-constrained edge devices require artificial intelligence (AI) services but are not powerful enough to store or execute neural networks (NNs). Analog radio frequency (RF) computing addresses this limitation by letting a base station (BS) multicast a waveform encoding NN weights to different clients. Each client then multiplies the received weight-encoded waveform with its locally generated input-encoded waveform through a passive mixer in its RF frontend, thereby realizing the matrix-vector multiplications (MVMs) needed for AI inference with an extremely low power and memory requirement. This can enable telecom operators to provide AI inference services to the edge devices connected to their networks. In practice, however, this multicast AI flow must share the spectrum, power, and spatial resources with other data flows. This paper considers a multi-user multiple-input multiple-output (MU-MIMO) downlink scenario and studies the resulting relative aggregate data rate reduction from integrating the multicast AI flow with the unicast data flows. We formulate a joint beamforming problem for the data and AI flows to maximize the aggregate data rate subject to computing accuracy, client energy, total power, and hardware-related constraints. We develop a weighted minimum mean-square error (WMMSE)-based algorithm to solve the problem. Numerical results based on 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) channels show that the relative aggregate data rate reduction from integrating an AI flow with data flows is below 5% in representative settings. This indicates that telecom operators can use analog RF computing to provide edge AI services while providing data communication services simultaneously.
item.title: Analog RF Computing for Integrated Data and AI Flows Over Wireless Networks

item.summary: A Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) framework is proposed for quickest change detection (QCD) where there are multiple experts, and each expert produces a sequence of statistics for change detection. A change is declared when a weighted sum of these statistics crosses a threshold. This framework is then applied to the problem of multi-stream QCD to obtain a family of powerful algorithms that outperform the best known algorithms in the literature. In the multi-stream QCD problem, a decision-maker observes multiple streams of observations. At the change point, the distribution of an unknown subset of the streams changes. The optimal algorithm based on a generalized likelihood ratio is computationally expensive. One of the most computationally and performance-efficient algorithms in the literature is the rank-weighted sum (RWS) scheme based on Shiryaev-Roberts statistics. It is shown in the paper that the MoE-based QCD algorithm for multi-stream data outperforms the RWS scheme. This is demonstrated through simulation results on real-valued Gaussian mean shift data and high-dimensional data from Gaussian--Bernoulli Restricted Boltzmann Machines (GB-RBMs).
item.title: A Mixture-of-Experts Framework for Multi-Stream Quickest Change Detection

item.summary: This paper considers uplink channel state information (CSI)-based sensing as an opportunistic approach to enabling sensing in cellular networks, with minimum required modifications to the infrastructure. item.summary: This paper proposes a pinching antenna system to enhance the connectivity and efficiency in aerial wireless networks. The algebraic connectivity of the network's graph is maximized by optimizing the placement of the pinching antenna elements in the uplink and downlink waveguides. The number of deployed unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) is minimized while maintaining a minimum network connectivity indicator. A heuristic pinching antenna placement algorithm is designed to maximize the network connectivity. An iterative UAV deployment algorithm is also designed to find the minimum number of UAVs, their placement locations, and the pinching antenna placement. Simulation results show that the considered pinching antenna system improves network connectivity and efficiency.
item.title: Resilient and Efficient Aerial Wireless Sensor Networks Using Pinching-Antenna Systems

item.summary: High pulse repetition frequency (PRF) operation improves Doppler unambiguous sensing but reduces the maximum unambiguous range of a terahertz (THz) pulsed radar. Echoes from targets beyond this range can be incorrectly associated with subsequent transmitted pulses, causing the targets to appear at shorter ranges. This paper proposes a receiver-side framework that exploits the THz-specific temporal broadening effect as a distance-dependent signature to resolve range ambiguity. For each detected echo, the receiver applies broadening-matched filtering with references corresponding to candidate target ranges. The filter outputs are combined across pulses with Doppler compensation, and the largest normalised combined response identifies the ambiguity order needed to recover the true target range. The selected reference is then reused to reduce mismatch loss in subsequent range and velocity estimation. Simulations under known atmospheric conditions, with targets occupying distinct apparent-delay bins, demonstrate reliable range recovery beyond the conventional unambiguous interval. Range estimation errors conditioned on correct ambiguity-order identification, together with the reported velocity estimation errors, approach their corresponding derived Cramér--Rao bounds. The method preserves a fixed transmitted pulse shape, PRF, and sampling rate, at the expense of a higher signal-to-clutter-plus-noise ratio requirement for ambiguity identification relative to the evaluated diversity-based techniques.
item.title: Range Ambiguity Identification and Elimination by Leveraging Temporal Broadening Effect for THz Sensing

item.summary: Objective. Studies that decode imagined speech from scalp electroencephalography (EEG) commonly validate their pipelines with a positive control, usually overt speech, and report null results without stating what effect size the pipeline could have detected. Approach. Using ds003626 ("Thinking out loud"), KaraOne and Track 3 of the 2020 International Brain-Computer Interface Competition, we audited decoding of overt speech, articulator preparation and imagined speech with artifact-channel subsets, band-limited decoding and trial selection, under a protocol that enforces split integrity by assertion. We injected class-dependent effects of known amplitude into the real recordings to measure the detection floor of five decoder families, and we checked the ds003626 labels against the dataset's acquisition protocol. Main results. On ds003626, two lip electrodes decoded overt speech at 0.7430 and the eight external channels at 0.7068, against 0.4231 for the 128-channel scalp montage, and no decodable signal survived in the 8-30 Hz band. On the other two corpora, within-subject accuracy rose monotonically with frequency into the range dominated by muscle activity. Band-power logistic regression detected an injected 8-30 Hz desynchronization of 0.54 uV under a criterion fixed in advance, whereas a compact convolutional network (EEGNet) detected nothing within subject up to 4.31 uV. In ds003626, the condition codes are the reverse of the intuitive reading, the class encoding changed between public releases, and condition is a deterministic function of time within each session. Significance. In these corpora the overt-speech positive control is dominated by myogenic signal and cannot validate a decoding pipeline. We recommend that speech-decoding studies report band-limited and artifact-channel accuracy, the direction of accuracy across frequency, and a measured detection floor.
item.title: How large an effect would we have seen? Positive controls, detection floors and dataset pitfalls in scalp-EEG speech decoding

item.summary: Objective. A decoder of imagined speech that works for a new user without calibration would make a non-invasive speech interface practical. We tested whether imagined-speech content recorded with scalp electroencephalography (EEG) transfers across people, and examined why accuracy within a single person remains low. Approach. We analyzed three public corpora, ds003626, KaraOne and Track 3 of the 2020 International Brain-Computer Interface Competition, under a protocol that enforces split integrity by assertion and reports exact binomial thresholds, group tests and bootstrap confidence intervals. We trained decoders on each participant and tested them on every other, compared representational geometry across participants without a classifier, applied subject-level alignment, and tested five explanations for the within-subject ceiling. Main results. Across 482 ordered pairs of participants, no pair survived correction for multiple comparisons; mean pair-transfer accuracy lay within 0.006 of chance on every corpus, while every within-subject reference lay above it. Imagery against pre-stimulus rest generalized at about 0.61 after artifact and elapsed-time controls, but its decoder labelled the interval preceding imagery as imagery as often as imagery itself, so the contrast reflects a post-stimulus state, not imagery. Within subject, only the competition corpus decoded above threshold for every participant (0.3147; chance 0.200); syllable count explained little of this, but its frequency profile failed an artifact audit. Significance. In these corpora, imagined-speech content did not transfer between people through any representation we examined. Trial count per class was the only variable that ordered the corpora, which favors larger single-condition datasets over further model development.
item.title: Cross-subject decoding of imagined speech from scalp EEG: a leakage-controlled evaluation on three public corpora

item.summary: Received OFDM grids preserve both pilot and payload observations, yet wireless foundation models are rarely pre-trained on them. We introduce LWM-TF, a 9.58M-parameter factorized masked autoencoder pre-trained on complex 5G NR uplink grids taken after the FFT and before channel estimation. Each block attends first across OFDM symbols and then across resource blocks and receive antennas, and the mask follows the same two axes. Because the payload phase is unpredictable, the model reconstructs the normalized log-power of each masked token and predicts its scale separately; ablations show that the two terms are complementary and that this target outperforms complex-signal reconstruction. The encoder is pre-trained on 850,496 physical uplink shared channel (PUSCH) slots from a 10^6-slot dataset simulated with the NR transmit chain under various channel conditions. With the encoder frozen, linear probes classify modulation, predict CRC success, and detect UE mobility. On a separately generated test set, 16 labeled slots per class give 0.85 modulation accuracy, 0.82 CRC area under the ROC curve (AUROC), and 0.73 mobility AUROC, ahead of a supervised CNN on every paired draw. With 10,000 labels the probes reach 0.94, 0.96, and 0.92, well above engineered receiver statistics, and detect mobility where the CNN stays at chance. Without any impairment labels, distances in the frozen feature space flag unseen waveform impairments with 0.78 macro AUROC, against 0.68 for receiver statistics. A single pre-trained encoder thus provides receiver features that transfer across tasks, most strongly when labels are scarce.
item.title: LWM-TF: A Wireless Foundation Model on 5G NR Time-Frequency Resource Grids
