item.summary: In settings such as online recommendation platforms, medical decision-making with interim summaries, and stochastic control with static plants, the underlying system is often static so that the next state depends only on the most recent action. Moreover, the true system state is high-dimensional and cannot be observed directly, so actions must be selected based on information received through a rate-limited communication link, which constrains the control performance. This leads to a fundamental rate-cost tradeoff$\unicode{x2014}$the minimum communication rate required to achieve a prescribed average control cost. We study this tradeoff for a class of static systems we term static time-invariant control (STIC) systems, namely, control systems in which the next state depends on the history only through the most recent control action via a time-invariant kernel. For general control systems$\unicode{x2014}$not necessarily static or time-invariant$\unicode{x2014}$our prior work characterized this tradeoff through the limit of a sequence of directed-information minimization problems. However, the dimension of these problems grows with the time horizon, making the limiting formulation computationally intractable. In the present paper, we show for STIC systems that this growing-size formulation admits a single-letter characterization. This identifies STIC systems as the control-side counterpart of Noisy Output is the STate (NOST) channels$\unicode{x2014}$one of the few channel models whose feedback capacity admits a single-letter characterization. This yields, to our knowledge, the first constant-size convex characterization of the rate$\unicode{x2013}$cost tradeoff beyond linear quadratic Gaussian (LQG) control.
item.title: Single-Letterization of Rate-Cost Tradeoffs in Static Time-Invariant Control (STIC) Systems

item.summary: We study the identification capacity of discrete-time Gaussian multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) channels under per-antenna, per-symbol peak-amplitude constraints. We establish upper and lower bounds on the identification capacity that scale linearly with the channel rank $r.$ The number of reliably identifiable messages can grow super-exponentially with blocklength $n,$ following $M_n(R)=2^{(n\log n)R},$ where $R$ is an achievable rate. The channel rank provides a spatial-multiplexing advantage, enabling higher achievable rates and, consequently, stronger super-exponential codebook growth. These results characterize the rank-dependent gain in achievable identification performance.
item.title: Gaussian Identification in MIMO Channels

item.summary: Frequency-hopping MIMO integrated sensing and communications (FH-MIMO-ISAC) supports agile multidimensional signaling but faces challenges in phase-continuous transmission, demodulation without channel-phase information, and coherent processing of multi-frequency echoes. We propose a continuous-phase frequency-hopping (CP-FH) MIMO ISAC waveform with matched communication and radar processing. Information is conveyed jointly by frequency combinations and continuous-phase-modulation symbols. CPM phase accumulation and frequency-hopping linear-frequency-modulation phase compensation maintain phase continuity and reduce spectral leakage. We derive exact inter-element orthogonality conditions, residual cross-correlation bounds, and a bound on averaged transmit-beampattern ripple. For communication, projection-energy demodulation requires no channel-phase information and approximates least-squares detection under weak inter-branch correlation. It separates frequency-combination search from CPM-symbol decisions, reducing complexity while retaining direct joint-search decisions. For radar, structure-matched coherent processing combines space-time-frequency matched filtering, velocity-consistent Doppler focusing, and frequency-aperture focusing to form a three-dimensional coarse-range--velocity--fine-range response. It reduces Doppler-mismatch loss and extra detections from periodic range grating lobes in conventional pulse-Doppler processing. We further derive the joint range response, output signal and noise powers, and receive beampattern. The analysis characterizes target-discrimination limits under periodic ambiguity and shows that the proposed processor preserves frequency-aperture range resolution and full-aperture angular resolution, with equal output noise power under the stated conditions.
item.title: Continuous-Phase Frequency-Hopping MIMO Signaling and Processing for ISAC

item.summary: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) is evolving from a primarily physical-layer research into a standardized cellular-network capability spanning channel modeling, radio procedures, network architecture, and the delivery of sensing services. We review this progression within the Third Generation Partnership Project (3GPP), from Release 19 service requirements and target-aware channel modeling to the Release 20 New Radio (NR) sensing evaluation framework, radio access network procedures, and system architecture, and discuss future directions toward 6G. We then present two 3GPP-aligned simulation case studies to demonstrate the corresponding evaluation approaches. The first case study compares hard-decision, soft-decision, and hybrid fusion for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) sensing using multiple transmission and reception points (TRPs). Detection, false alarms, and conditional position and velocity accuracy are evaluated using receiver-derived angle estimates and separately calibrated method-specific thresholds. The second case study compares ideal and practical sensing-assisted predictive handover with conventional handover, while accounting for sensing error and information age. We further present a testbed-based measurement study that characterizes monostatic and bistatic UAV radar cross sections across frequencies, platforms, and observation angles and provides empirical support for correlated target-response modeling. Finally, we discuss open challenges and future research directions in multi-node fusion, resource and interference management, network evolution, security, privacy, and reproducible evaluation. Together, these components connect calibrated channel models, link- and system-level simulation, real-time prototypes, controlled measurements, and field trials through a staged evaluation roadmap.
item.title: Integrated Sensing and Communication in 3GPP: Standardization, Performance Evaluation, and Experimental Validation Toward 6G

item.summary: This study investigates efficient detector designs for the blind detection of orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) signals with unknown power, bandwidth, and carrier frequency in wideband spectrum sensing. We first describe the received signal model and conduct an asymptotic covariance analysis to obtain a tractable discrete-time representation. Based on this model, generalized likelihood ratio test (GLRT) detectors are derived for both known and unknown noise power cases in a single-antenna receiver setting. The proposed framework is subsequently extended to multi-antenna receivers, and the corresponding multi-antenna GLRT detectors are developed for both known and unknown noise power cases. Importantly, using the cumulative-sum (CUSUM) operations, the resulting detectors reduce to an efficient one-dimensional (1D) search in both single-antenna and multi-antenna settings. We also provide theoretical analysis for the conventional energy detector (Conv-ED) and the hypothetical uniformly most powerful (UMP) test to reveal the impact of system parameters on detection performance. In addition, computational complexity analysis is presented for both the proposed and conventional detectors. Finally, comprehensive simulation results are provided to evaluate the probability of detection. The results demonstrate that the proposed detectors achieve performance close to that of a genie-aided detector while significantly outperforming conventional detection approaches.
item.title: An Efficient Blind Detection of OFDM Signals with Unknown Parameters

item.summary: This paper characterizes the achievable rate region of a rotatable antenna (RA)-assisted multiple-input single-output (MISO) interference channel. We exploit the additional spatial degrees of freedom (DoFs) offered by the dynamic orientation of RAs to simultaneously enhance the desired signal and suppress interference, thereby significantly enlarging the achievable rate region of the interference network. To this end, we invoke the rate-profile technique to formulate a sum-rate maximization problem for jointly optimizing the transmit beamforming and the array rotation, subject to the practical mechanical constraints of the RAs. For the special case of a two-receiver scenario, we introduce the concept of subspace correlation coefficient to derive closed-form solutions for the optimal RA rotation angles and transmit beamforming vectors. Inspired by the insights obtained in the two-receiver special case, we propose an efficient two-step optimization framework to obtain a high-quality solution for the general multi-receiver case. In particular, the array rotation angle of each transmitter is optimized to minimize the leakage interference to non-associated receivers. With the optimized array rotation angles, the optimal transmit beamforming is obtained by invoking the second order cone programming based approach. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed solution achieves near-optimal performance and that integrating RAs effectively simplifies transceiver designs by enabling simple maximum ratio transmission (MRT) beamforming with negligible performance loss.

item.summary: Mobility in three-dimensional (3D) cellular networks induces frequent handovers and random sojourn times for aerial users. Analyzing these events is challenging because they jointly depend on user trajectories and random service-boundary geometry. This paper develops a unified geometric--kinematic framework in which service regions form a stationary random tessellation, their boundaries constitute a random closed set, and user motion follows a cruise--turn mobility model. Under the stated stationarity, isotropy, and independence conditions, the handover rate satisfies the exact law \(H=(S_V/2)\bar v\), where \(S_V\) is the specific surface area and \(\bar v\) is the long-run mean speed. The forward boundary-distance distribution provides the local geometric input to an effective-traversal approximation for the mean remaining sojourn time. These results link global and local geometric descriptors to complementary mobility metrics. Combining the handover law with link coverage yields a handover-aware effective spectral efficiency for base station (BS) density selection and service-architecture comparison. We then specialize the framework to Poisson--Voronoi single-BS service and Poisson--Delaunay four-BS coordinated multi-point service; under both models, the handover rate scales as \(\lambda^{1/3}\bar v\). Numerical results corroborate the exact handover expressions, assess the sojourn-time approximations, and show how user speed and interruption duration affect the preferred density and architecture.

item.summary: Digital semantic communication (SemCom) is emerging as a bandwidth-efficient paradigm for next-generation wireless networks by delivering the meaning of a source over finite constellations. However, the broadcast nature of wireless channels exposes transmissions to adversarial wardens, while discrete symbols deviate from the Gaussian signaling assumed by conventional covert communication. In this paper, we propose a covert digital SemCom system assisted by movable antennas (MAs), where the constellation, the antenna positions, and the semantic transceiver are jointly designed to conceal the transmission while preserving the semantic fidelity. Specifically, the maximum covert rate against the optimal detector with unknown noise level is derived in closed-form, which reveals that the legitimate signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) scales with the moment-matching order of the constellation and the spatial gain provided by the MA array. A Gauss-Laguerre ring constellation is then designed to raise the moment-matching order under the peak power constraints, and a covert symbol mapping with rank-to-ring assignment and scrambling is developed to carry the semantics in the ordering of the latent magnitudes. Guided by the derived semantic distortion bound, the semantic encoder and decoder are trained end-to-end through an invertible flow over the designed constellation and MA array. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme supports a higher achievable covert rate and improves the reconstruction quality by 24% compared to state-of-the-art SemCom schemes.

item.summary: The growing diversity of wireless services in sixth-generation (6G) wireless communication systems calls for reusable channel representations that support multiple tasks across different propagation environments. However, deploying such representations between user equipment and the base station in frequency-division duplexing systems faces uplink feedback constraints. This paper proposes a distributed framework based on an angle-delay-domain large wireless model (LWMa) for multiple tasks. LWMa exploits angle-delay structure and delay truncation to improve feature extraction and reduce computational cost. A scenario-specific network inspired by Perceiver IO (input-output) compresses embeddings for channel reconstruction tasks, while other tasks use a low-dimensional compact global embedding. Embedding reconstruction training followed by channel-quality-guided fine-tuning preserves information useful for downstream processing. Simulations demonstrate that the proposed method supports effective channel reconstruction and multiple tasks under limited feedback with reduced deployment complexity. Further evaluations show that the recovered embeddings generalize to additional tasks and support split inference.

item.summary: When a mobile terminal takes part in over-the-air training, its own motion rotates the gradient that travels back through it; a movable antenna that keeps pace with the terminal rotates it back---without any channel estimate. We give a speed law: under a scalar conditional-mean model of the physical return, landing the residual displacement inside the first positive lobe of the spatial correlation keeps the conditional mean gradient a descent direction, which, given sufficient travel, fixes a critical actuator-to-terminal speed ratio. We further prove a bias--jitter law: under the same scalar conditional-mean model and with zero effective bias, independent zero-mean Gaussian jitter of any finite amplitude scales the conditional mean gradient without reversing its direction, whereas a sub-wavelength systematic bias can reverse it. This result motivates prioritizing bias calibration to preserve gradient direction. Simulations on 3GPP CDL-A channels show that an antenna keeping pace with the terminal achieves near-CSI accuracy without digital channel correction, reaching 98.58 % compared with 98.59% for the ideal-CSI reference. The simulations also show that partial compensation can support learning when the residual displacement falls within a later positive correlation lobe, so a faster actuator does not necessarily yield higher accuracy. Separate positioning simulations show a sharp accuracy loss under systematic bias but little degradation under zero-mean Gaussian jitter of comparable spatial scale.
item.title: Keep Pace to Learn: Movable Antennas Restore the Backpropagated Gradient Under User Mobility

item.summary: Sometimes the best way to correct an aged gradient is to wait. In physical backpropagation, a receiver returns its loss gradient through the reciprocal channel. With a single moving antenna, the mean gradient returned at the antenna is the true one counter-rotated by the phase of the temporal correlation. In simulation, uncorrected training fails in negative correlation lobes and revives in positive ones. At correlation zeros the return is independent of the forward channel, so no linear correction has a mean to recover; near them, more calibration barely helps, but holding the return until the next correlation extremum does.
item.title: Wait to Learn: Lobes and Dead Zones in Physical Backpropagation over an Aging Single-Antenna Channel

item.summary: A channel can be almost perfectly coherent and still teach a transmitter the wrong direction. In physical ("over-the-air") backpropagation, the receiver sends its loss gradient back through the reciprocal channel; when the terminal moves in between, mobility does not merely add noise to the returned gradient, it rotates it. Under a scalar conditional mean model the rotation is set by the phase of the temporal correlation, so coherence, which measures only its magnitude, is the wrong ruler: in simulation, channels with absolute value of rho greater than 0.9 drive uncorrected training to 51.7% accuracy, while phase correction restores 92.5%. Arrays add a twist. Near zeros of the trace correlation, scalar correction fails even with rho known exactly, yet most of the information is still there: noise has moved it onto neighbouring antennas. Re-indexing the ports by the displacement, with zero digital feedback, recovers the lost performance in simulation, and so does rotating the returned seed with the unitary polar factor of the conditional mean operator, never inverting it; aligning each antenna's phase with its own past makes things worse. An exact array identity explains all three. The lesson fits in one line: correct the rotation, not the stretch.
item.title: Coherent but Discordant: Rotate, Don't Invert, to Backpropagate Through an Aging Channel

item.summary: Localization errors in estimating the position of a potential eavesdropper (Eve) pose a critical challenge to secure transmission in reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems. To address this issue, this paper proposes a sensing-assisted robust secure transmission framework that exploits ISAC sensing to characterize the positioning uncertainty induced by these errors. The RIS is partitioned into a reflection region and a sensing reception region, supporting sensing and communication through spatial separation. By jointly exploiting observations collected at the base station (BS) and the RIS sensing reception region, maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) is employed to estimate the arrival angles, from which Eve's three-dimensional (3D) position is obtained through cross localization. The resulting localization Cramer-Rao lower bound (CRLB) is then used to construct an ellipsoidal uncertainty region around the estimated position. A two-stage optimization strategy is developed. In Stage I, the sensing beamformer and RIS reflection coefficients are jointly optimized to improve localization accuracy. In Stage II, the resulting positioning uncertainty is incorporated into a robust secure transmission design, where the communication beamformer and RIS reflection coefficients are jointly optimized to maximize the worst-case secrecy rate. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms benchmark schemes without RIS assistance and with random RIS configurations in terms of secrecy performance. The proposed framework effectively mitigates secrecy performance degradation caused by localization errors in Eve's position.
item.title: Robust Design of Sensing-Assisted Secure Transmission for RIS-Aided ISAC System under Eavesdropper 3D Positioning Uncertainty

item.summary: Wireless Technology Recognition (WTR) enables identifying wireless technologies from received radio signals and is important for spectrum monitoring and management systems. Existing approaches either rely on handcrafted signal features with limited robustness or computationally intensive Deep Learning (DL) models operating on high-dimensional In-phase and Quadrature (IQ) samples or spectrograms. In this paper, we investigate a different hypothesis: wireless technologies can be distinguished through the temporal evolution of their local time-frequency complexity. To capture this behavior, we propose a lightweight WTR framework based on two-dimensional dispersion entropy. Entropy values are extracted from successive spectrogram regions to characterize the evolution of local spectrogram complexity throughout a transmission and summarized into a compact feature representation for classification using a Multilayer Perceptron (MLP). The framework is evaluated on seven wireless technologies, namely IEEE 802.11ah, IEEE 802.15.4 SUN-FSK, IEEE 802.15.4 SUN-OFDM, LoRa, IEEE 802.11n, LTE, and 5G NR, at Signal-to-Noise Ratios (SNRs) ranging from -20 dB to 40 dB. Experimental results show that the proposed approach consistently outperforms IQ-based and Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT)-based Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) baselines, particularly at low and moderate SNRs. Averaged across all evaluated SNR levels, it achieves 82.73% accuracy, corresponding to improvements of 23.8% and 14.6% over the IQ-based and STFT-based CNN approaches, respectively. Furthermore, the approach maintains its recognition advantage with data-augmented training while requiring substantially shorter training times. The results demonstrate that temporal evolution of local spectrogram complexity provides a robust technology-specific fingerprint and an effective, computationally efficient representation for WTR.
item.title: Entropy-Based Wireless Technology Recognition

item.summary: Visible Light Positioning (VLP) offers high-precision indoor positioning using existing LED infrastructure. However, in VLP systems using Photodiodes (PDs) as receivers, rapid movement of the PD causes measurement inaccuracies as the Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT) processing yields averaged rather than instantaneous Received Signal Strength (RSS) values. To address this challenge, we propose an RSS correction algorithm that integrates Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) data with VLP observations to compensate for motion-induced distortions. Our approach leverages IMU-derived motion parameters to model the temporal variation of optical signals during the DFT window, enabling instantaneous RSS estimation. The algorithm is embedded within both tightly and simply coupled VLP/INS integration frameworks that estimate the pose of the moving receiver. This work targets highly dynamic indoor navigation. Simulations validate the correction model, and total-station-tracked experiments confirm reduced RSS discrepancies against model references. Across eight held-out high-dynamic handheld trials with peak translational and angular speeds of 2.25 m/s and 284 deg/s, correction reduces the pooled 3D position and PD-normal inclination root mean square errors relative to the LiDAR/IMU reference with a shared IMU by 56.0% and 71.9%, respectively. Both datasets and source code are publicly available.
item.title: IMU-Aided Motion Compensation of RSS Measurements for Dynamic Visible Light-Inertial Localization

item.summary: The interpretability of artificial intelligence models has become a central concern, especially for black-box models such as multilayer perceptrons (MLPs). Kolmogorov-Arnold Geometry has recently emerged as a framework for analysing the internal representations of these networks, by examining how the hidden layer locally responds to changes in the input through the minors of its Jacobian. The degree to which a few of these minors dominate the rest, known as their concentration, has so far been measured with the Participation Ratio. Although this metric has useful properties, its maximum value depends on the size of the network, so a given value cannot be read as high or low concentration without reference to the architecture. To overcome this limitation, in this paper we propose the $\alpha$-RC metrics, a family of Rényi-based concentration measures that compare the normalized magnitudes of the minors with the uniform distribution through the Rényi divergence of order $\alpha$. All the metrics in the family are bounded between 0 and 1 regardless of the architecture, with 0 indicating that the magnitude is evenly spread over the minors and 1 that it is carried by a single one. Moreover, the metrics are non-decreasing in $\alpha$, and for $\alpha$ = 2 they reduce to an explicit transformation of the Participation Ratio. Computational experiments with single-hidden-layer MLPs trained on a synthetic dataset show the benefits of our proposal.
item.title: A Class of Rényi-based Concentration Metrics for Kolmogorov-Arnold Geometry in Multilayer Perceptrons

item.summary: We derive an upper bound on the rate of a linear code capable of list decoding from insertion and deletion errors. Subsequently, we show that a linear code can list decode from at most $n - \frac{L}{L+1}k + 1$ insdel errors with fixed list size $L$, and that this bound is strict when the code does not contain the all-ones vector. We also provide a simple construction of codes achieving the optimal rate for any given list size capable of correcting a single insdel error. All the results hold for linear codes over finite fields of size $q \geq 3$.
item.title: A Generalized Half-Singleton Bound for List Decoding of Insertion/Deletion Errors

item.summary: Multi-carrier underwater integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) realizes concurrent acoustic communication and localization, yet the frequency selectivity of the acoustic channel creates uneven positioning capabilities across subcarriers. This paper proposes a localization-oriented subcarrier and power allocation scheme for multi-anchor underwater ISAC systems. We build a unified orthogonal subcarrier multiplexing framework and derive closed-form Cramer-Rao bounds (CRBs) under frequency-selective channels with colored noise. We derive a subcarrier-level localization information contribution from the time of arrival Fisher information, which enables localization-oriented resource allocation. We derive several theoretical properties regarding the distance and frequency dependence of the localization information metric, and establish a distance-frequency matching principle. These results provide a theoretical foundation for localization-oriented resource allocation and guide the design of a low-complexity greedy algorithm that improves positioning accuracy. Specifically, the algorithm iteratively allocates subcarriers to minimize the residual positioning-error objective, thereby improving positioning accuracy while satisfying communication quality-of-service (QoS) constraints. Simulations verify that our method yields much lower positioning error bound than uniform, random and high-frequency-first subcarrier allocation in symmetric or asymmetric topologies while guaranteeing communication QoS, achieving superior communication-localization tradeoffs.
item.title: Joint Subcarrier and Power Allocation for Localization-Oriented Multi-Carrier Underwater ISAC Systems

item.summary: Wireless foundation models (WFMs) seek to unify diverse wireless tasks and scenarios, yet existing methods still rely on task- or scenario-specific components or deployment-time fine-tuning. This paper presents an all-in-one wireless model (AWM), a WFM that unifies multi-user channel acquisition and localization, despite their distinct data modalities and functional objectives. We reveal that user location and channel state information (CSI) at different frequencies can be viewed as attribute-specific measurements of the same wireless link. By introducing in-scenario same-attribute reference pairs as prompts, AWM converts heterogeneous attributes into alignable relativity representations, formulating intra-band channel interpolation, inter-band channel prediction, and wireless localization as unified wireless-state transformations. Further, a multi-task MateFormer is developed to perform source-attribute relativity extraction, cross-attribute relativity alignment, and target-attribute synthesis within a unified architecture, avoiding task-specific output heads or downstream fine-tuning. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of model unification, including substantial gains from cross-task knowledge sharing, seamless generalization to unseen scenarios, and an efficient closed-loop service for mobile users.
item.title: AWM: An All-in-One Wireless Foundation Model for Multi-User Channel Acquisition and Localization Without Downstream Tuning

item.summary: As a waveform candidate for next-generation wireless systems, affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM) has often been compared with orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) under different configurations, while a systematic comparison of their pilot-based sensing performance remains lacking. This paper establishes a comparison with the same bandwidth, frame duration, pilot energy, and reserved-resource overhead. OFDM-random, OFDM-fixed-comb, and OFDM-shifted-comb pilots are compared with AFDM pilots surrounded by guard resources using aperiodic ambiguity functions without cyclic prefix/chirp-periodic prefix (CP/CPP) and cyclic ambiguity functions with CP/CPP, followed by target detection experiments. The results show that OFDM-fixed-comb exhibits low range sidelobes but periodic range ambiguity peaks, while AFDM and OFDM-shifted-comb effectively suppress zero-Doppler range ambiguities. Within the common unambiguous region, all pilot configurations for both waveforms exhibit similar detection thresholds in strong-target detection, while structured OFDM and AFDM pilot placements outperform OFDM-random in weak-target detection. At high mobility, the AFDM receiver using the discrete affine Fourier transform (DAFT) can resolve integer Doppler beyond the conventional slow-time maximum unambiguous velocity, outperforming the tested conventional OFDM and AFDM receivers at the increased search complexity. These results separate the effects of waveform, pilot placement, and receiver processing, providing a basis for AFDM and OFDM pilot-based sensing design.
item.title: Pilot-Based Sensing With OFDM and AFDM: A Resource-Matched Performance Comparison

item.summary: CSI feedback is fundamental to proposed uses of Wi-Fi sensing such as human activity recognition (HAR); but it also constitutes significant overhead as resources must be allocated away from data communications. Wi-Fi CSI extraction can be explored along two dimensions in IEEE 802.11bf: reporting intensity, i.e., temporal resolution, and number of reported subcarriers, i.e., spectral resolution. We explore periodic and IEEE 802.11bf threshold-based reporting at matched rates, and uniform decimation and block-mean grouping at matched report sizes. We further propose reporting the mean CSI accumulated since the last report. Using the 802.11bf report size as the metric, we evaluate the accuracy-cost tradeoffs on three public datasets with our proposed model, a convolutional neural network combined with a gated recurrent unit and temporal pyramid pooling. The proposed periodic reporting with mean payload and block-mean grouping improves accuracy by up to 53 percentage points at equal CSI overhead cost. Temporal resolution is generally more cost-effective than spectral resolution. With only at most 7.7% of full-CSI feedback cost, the proposed scheme achieves 96-98% of full-CSI accuracy.
item.title: Temporal vs Spectral Resolution in CSI Reporting for Wi-Fi ISAC

item.summary: The mobility of potential eavesdroppers (Eves) poses a critical challenge to physical-layer security (PLS) in integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems, since rapidly varying Eve positions lead to time-varying eavesdropping channels and outdated security decisions. To address this challenge, this paper investigates sensing-driven secure transmission for reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted ISAC systems with a maneuvering Eve. To this end, by exploiting the dual functionality of the ISAC waveform, a multi-view angle estimation method jointly exploiting the base station (BS) and RIS is developed based on MUSIC and maximum likelihood estimation (MLE), enabling three-dimensional (3D) Eve localization, whose accuracy is characterized by the Cramer-Rao lower bound (CRLB). Subsequently, an interacting multiple model extended Kalman filter (IMM-EKF) with out-of-sequence measurement (OOSM) compensation is employed to track and predict the maneuvering Eve. Based on the predicted trajectory, the time-varying eavesdropping channel is updated, and the transmit beamforming and RIS phase shifts are jointly optimized subject to a sensing CRLB constraint. Furthermore, an alternating optimization (AO) algorithm integrating fractional programming, semidefinite relaxation (SDR), and Riemannian manifold optimization is developed to solve the resulting non-convex problem. Finally, numerical results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in accurately tracking maneuvering Eves and enhancing secure transmission in dynamic ISAC environments.
item.title: Sensing-Driven Secure Transmission with Mobile Eavesdropper Tracking in RIS-Assisted ISAC

item.summary: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) has been recognized as a critical technology for the sixth generation (6G) wireless networks. Under monostatic sensing mode, achieving a balance between communication and sensing performance via optimal beamforming is a critical research problem. In multiple input multiple output (MIMO) systems, such beamforming problems are of substantial computational complexity due to the large number of antennas. Existing methods exploit exact subspaces of lower dimensions to speed up the beamforming process where the complexity is proportional to the number of communication users and sensing targets instead of antennas. In this paper, it is demonstrated that the beamforming problem can be solved in an even lower-dimensional subspace with only a small sensing performance loss. Numerical results compare the sensing performance and computational complexity of ISAC beamforming problem in the exact subspace and smaller subspaces.
item.title: A Smaller Subspace is All You Need: Efficient ISAC Beamforming via Dimensionality Reduction

item.summary: Stress detection based on heart rate variability (HRV) has received increasing attention. However, existing personalized approaches integrate personal attributes with HRV through latent representations, limiting the interpretability of their interactions. In this work, we propose an LLM-enhanced personalized stress detection framework that integrates HRV features and personal attributes through LLM-based semantic interpretation. The proposed framework achieves a 29.9% relative MCC improvement over the strongest baseline on TILES-2018 while providing human-readable descriptions of individual physiological responses. The results highlight the potential of LLM-based semantic interpretation for achieving both effective and interpretable personalized stress detection.
item.title: Beyond Latent Personalization: Integrating HRV-Conditioned Personalization via LLM for Interpretable Stress Detection

item.summary: Non-terrestrial networks (NTNs), such as Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites, can provide consistent coverage for Internet of Things (IoT) nodes, particularly in rural areas where cellular coverage is lacking. These IoT nodes are used to monitor and record their surroundings, supporting various applications, including real-time applications. In such cases, transmission of the most up-to-date data is essential, making the Age of Information (AoI) a critical metric to consider. The AoI measures the elapsed time from the data generation at the source node to its reception at the destination. Moreover, the Peak AoI (PAoI), which denotes the maximum AoI in the system before an update is received, provides valuable insights into the network's performance. Therefore, this encourages us to focus on the PAoI within a large-scale and fully loaded IoT network, which is covered by LEOSATs. Using tools from stochastic geometry, this paper derives the spatial distribution of the uplink mean PAoI in a LEOSAT-enabled IoT network. To achieve that purpose, the meta distribution of the uplink conditional coverage probability is derived. Numerical results articulate how varying the number of deployed LEOSATs and their altitudes affects the coverage probability meta distribution and the spatial distribution of the mean PAoI. Additionally, by examining various scenarios with different numbers of LEOSATs and altitudes, we can derive valuable insights to determine the optimal beamwidth for LEOSATs tailored to each specific scenario to minimize the conditional mean PAoI.
item.title: Spatial Distribution of Mean PAoI in LEO Satellite-enabled IoT Networks

item.summary: With the rapid development of low-altitude economy (LAE), low-altitude information networks (LAINs) must provide reliable communication, environmental sensing, and target identification to support efficient and safe airspace operation. Although integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) provides a foundation for the joint design of communication and sensing, identification must also be incorporated to meet airspace safety and regulatory requirements. This paper reviews integrated sensing, communications, and identification (ISCAI) for LAE. We first review low-altitude communication, sensing, and identification approaches and explain how representative applications motivate their integration. We then summarize low-altitude ISAC fundamentals, including system architectures, channel modeling, unified signal models, and performance metrics, followed by communication-centric and sensing-centric designs, resource allocation, and aircraft trajectory optimization. Building on these, we introduce ISCAI, focusing on a backscatter communication (BackCom)-based identification mechanism in which backscatter devices serve as electronic license plates for aircraft. We present system and signal models for integrated sensing and identification (ISAI) and ISCAI, together with multifunctional receiver designs and mutual integration gains. Finally, we discuss open problems and future directions, including an information-theoretic framework, artificial intelligence-empowered system design, and reconfigurable intelligent surface-enhanced ISCAI. This review provides a structured perspective on the evolution of LAINs toward integrated communication, sensing, and identification.
item.title: Integrated sensing, communications, and identification for low-altitude economy

item.summary: The classical theory of arcs in finite projective spaces provides a powerful geometric framework for studying maximum distance separable (MDS) codes and their possible lengths. In this paper, we investigate how this perspective extends to maximum sum-rank distance (MSRD) codes, whose geometric description involves systems of linear sets rather than individual projective points. Our main goal is to understand how the block structure of an MSRD code constrains its length. In dimension three, we determine the possible intersection patterns of lines with the associated linear sets and obtain explicit formulas for their characters and the weight distribution of the corresponding codes. These results lead to new length bounds and show that the block structure comes at a cost: the presence of a block of rank at least two reduces the maximum possible total length by at least $q-1$, and sufficiently long MSRD codes must be classical, that is, MDS codes over $\mathbb F_{q^m}$. We also prove that three-dimensional one-weight MSRD codes do not exist. In arbitrary dimension, we interpret shortening geometrically as projection and establish a general projection bound that extends classical counting arguments for arcs. This yields restrictions depending explicitly on the block profile and, for full-length blocks, identifies parameter ranges in which linearized Reed--Solomon codes attain the maximum possible number of blocks. Finally, we construct an exceptional three-dimensional MSRD code over $\mathbb F_9$ with three blocks of length two and propose a sum-rank analogue of the MDS conjecture.
item.title: On the Length of Maximum Sum-Rank Distance Codes

AI.conclusion: 解析PLR模型可作为有效奖励驱动强化学习资源分配，在卫星直连LoRaWAN大规模场景下显著降低丢包率、提升网络容量，优于随机分配。
AI.method: 构建联合多普勒损伤与时频域碰撞的解析PLR模型，用蒙特卡洛仿真验证；以PLR为奖励，采用DQN与PPO两种强化学习算法优化扩频因子/信道等资源分配。

item.summary: Long range wide area network (LoRaWAN) has a long communication range and low power consumption, making it a potential technology for direct-to-satellite (DtS) Internet of Things (IoT) connectivity. However, packet collisions and Doppler impairments brought on by satellite motion can greatly increase the packet loss ratio (PLR) in large-scale DtS-IoT networks. In this paper, we study resource allocation in DtSIoT LoRaWAN by first developing an analytical PLR model that simultaneously takes Doppler impairments and packet collisions in the temporal and frequency domains into account. In order to maximize resource allocation, the generated PLR is then used as the reward function for two reinforcement learning (RL) schemes: deep Q-network (DQN) and proximal policy optimization (PPO). Simulation results validate the analytical PLR model against Monte Carlo simulations and demonstrate significant improvements over random resource allocation. At a target PLR of 3*10^-2, while random allocation supports only 100 end devices (EDs), PPO and DQN support approximately 650 and 690 EDs, respectively, representing nearly a seven-fold increase. Furthermore, for 800 EDs, PPO and DQN increase the total number of transmitted packets by 106.7% and 88.0%, respectively, compared with random allocation.
item.title: Packet Loss Analysis Under Doppler Effects and Reinforcement-Learning-Based Resource Allocation for Direct-to-Satellite LoRaWAN

item.summary: Conventional sleep staging provides a coarse-grained representation that obscures within-stage depth variation. We developed ECG-SDI, a single-lead electrocardiography (ECG) framework for continuous sleep-depth profiling and digital biomarker extraction. Using 12,392 overnight polysomnographic recordings, we trained and validated a two-stage deep learning model supervised by conventional sleep-stage labels. Correlations with ordered stages excluding rapid eye movement (REM) sleep were 0.828 in the pooled internal test set and 0.848 in the external Cleveland Family Study; corresponding REM classification AUROCs were 0.954 and 0.977. Overnight trajectories captured within-stage variation. Biomarker-based phenotyping identified a disturbed subtype associated with poorer subjective sleep quality and higher all-cause mortality in the Sleep Heart Health Study (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.20; 95% CI, 1.05-1.38). Among 507 participants with paired recordings before and after continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP), normalized sleep-depth area increased by 6.1% and shallow-sleep burden below 0.3 decreased by 16.0%. Exploratory analyses linked reductions in approximate entropy and depth variability to reduced oxygen desaturation and increased sleep efficiency, respectively (Spearman rho = 0.24 and 0.12); both associations remained positive after covariate adjustment. Mean ECG-SDI within N2 increased by 0.017 (95% CI, 0.004-0.030). A wearable proof-of-concept illustrated the acquisition-to-report workflow. These findings support ECG-based sleep phenotyping and further evaluation of CPAP response monitoring at home.
item.title: ECG-SDI: Single-lead Electrocardiogram Enables Continuous Sleep Depth Index Profiling and Scalable Digital Biomarkers for Sleep Health
