2610.24243.title: Pilot-Projected Nonlinear Self-Interference Estimation with Simultaneous Uplink Training

2610.24274.summary: Illicit activity in financial networks is difficult to detect. We exploit the idea that the chance of a transaction being illicit depends partly on the concurrent positions and recent actions of counterparties, as well as the higher-order organization of fund flows. We combine hypergraph features and machine learning to demonstrate practical ef fectiveness. Specifically, we use the Elliptic++ Bitcoin dataset to show that graph and directed-hypergraph-based features improve illicit-address classification. The suc cess of the predictive model then allows us to examine potential money-laundering chains are structurally fragile. Several illicit-to-licit transaction motifs with unknown intermediary addresses specified, and the fragility of these motifs is evaluated through progressive removal of the highest-risk intermediaries. Surprisingly, these motifs are fragile, suggesting that money laundering could be disrupted via the identification and exclusion of owners of a limited number of crypto wallets.
2610.24274.title: Directed-Hypergraph Analytics and Fragility Testing for Anti-Money Laundering

2610.24368.summary: High-frequency (HF) skywave radars require high gain at elevation angles of 3 degrees to 30 degrees, where vertically-polarized monopoles over lossy land suffer from pseudo-Brewster cancellation. This letter shows that curving a long monopole creates a horizontally-polarized radiation channel much less affected by this cancellation. Closed-form bounds derived from the space-wave field over a homogeneous half-space show that the vertical-current field is suppressed below an elevation set by the soil permittivity, whereas the horizontally-polarized field of an elevated arc is nearly unaffected by the soil. Bayesian optimization (BO) of an analytical model, followed by 182 full-wave HFSS simulations with analytical Fresnel far-field post-processing, was used to design the element at 15 MHz. Over moist soil, a 15-m element with an 86 degrees arc is near-resonant (-25-dB match), 93% efficient, and 25% lower than a straight element of equal length. It raises the azimuth-averaged 3 degrees-30 degrees gain by 2.5 dB and, on every land ground considered, exceeds the 0.575{\lambda} straight monopole that is optimal over seawater and PEC by 1.0-2.6 dB.
2610.24368.title: Curved HF Monopole Antennas for Improved Low-Angle Skywave Gain Over Lossy Ground

2610.24415.summary: The broadcast nature of integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) signals exposes them to physical-layer security (PLS) threats, including eavesdropping and jamming. Conventional fixed-position antennas provide limited spatial flexibility under highly correlated legitimate, sensing, and adversarial channels, while multi-static cooperative ISAC offers distributed spatial diversity but remains vulnerable to information leakage. To address these limitations, this article proposes a novel movable antenna (MA)-enabled multi-static cooperative secure ISAC framework centered on dual-scale spatial reconfiguration. Specifically, continuous MA repositioning reshapes local propagation channels, while distributed multi-static nodes provide complementary network-level spatial diversity. Their synergy transforms local antenna geometry and distributed network geometry into a unified controllable spatial resource for jointly enhancing communication, sensing, and PLS. This article first presents the system architecture of the proposed framework and its representative application scenarios, followed by an analysis of the physical-layer mechanisms underlying the resulting gains. Subsequently, we elaborate on the key enabling technologies for practical deployment. A case study further demonstrates the communication-sensing-security trade-off and antenna-saving potential of the proposed framework. Finally, open challenges and future research directions are identified toward practical MA-enabled multi-static secure ISAC networks.
2610.24415.title: Movable Antenna-Enabled Multi-Static Cooperative Secure ISAC: Architecture, Mechanisms, and Enabling Technologies

2610.24416.summary: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) is envisioned as a cornerstone technology for next-generation networks, yet it introduces significant security risks in both communication and sensing domains. To mitigate the coverage limitations inherent in conventional mono-static or bi-static setups, this paper proposes a networked ISAC framework empowered by movable antennas (MAs). By leveraging flexible antenna reconfiguration, MAs provide additional spatial degrees of freedom to significantly boost beamforming gain and interference suppression. Specifically, we investigate a novel dual-domain security paradigm where networked base stations collaboratively protect uplink (UL) and downlink (DL) transmissions from communication eavesdropping while simultaneously safeguarding target sensing data against sensing eavesdroppers (SEs). To this end, we formulate a joint optimization problem to maximize the sum of secrecy rates, subject to sensing requirements, SE eavesdropping probability constraint, and practical MA deployment constraints, by jointly optimizing receive combiners, transmit beamformers, UL power allocation, and MA positions. To address this non-convex problem with highly coupled variables, an efficient alternating optimization algorithm is proposed, integrating closed-form solutions for receive combiners, successive convex approximation for transmit beamforming and UL power, and a tailored sensing-aware multi-candidate particle swarm optimization for the high-dimensional MA positioning. Extensive numerical results validate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithms, demonstrating that the proposed MA-enabled networked cooperative ISAC design significantly outperforms conventional fixed-position antenna-based designs in terms of security performance, while achieving notable power- and antenna-saving gains.
2610.24416.title: Dual Secure Sensing and Communications in MA-Enabled Networked ISAC Systems

2610.24529.summary: This paper investigates discrete-activation pinching antenna (DAPA) systems, where a finite set of pinching antennas (PAs) is deployed along a dielectric waveguide, from which PAs are selectively activated to serve users. Performance analyses are developed for both orthogonal multiple access (OMA) and non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) by explicitly accounting for the system geometry and discrete PA activation. Specifically, analytical expressions for the outage probability (OP) and ergodic rate (ER) are derived. Furthermore, the discrete-to-continuous gain ratio (DCGR) is introduced to quantify the normalized ER gain of a finite PA deployment relative to the single-PA and continuous-activation references. Monte Carlo simulations validate the derived expressions and show that DAPA systems can closely approach continuous-activation performance with only a moderate number of candidate PAs. For example, under the considered setup, DAPA with five PAs recovers approximately 92% and 90% of the continuous-activation ER gain under OMA and NOMA, respectively, at a transmit power of 0 dBm.
2610.24529.title: Performance Analysis of Discrete-Activation Pinching-Antenna Systems

2610.24578.comment: 11 pages, 6 figures, 4 tables, submitted to an IEEE venue for possible publication
2610.24578.summary: Maternal and perinatal deaths are concentrated in low- and middle-income countries, where routine fetal monitoring is largely inaccessible. With the prevalence of smartphone as personal assistive gadget, we ask whether a phone's built-in microphone, with no extra hardware or emitted signal, can serve as a software-only maternal-fetal cardiac screening aid when moved from the chest to the lower abdomen? We report a longitudinal, self-recorded case study of a single subject (Z) over the last five weeks of a singleton pregnancy, later delivered at term without complications: 28 short, uncontrolled recordings (rest, morning, post-exercise). Lacking maternal/fetal ground truth, we exploit the prior that maternal and fetal heart rates occupy largely disjoint frequency bands, blindly decomposing a Shannon-energy envelope into two candidate-rate bands, and additionally probe a slower breathing-rate band as a rest/exercise discriminator. A fast, regular, fetal-plausible rhythm was recovered from most recordings and remained essentially unchanged across maternal activity states, consistent with normal fetal cardiac autonomy; a slower, noisier maternal-plausible rhythm was recovered less reliably. Beat-to-beat variability proved largely noise-dominated at our short window lengths, and the breathing-rate probe did not significantly separate rest from exercise; both are reported as negative findings. We position the work within AI for global health: a low-cost screening aid for remote and underserved communities, pending reference-validated follow-up, not a replacement for clinical monitoring.
2610.24578.title: Passive Smartphone-Microphone Phonocardiography for Joint Maternal-Fetal Cardiac Well-Being Monitoring: A Longitudinal Self-Recorded Case Study in Late Pregnancy

2610.24581.summary: The beam squint effect has traditionally been viewed as detrimental to near-field wideband beamforming due to the reduction of beamforming gain towards the desired direction. In this paper, we show that it can instead be harnessed as a benefit in a hardware-constrained orthogonal frequency division multiple access (OFDMA) system, where the system, equipped with a single radio-frequency (RF) chain, aims to serve multiple spatially distributed users by allocating different subcarriers to different users. By exploiting the beam squint effect, flexible frequency-dependent beamfocusing patterns are realized via parallel true-time-delay (TTD) units, enabling nearly full beamforming gain across users. In particular, we formulate a max-min rate optimization problem that jointly designs the time delays, subcarrier-user association, analog beamforming, and power allocation. To tackle the resulting nonconvex mixed-integer problem, a two-stage optimization framework is proposed. In Stage~I, subcarrier-user association and structured analog beamforming are jointly optimized. In Stage~II, power allocation is obtained via bisection search and inverse water-filling. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method can achieve a significant improvement by utilizing beam squint to serve multiple spatially distributed users in OFDMA systems.
2610.24581.title: Exploiting Beam Squint for Near-Field Wideband Beamforming in Multi-User OFDMA Systems

2610.24622.comment: IEEE International Symposium on the Internet of Sounds (IS2) 2026
2610.24622.summary: Native real-time audio engines meet audio deadlines but are hard to connect to machine-learning workflows, while tensor frameworks integrate with machine learning but process audio as offline batches without timing guarantees; runtime layers built on them inherit the host's scheduling and deployment footprint. This paper presents Fluxion, a Rust audio DSP runtime for cascaded second-order sections, FIR filters, and delay-line effects. Fluxion implements the parts that are specific to DSP: closed-form filter design, forward kernels, analytic adjoints for the recursion, and stability checks. It relies on existing libraries for the autodiff graph, GPU code generation (tested here on CUDA), and array interchange. One graph algebra is lowered to a differentiable training engine and to an allocation-free real-time engine; between them, a trained graph is checked for stability and frozen into a versioned artifact that an edge device checks again before playback. We compare Fluxion with six framework-hosted and native baselines under one float32 protocol. Among the systems that compute the exact recursion, Fluxion has the highest GPU throughput when data stays on the device and the highest throughput on most CPU workloads, while its CPU training step is slower than those of torchaudio and GRAFX. Its test suite checks the audio thread for allocations with an instrumented allocator, and we report measured latency tails. Fluxion is open source at \url{this https URL}.
2610.24622.title: Fluxion: A Differentiable DSP Runtime from Training GPU to Real-Time Edge

2610.24641.summary: Internet of Things (IoT) networks require reliable and spectrally efficient wireless links to support massive device connectivity and high mobility applications. To meet these requirements, this paper investigates a widely linear (WL)-empowered receiver design for affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM) with faster-than-Nyquist (FTN) signaling under practical receiver in phase and quadrature imbalance (IQI). The considered AFDM-FTN system couples the direct and image branches with FTN induced intersymbol interference (FTN-ISI) and delay-Doppler spreading in the affine domain. To address this coupled interference structure, a unified conjugate augmented input output model is established for IQI impaired AFDM-FTN systems. Based on this model, a WL minimum mean square error receiver with parallel interference cancellation (WL-MMSE-PIC) is developed, where WL-MMSE preprocessing is followed by the proposed hard decision PIC (HD-PIC) and damped soft decision PIC (SD-PIC). The proposed receiver is further analyzed in terms of the local stability of HD-PIC, a genie aided performance reference under ideal residual interference cancellation, and the impact of the AFDM chirp parameter on the post equalization interference distribution. Simulation results show that the proposed WL-MMSE-HD-PIC and WL-MMSE-SD-PIC receivers achieve significant error rate performance gains over the conventional linear-MMSE and WL-MMSE baselines. The results further show that FTN signaling provides a nominal spectral-efficiency gain, while residual-coupling-based chirp-parameter selection reduces the post-equalization residual coupling and improves detection reliability for high-mobility IoT links.
2610.24641.title: Widely Linear-Enhanced IQ Imbalance Interference Cancellation for AFDM-FTN Systems

2610.24651.summary: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) has been recognized as a key enabler for future wireless communication systems. However, existing ISAC designs based on MIMO-OFDM generally fail to fully exploit the spatial degrees of freedom and the communication data payload, resulting in restricted target sensing performance. To cope with this issue, in this paper we propose a novel target sensing method for full-dimensional (FD) MIMO-OFDM ISAC systems based on coupled tensor decomposition. We first characterize the system model of FD MIMO-OFDM ISAC, where the base station employs a large number of antennas in two dimensions and facilitates both sensing and communication via the data payload of OFDM signals. Then, we formulate the problem of estimating target parameters as a coupled canonical polyadic decomposition (CPD) problem, which jointly leverages the echo signals of communication data payload over multiple subcarriers in the frequency domain. The theoretical analysis indicates that the formulated coupled CPD problem possesses a more relaxed uniqueness condition compared with the ordinary CPD problem, thereby enabling more stable target sensing performance through the pure communication data payload in FD MIMO-OFDM ISAC. In addition, we develop a coupled CPD-based target sensing algorithm, where the target parameters, including azimuth and elevation angles, ranges, and velocities, are extracted from the decomposed factor matrices. Numerical results show that the proposed target sensing method achieves a higher success rate and more accurate parameter estimation than existing tensor decomposition methods.
2610.24651.title: Target Sensing in Full-Dimensional MIMO-OFDM ISAC Systems Via Coupled Tensor Decomposition

2610.24732.summary: Electroencephalographic (EEG) functional connectivity is quantified using diverse measures of statistical dependence, spectral coupling, phase synchronization, information transfer, directed interactions, cross-frequency coupling, and network topology. An important question is what can be inferred about one connectivity measure from another. This paper develops a mathematical framework that treats connectivity measures as mappings from an explicitly defined admissible state space to observable values. For a source measure and a target measure, the set of target values compatible with an observed source value is defined as a cross-connectivity attainable set. This formulation distinguishes exact determination, conditional determination using additional information, bounded inference, approximate identification, and non-identifiability. The framework is extended to multichannel connectivity matrices, graph measures, and dynamic connectivity. It also incorporates the influence of filtering, referencing, volume conduction, source leakage, inverse modeling, epoch duration, and estimator assumptions on admissible inferences. Analytical examples examine relationships between covariance and correlation, mutual information and correlation under joint Gaussianity, coherence and phase-locking value under restrictive signal conditions, and the general non-identifiability of the phase-lag index and weighted phase-lag index without additional assumptions. By making assumptions and attainable values explicit, the framework provides a systematic basis for determining what connectivity results can and cannot establish about other measures.
2610.24732.title: A Mathematical Framework for EEG Functional Connectivity: Taxonomy, Measure Relationships, Identifiability, and Analytical Bounds

2610.24788.summary: Random composition trees model the hierarchical semantic structures of meaningful texts as a statistical ensemble generated by recursively splitting texts into coherent chunks. A recent study shows that different text types can be described by random composition trees with distinct branching factors, and that the entropy rates of these trees exhibit a similar dependence across text types as the entropy rates of the actual texts. Motivated by this correspondence, we analyze information-theoretic properties of this stochastic splitting model. First, we demonstrate that the entropy of random composition trees grows linearly with the root size, and we derive an analytical expression for the entropy rate as a function of the branching factor. Second, we prove that large trees exhibit typicality: with high probability, they belong to a typical set in which each tree is approximately equally likely. Our analysis reveals that the random composition tree model shares two key information-theoretic properties of language when modeled as a stationary and ergodic stochastic process: linear entropy growth and typicality.
2610.24788.title: Information Theory of Random Composition Trees

2610.24800.summary: The wide footprint of low-Earth-orbit (LEO) satellite downlinks exposes the mere occurrence of a transmission to any receiver within it. This paper studies covert multiuser LEO downlinks, where a passive warden at an unknown but fixed ground location accumulates observations as the satellite moves. We jointly optimize the precoding and the occurrence probabilities of the multiuser symbol combinations to provide covertness against such wardens. Each phase-shift keying (PSK) symbol vector is decomposed into a relative pattern and a common rotation, so that shaping the pattern probabilities leaves the symbols of every legitimate user uniformly distributed. We develop probabilistically shaped symbol-level precoding and probabilistically shaped block-level precoding. We derive the exact chi-square divergence of the warden's Gaussian-mixture observation over the complete session and, by bounding the leakage over a continuous location uncertainty region, obtain certificates that guarantee covertness throughout that region. The certified covertness level is minimized under robust constructive-interference, power, and entropy constraints through an alternating optimization whose updates are equivalent to convex conic problems, and the optimized probabilities follow a Maxwell--Boltzmann-type law. Numerical results show that shaping substantially reduces the certified covertness level of both precoding structures, particularly under large location uncertainty, low elevation, and scarce power.
2610.24800.title: Joint Probabilistic Shaping and Symbol-Level Precoding for Covert LEO Satellite Downlinks

2610.24802.comment: Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Neural Systems and Rehabilitation Engineering
2610.24802.summary: The need for user-specific calibration remains an often-cited barrier to widespread adoption of myoelectric control. Cross-user models trained on large multi-user datasets can now recognize gestures from unseen users without calibration, but they have been evaluated almost exclusively offline, leaving open whether calibration is still needed in closed-loop control. This study compared six calibration-free controllers, trained on 306 users of the EMG-EPN-612 dataset and used without any calibration data from the test participant, against three calibrated controllers in a closed-loop Fitts' law target-acquisition task with sixteen participants. The calibrated controllers achieved higher offline balanced accuracy (90.6% against 73.1% for the best controller of each paradigm), but completion rates did not differ significantly between paradigms, and the highest completion rate was achieved by a calibration-free controller. Calibrated controllers moved faster on successful acquisitions, partly because of their individually fitted speed mappings, though not significantly after correction for multiple comparisons. However, every calibration-free controller produced more direct and stable trajectories than every calibrated controller, even after adjusting for cursor speed. Offline accuracy did not predict completion rate across controllers or within participants, and across paradigms higher offline accuracy was associated with poorer trajectory quality in 15 of 16 participants. Without any calibration data from the end user, a model trained across a large population matched calibrated control in completion rate and exceeded it in trajectory quality. The offline accuracy gained through calibration should therefore not be taken as evidence of a closed-loop benefit.
2610.24802.title: Is User Calibration Still Necessary for Continuous Myoelectric Control? A Closed-Loop Comparison of Calibration-Free Controllers

2610.24890.summary: We study quantization for inner-product estimation when storage and reading have separate budgets. In the static bit-probe model [Yao, 1981], an encoder stores $w$ bits about $x$ before seeing a query $y$, and a reader probes at most $r<w$ bits to estimate $x^\top y$. Both vectors lie in the $d$-dimensional Euclidean unit ball. Protocols may be randomized, and computation is unrestricted. Performance is measured by $d$ times the worst-case mean-squared error over $x,y$, averaged over protocol randomness. First, we show that query-independent reading cannot benefit from extra storage. Any such reader is equivalent to fully reading an $r$-bit message, even when later reads depend on previously returned bits. At fixed positive rates $W=w/d$ and $R=r/d$, the normalized minimax error converges to $1/(4^R-1)$, independent of $W$. The upper bound was already known [Ordentlich and Polyanskiy, 2025]. We prove the matching lower bound for arbitrary scalar decoders, extending the result for unbiased compressors [Safaryan et al., 2020]. Then, we show that query-dependent reading makes extra storage useful. We construct a two-batch protocol using Gaussian projections and random thresholds, with asymptotic normalized error at most $(\pi+o(1))/[4R\log(W/R)]$ as $W/R\to\infty$. At fixed $R$, this error vanishes as storage grows, giving an unbounded advantage over query-independent reading. We also prove a finite-dimensional lower bound for arbitrary encoders, decoders, and fully branching readers. In the doubly sparse regime $W/R\to\infty$ and $R\log(W/R)\to0$, it gives normalized error at least $(1-o(1))/[2R\log(W/R)]$. Thus, our protocol is optimal within a factor of $\pi/2$ in the leading constant.
2610.24890.title: Query-Dependent Reading for Quantized Inner-Product Estimation: A Minimax Separation

2610.24984.summary: Denoising diffusion probabilistic models (DDPMs) have emerged as a powerful framework for generative modeling by transforming standard Gaussian inputs into outputs that approximate a target distribution. While DDPMs have been proved to converge in total variation, KL divergence, and Wasserstein distance, these discrepancy measures share a fundamental limitation of being insensitive to distributional mismatch in low-probability regions. To address this, we adopt the stronger Rényi divergence as the discrepancy measure. Leveraging a Girsanov-type change-of-measure argument, we establish the first Rényi characterization of DDPMs to the best of our knowledge, showing that the total error decomposes into a mixing error, a discretization error, and a score estimation error. We assume the target distribution is sub-Gaussian and characterize the score error via the cumulant generating function, relaxing both the log-Sobolev-inequality and $L^\infty$-score-error conditions used in prior Rényi divergence analyses of inexact Langevin Monte Carlo, a score-based sampling algorithm closely related to DDPM. Our results also establish an iteration complexity for achieving $\epsilon$-accuracy in $\alpha$-Rényi divergence that is asymptotically proportional to $\alpha^3/\epsilon$. Finally, by extending our analysis, we establish the first Rényi divergence convergence guarantee for critically damped DDPMs, a kinetic variant governed by critically damped Langevin dynamics. Similar to existing characterizations of critically damped DDPMs, this result shares the structural scaling of standard DDPMs, differing by at most a logarithmic factor in the mixing error exponent, and supports the conjecture that critically damped DDPMs do not yield a theoretical improvement.
2610.24984.title: Convergence of Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models: A Rényi Divergence Perspective

2610.25041.comment: 31 pages. Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Information Theory
2610.25041.summary: How much mutual information is needed to achieve a target correlation between two copies of a prescribed distribution? We prove a sharp Gaussian extremal inequality for this self-coupling problem: among distributions with a fixed mean and covariance, the Gaussian has the greatest minimum information cost for meeting a positive semidefinite cross-covariance target. The inequality is strict for non-Gaussian distributions when the target is positive definite. The proof uses a midpoint gluing construction. Two Ornstein--Uhlenbeck half-bridges, each started from the prescribed endpoint law, meet at a common intermediate distribution and are joined by conditional gluing. Changing the Gaussian reference then turns the resulting relative-entropy bound into the desired extremal inequality. As a first application, scaling one endpoint of the self-coupling establishes Gaussian extremality for rate-distortion-perception with unlimited common randomness, under quadratic distortion and squared Wasserstein-2 perception measures. We also establish an analogous result for finite common randomness, where the problem involves two mutual information constraints associated with an auxiliary random variable. In that setting, we retain an intermediate observation on one half-bridge and balance the two information budgets simultaneously using the Poincaré-Miranda theorem.
2610.25041.title: A Self-Coupling Gaussian Extremal Inequality for Information-Constrained Optimal Transport with Applications to Rate-Distortion-Perception

2610.25044.summary: Multiobject tracking (MOT) is a fundamental capability in autonomous navigation, radar and sonar systems, as well as 6G integrated sensing-and-communication (ISAC) networks. In this paper, we propose a neural-enhanced track-before-detect (TkBD) framework that operates directly on complex-valued raw signals and learns a latent representation of unmodeled propagation effects during runtime. We introduce an environment-dependent latent intensity variable that characterizes the signal power of each object in the shared propagation environment. The probability density function of this intensity variable is represented by a normalizing flow and trained online in an unsupervised manner within the sequential Bayesian inference procedure. The learning objective is derived from a variational Bayes formulation by maximizing the evidence lower bound (ELBO), thereby accounting for the uncertainties inherent in the Bayesian TkBD problem. To enable scalable inference, we make use of a recently introduced Bayesian TkBD framework that combines belief propagation, which avoids high-dimensional operations, with sequential Monte Carlo methods for efficient low-dimensional updates.
2610.25044.title: Normalizing Flow for Neural-Enhanced Track-Before-Detect

2610.25098.comment: 24 pages, 4 figures. Complete proofs and experimental details included. Both authors contributed equally
2610.25098.summary: An agent can retain information before receiving a future question and later retrieve evidence from an archive. Evaluating this arrangement requires accounting for both retained information and the width of each retrieval response. Decision-tree capacity bounds describe individual sets of distinguishable records, but a memory writer must encode every possible record before the query is known. We study fixed-length retention beside an immutable binary archive, with a worst-case limit on raw bit or word reads. We characterize feasible one-bit-read memory cells and construct encoders that partition the complete record space. Supporting pairwise exclusive disjunction and conjunction with one bit read is equivalent to supporting every Boolean query. For multiple reads, we combine explicit encoders with decision-tree counting and an entropy converse. The word-read bounds differ by at most two retained bits when the read budget is at most half the archive length. Under an explicit condition on word width and archive length, raw-word caching attains the exact optimum among all writers. A related condition preserves this optimum under positive average error. Exhaustive checks validate the implementations. In a matched dialogue-agent study, a categorical sufficient statistic preserves source decisions with less storage and lower decoding latency than the universal encoder. A catalogue-specific index reduces private state further and requires additional shared storage. The results characterize how response width and future query structure determine retention requirements.
2610.25098.title: Pre-Query Retention with Bounded Bit and Word Retrieval

2610.25106.summary: With the advent of 6th Generation (6G) wireless networks, integrating Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) and Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave (FMCW) waveforms presents a promising solution for simultaneous communication and sensing. While OFDM offers high communication performance, it requires complex transceivers for sensing applications. Conversely, FMCW is easily implemented for sensing but provides low data rates for communication. This letter derives the mathematical relationship between OFDM and FMCW, showing how FMCW can be generated from the diagonal elements of the OFDM modulator (\ie, the Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT) matrix). We propose a novel approach that leverages the DFT matrix to seamlessly integrate these two waveforms, minimizing interference and enabling high data rate communication alongside low-complexity sensing receiver design. Extensive simulations demonstrate the effectiveness of our technique in achieving simultaneous sensing and
2610.25106.title: A Novel OFDM-FMCW Waveform for Low-Complexity Joint Sensing and Communication

2610.25124.summary: This paper considers a cell-free (CF) network under active eavesdropping. We show that nonlinear power amplifier (PA) distortion, together with the per-access point (AP) large-scale-gain fingerprint of the attack, can be exploited across cooperating APs to enhance physical layer security (PLS). Classical zero-forcing (ZF)-artificial noise (AN) precoders rely on a linear transmitter and an unbiased estimate, and thus cannot exploit either. We propose a distortion aware graph neural network (GNN) precoder that designs the signal beams at cooperating APs and exploits both the PA distortion and the per-AP fingerprint to enhance the secrecy rate, combined with a null-space AN block to form the GNN-AN scheme. The GNN is trained on channel estimates biased by an uplink pilot-spoofing attack to maximise the average per-user secrecy rate. Simulations across different numbers of APs show uniformly higher outage secrecy rates than ZF-AN under attack, reaching gains of 15% at the 1% outage level and 8.9% at the 5% outage level at L = 32 APs, input back-off (IBO) = -1 dB, and attacker-to-targeted user pilot power ratio of 0.5, under the same signal/AN power split.
2610.25124.title: Secure Distortion-Aware GNN Precoding under Active Eavesdropping in Cell-Free Networks

2610.25168.comment: Submitted to IEEE International Conference on Communications (ICC 2027)
2610.25168.summary: Affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM) is a promising waveform for future high-mobility communications due to its Doppler robustness and diversity gain. However, existing continuous-time AFDM relies on chirp-dependent wideband receive filtering, which increases noise power and causes channel-energy leakage. In this paper, we propose an AFDM reception scheme based on pre-filter de-chirp for doubly selective channels. The coupling between de-chirp and the channel is first characterized, yielding an equivalent path representation with delay-coupled effective Doppler shifts. The discrete affine Fourier transform (DAFT)-domain equivalent channel is then derived under general transmit pulse shaping and linear time-invariant receive filtering, showing that the effective filtering kernel depends only on the relative sample offset and avoids the additional spreading caused by conventional chirp-dependent filtering. The receive-noise power is further analyzed, and an explicit expression for the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) gap is obtained by the required receive-filter bandwidths. Simulations verify the theoretical SNR analysis and show that the proposed scheme significantly outperforms the conventional scheme while approaching ideal discrete-time AFDM.
2610.25168.title: Receiver Design for Continuous-Time AFDM based on Pre-Filter De-Chirp

2610.25199.comment: To be published in the proceedings of the 16th International Conference on Indoor Positioning and Indoor Navigation (IPIN)
2610.25199.summary: Accurate radio-based indoor localization remains challenging in multipath-rich and dynamic indoor environments. Supervised fingerprinting methods achieve high positioning accuracy by learning mappings from radio channel measurements to physical locations, but require costly position labels and frequent recalibration. Channel Charting (CC) addresses this limitation by learning low-dimensional representations of Channel State Information (CSI) without position labels, yielding channel charts in which nearby points correspond to nearby physical locations. However, prominent CC methods rely on setup-specific dissimilarity metrics, such as ADP-, CIRA-, or PDR-based distances, and on precomputed $O(n^2)$ distance matrices, limiting scalability and transferability across radio systems. We propose ChronoChart, a timestamp-supervised CC framework that requires only CSI and timestamps without prior knowledge for training. Our method jointly optimizes complementary objectives: a triplet loss using temporally derived positive and negative samples to establish coarse global structure, a temporal-proximity loss that promotes smooth trajectories in the chart, and a joint-embedding loss that enforces consistency between representations of different augmentations. Evaluated on real-world 5G, MIMO, and passive UWB data, our method matches or exceeds prior CC baselines that depend on tailored distance metrics, and remains scalable and applicable across heterogeneous radio systems.
2610.25199.title: ChronoChart: Setup-Agnostic Channel Charting for Label-Free Indoor Localization

2610.25201.comment: To be published in the proceedings of the 16th International Conference on Indoor Positioning and Indoor Navigation (IPIN)
2610.25201.summary: Reliable radio-based indoor localization is essential for industrial automation, yet existing methods are often evaluated in environments that do not fully reflect the severe multipath and non-line-of-sight (NLOS) conditions encountered in real deployments. This limits our understanding of how AI, i.e., modern geometric, unsupervised, and semi-supervised localization methods generalize to industrial 5G settings. We present RAIL-5G, a public real-world 5G NR channel impulse response (CIR) benchmark recorded in an operational railway maintenance facility. RAIL-5G covers an 811m$^2$ indoor area with eight distributed radio units, robot-mounted user equipment (UE) trajectories, high-accuracy iGPS reference positions, and severe metal-induced multipath caused by train compartments and maintenance infrastructure. We benchmark geometric time-difference of arrival (TDoA), supervised fingerprinting, unsupervised channel charting, and self-supervised wireless pretraining methods. Our results highlight the difficulty of RAIL-5G: on the full dataset, TDoA reaches 7.02m mean average error (MAE), the best unsupervised method reaches 2.46m, and supervised fingerprinting achieves 0.52m. Self-supervised pretraining reduces the labeling effort by up to one order of magnitude, but the remaining gap to supervised learning shows that robust AI-based localization under severe multipath remains an open challenge. The dataset and code are available at this https URL.
2610.25201.title: RAIL-5G: A Challenging Real-World Dataset and Benchmark for AI-Based 5G Indoor Localization

2610.25490.summary: Recent advances in artificial intelligence have contributed to several information-theoretic results through genuinely different modes: a language model may suggest a proof, participate in an extended mathematical dialogue, coordinate computation, or operate as one component of a search harness. Treating all of these as "AI-discovered mathematics" obscures distinctions that matter for scientific reliability, attribution, and reproducibility. This article examines a set of recent cases through a four-stage pipeline: how the problem was formulated; how AI participated in finding a solution; how the resulting analytical and computational claims were verified; and how machine-generated outputs were translated into mathematical exposition for human understanding. Based on these cases, we recommend that research publications (1) disclose the nature and extent of AI assistance at each stage, (2) report verification of analytical reasoning separately from certification of numerical computations, and (3) place more emphasis on articulating the underlying ideas, techniques, and interpretations.
2610.25490.title: From Formulation to Articulation: Considerations for AI-Assisted Research in Information Theory

2610.25526.summary: We analyze the reconstruction error of a low-dimensional Hermite--Gaussian (HG) ptychographic method used in real-time Wigner distribution deconvolution (WDD) reconstruction. We derive an upper bound on the discrepancy between the low-dimensional, aberration-corrected reconstruction and classical Fourier-domain WDD. The bound decomposes the reconstruction error into contributions from HG--Fourier basis mismatch and aberration-coefficient mismatch, explicitly characterizing their dependence on the number of retained HG modes, Wiener regularization, aberration mismatch, and measurement dose. Numerical experiments on simulated electron and X-ray ptychographic data characterize these dependencies and demonstrate robustness to Poisson noise. These results provide theoretical and guidance for selecting the reduced representation and reconstruction parameters, enabling computationally and memory-efficient for near-real-time ptychographic reconstruction.
2610.25526.title: Low-Dimensional Hermite-Gaussian Representations for Ptychographic Reconstruction

2610.25643.summary: In this paper, we study the sampling of bandlimited signals on multigraphs, where several graphs with different shift operators are defined on the same set of nodes. Since the shift operators do not commute in general, they admit only a joint block diagonalization, and the frequencies of the multigraph signal model are matrices rather than scalars. Relying on a formal algebraic convolutional signal model, we introduce a notion of frequency and bandwidth for multigraph signals that does not depend on any individual layer, and we extend the notions of removable and uniqueness sets to multigraphs. We prove that the optimality of a sampling set is determined exclusively by the common Fourier basis and its invariant subspaces, and not by any individual layer, although the individual layers provide computable sufficient conditions that certify a sampling set as a uniqueness set. Since identifying which layers provide reliable certificates requires spectral information, we propose an aggregate operator that pools the information of all the layers, is computable directly from the shift operators, and certifies uniqueness without any assumption on the individual layers. This operator leads to a greedy sampling algorithm that does not require computing the joint block diagonalization. Numerical experiments on multigraphs whose layers order the frequencies inconsistently show that the proposed algorithm selects better-conditioned sampling sets and attains lower reconstruction errors than single-layer methods.
2610.25643.title: Sampling of Signals on Multigraphs: From Removable and Uniqueness sets to Spectral Proxies

2610.25644.comment: 6 pages, 4 figures. Submitted to IEEE ICC 2027
2610.25644.summary: We propose a posterior-mass rescue (PMR)-aided shifted-pruning SCL-flip decoder for CRC-aided polar codes. After CRC-aided SCL (CA-SCL) and differential-metric shifted-pruning recovery fail to find a CRC-valid candidate, PMR locally continues discarded prefixes stored during the initial CA-SCL pass, ranked by estimated posterior mass, without increasing the shifted-pruning retry budget. Simulation results for a (128, 64) code with the Reed-Muller (RM) rate profile and a (256, 128) code with the polarization-weight (PW) rate profile, both using an 11-bit CRC, show lower observed FER than SCLF-Diff (T = 15) and the considered literature baselines under the evaluated recovery budgets, with observed FER close to that of SCLF-Diff (T = 20). At the reported moderate and high SNRs, the average reconstruction-aware path-step count is within a few percent of that of SCLF-Diff (T = 20), while at 2.0 dB it is 9.4% and 4.3% higher for the two codes, respectively. The proposed decoder also has a larger worst-case path-step bound.
2610.25644.title: PMR-Aided Shifted-Pruning SCL-Flip Decoding for CRC-Aided Polar Codes

2610.25708.summary: Hybrid non-orthogonal multiple access (H-NOMA), which leverages the complementary advantages of orthogonal multiple access (OMA) and NOMA, has emerged as a promising technique for next-generation wireless networks. This paper investigates power allocation optimization for the OMA and NOMA time slots allocated to the opportunistic user in H-NOMA systems, aiming to overcome the limitations of conventional equal power allocation strategies. Specifically, we consider an H-NOMA scheme that integrates hybrid successive interference cancellation (HSIC) with power adaptation (PA), referred to as the HSIC-PA aided H-NOMA scheme. To better adapt to practical communication scenarios, distinct power coefficients are assigned to the OMA and NOMA time slots of the opportunistic user to maximize the achievable data rate. Closed-form expressions for the optimal power allocation coefficients are derived, and simulation results validate the accuracy and effectiveness of the theoretical analysis.
2610.25708.title: On the Optimal Power Allocation and Performance Analysis for the HSIC-PA Aided Hybrid NOMA

2610.25743.comment: The abstract was shortened to meet arXiv's requirements. The full version is included in the manuscript
2610.25743.summary: Secure aggregation enables a server to compute the sum of users' gradients or model updates without revealing individual values. With user dropouts, correlated random keys protect local gradients while allowing recovery of the desired gradient sum. We consider three phases: key distribution, masked-gradient upload, and mask elimination. Users establish correlated keys, upload masked gradients, and provide additional messages to eliminate residual aggregate masks. Existing information-theoretic schemes typically design mask-elimination communication for a prescribed dropout threshold and evaluate its cost under worst-case dropouts across the masked-gradient upload and mask-elimination phases. Such designs cannot adjust communication to actual dropout scenarios. Moreover, the randomness and communication costs of establishing correlated keys remain largely unexplored. To address these limitations, we formulate an adaptive secure aggregation framework under the T-colluding security constraint and construct a single scheme that supports all feasible dropout scenarios by adapting its communication to the actual number of dropouts. We establish converse bounds on four resources: key randomness, key-distribution communication, masked-gradient communication, and mask-elimination communication. The latter two bounds are characterized for each realized dropout set in the masked-gradient upload phase. The proposed scheme achieves the optimal masked-gradient communication rate for every feasible dropout scenario and the optimal mask-elimination communication rate in almost all feasible regimes. Its key rate and key-distribution communication rate are each optimal or within a factor of two of their respective information-theoretic optima. These results characterize the fundamental randomness and communication costs of secure aggregation with user dropouts.
2610.25743.title: Fundamental Limits of Information-Theoretic Secure Aggregation with User Dropouts in Federated Learning

2610.25794.summary: We propose a finite BSC-decomposition method for representing an arbitrary binary-input symmetric-output channel (BISOC) as a mixture of binary symmetric channels (BSCs) with at most $\ell+1$ distinct crossover probabilities. We show that the weighted average capacity of the component BSCs exceeds the capacity of the original BISOC by at most $(\pi^2\log e)/(48\ell^2)+O(\ell^{-5/2})$ bits, and the leading term is asymptotically optimal in the worst case. Based on the finite BSC-decomposition, we design a channel simulation scheme for arbitrary BISOCs. Combined with efficient channel simulation algorithms for BSCs, our scheme achieves a communication rate with $O((\log n / n)^{2/3})$ redundancy over the capacity for simulating $n$ copies of a BISOC.
2610.25794.title: Finite BSC-Decomposition of Binary-Input Symmetric-Output Channels and Applications to Channel Simulation

2610.25911.summary: Coherent distributed radar architectures enhance the detectability of low-reflectivity targets. However, conventional coherent processing generally entails prohibitively large volumes of inter-station data exchange, thereby motivating the adoption of one-bit quantization strategies. In this work, we investigate a clutter-dominated regime in which the interference is driven by a dense ensemble of weak scatterers. We demonstrate that, under these conditions, one-bit quantization can exhibit a vanishing performance loss with respect to ideal high-resolution sampling in terms of detection capability, in contrast to the classical 2 dB performance penalty associated with one-bit detection in white Gaussian noise environments. For unknown target velocity, we reformulate joint velocity-search processing under the effective one-bit model. Maximizing over the velocity plane makes false-alarm calibration an extreme-value problem for a correlated two-dimensional random field, whose maximum is not characterized by its pointwise null distribution alone. We therefore use an expected Euler characteristic approximation to calibrate the search threshold. We obtain analytic expressions for a separable two-station geometry and use constrained coefficient fitting for larger networks. Monte Carlo simulations demonstrate negligible quantization loss in the clutter-dominated setting and conservative false-alarm calibration under the tested Gaussian slow-time model.
2610.25911.title: One-Bit Coherent Distributed Radar Detection in Clutter via Velocity-Plane Search: Vanishing Loss and EEC-Calibrated Thresholding

2610.25952.summary: In this paper, we investigate the information bottleneck problem for sources that follow discrete-time ergodic finite-state Markov chains. We propose treating observations generated by the time-varying Markov chain as if they were drawn from its unique stationary distribution, and we use the solution to the information bottleneck problem for the stationary process to compress samples from the time-varying process. The resulting error is upper bounded by several information gap terms. We establish sufficient conditions under which these gaps converge to zero and analyze the convergence rates of the different information gap terms. The proofs are based on intricate analysis using convergence of subsequences along with the derivation of properties of the optimization sets associated with the information bottleneck problem. In addition to the inequalities and convergence results we establish, our analysis offers insights into how simple properties of ergodic Markov chains give rise to results concerning the information bottleneck problem for such chains.
2610.25952.title: On the Information Bottleneck for Ergodic Finite-State Markov Chains: Stationary Approximation and Asymptotic Optimality

2610.25974.summary: Time-interleaved analog-to-digital converters (TI-ADCs) enable multi-gigasample-per-second throughput in high-speed applications, but sub-picosecond timing skews among interleaved channels introduce large spectral artifacts that degrade dynamic performance. To continuously track parametric drifts without interrupting normal operation, background calibration is required. However, extracting timing skews under unknown inputs is challenging, and many existing correlation-based methods rely on resource-heavy derivative filters that restrict input bandwidth. This article proposes a novel background timing-skew estimation technique for two-channel TI-ADCs that overcomes these limitations. Closed-form timing-skew expressions are derived using: (a) adjacent-channel cross-correlation combined with single-channel auto-correlation for sinusoidal inputs, and (b) adjacent-channel cross-correlation for Wide-Sense Stationary (WSS) inputs, specifically bandpass-filtered wideband noise and Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexed (OFDM) signals. The derived analytical models are validated through comprehensive simulations, offering an efficient framework for real-time background calibration in high-speed data converters.
2610.25974.title: Timing Skew Estimation of Time-Interleaved ADC based on Inter-Channel Correlations without Computing Derivative of Input Signal

2610.25979.comment: Accepted for publication in the 2026 IEEE 103rd Vehicular Technology Conference (VTC2026-Spring)
2610.25979.summary: Recent advances in deep joint source-channel coding (DeepJSCC) have shown strong robustness to channel variations in wireless image transmission. However, its integration with orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) typically relies on fixed pilot patterns that are not optimized for receiver- side channel processing. This work introduces Pilot-Efficient DeepJSCC-OFDM (PE-JSCC), which learns pilot placement under a strictly fixed number of pilot symbols via a Gumbel- Top-k-based selector. The learned pilot placement improves end- to-end performance over the conventional Block-JSCC, Comb- JSCC, and Scatter-JSCC baselines. To support high mobility, the receiver incorporates a lightweight axial-attention-based inter- carrier interference (ICI) canceler and a CNN-based channel estimator. Simulation results show that PE-JSCC consistently outperforms fixed pilot patterns across diverse SNRs and remains robust over a wide mobility range.
2610.25979.title: Learnable Pilot Design for OFDM-based Deep Joint Source-Channel Coding

2610.26007.summary: Single-photon avalanche diode (SPAD) arrays offer photon-level sensitivity for sensing in optical integrated sensing and communication (O-ISAC). However, after each detection, a SPAD is blind for a dead time, which saturates the array at high received power. Existing O-ISAC analyses assume linear receivers and do not capture this effect. In this paper, we study ranging with a SPAD array in a monostatic O-ISAC system based on direct-current-biased optical orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (DCO-OFDM). Sampling the array once per dead time, we model the number of pixels that detect a photon in each sampling interval as a binomial random variable whose success probability accounts for the intensity variation of the echo within a dead time. Based on this model, we derive the Cramér-Rao bound (CRB) for range estimation. We show that the SPAD count model of optical wireless communication, which assumes a constant photon rate over a dead time, causes a range bias that depends on the received power. Moreover, unlike for a linear photodiode, saturation degrades the ranging accuracy beyond a sensing-optimal transmit power. The rate-constrained operating point is then the larger of this power and the power needed for the target data rate. Numerical results validate the analysis against a continuous-time photon-counting simulation and show that the proposed model is needed for ranging.
2610.26007.title: Optical ISAC with Single-Photon Avalanche Diode (SPAD) Arrays

2610.26021.summary: We introduce and study the adaptive covering complexity C adapt S (s), defined as the minimum number of contiguous factor blocks required to partition a string s when each block is either a factor of a fixed external dictionary S or a factor of the target's already decoded prefix. This hybrid admissibility model formalizes the structural interaction between static dictionary matching and dynamic nonoverlapping self-referencing. Our main theoretical result is the exact logarithmic law which is tight and proves that dynamic self-reference can reduce phrase count by at most an exponential factor over static dictionary covering alone. We establish structural equivalences showing that the measure bridges word-segmented Relative Lempel-Ziv and non-overlapping LZ77, and we prove exact preset-history LZ77 sandwich bounds. Furthermore, we establish the optimality of the longest-match greedy parse via an exchange lemma and present an optimal implementation based on dual suffix automata running in O(M + n) time and space for a constant alphabet. These analytical results are complemented by counting bounds, stationary-ergodic asymptotic invariance, a dictionaryselection NP-hardness result, and a concise empirical illustration.
2610.26021.title: On the Adaptive Covering Complexity of Strings: Unifying Relative and Self-Referential Compression

2610.26048.summary: Maximum rank-distance codes were introduced independently by Delsarte (1978) and Gabidulin (1985) for unrestricted matrix spaces, and their study was subsequently extended to the classical form spaces of alternating, symmetric, and Hermitian matrices. For Hermitian $d$-codes, Schmidt (2018) established the upper bound and constructed optimal additive codes for all admissible parameters except when $n$ and $d$ are both even and $4\le d\le n-2$. We settle this final open existence case, more generally, construct additive maximum Hermitian rank-metric codes for every admissible length and minimum distance. Rather than working directly in the space of Hermitian matrices, we construct our objects within central simple algebras with unitary involution arising from quotients of skew polynomial rings. We also introduce scalar-field and Lyapunov operators in these algebras, leading to new invariants for the equivalence of additive Hermitian codes. Explicitly determining these invariants yields strong necessary conditions for Hermitian equivalence and demonstrates that our construction contains a large number of pairwise inequivalent codes.
2610.26048.title: New Maximum Hermitian $d$-Codes and New Invariants from Skew Polynomial Rings

2610.26153.comment: Accepted at IEEE GLOBECOM 2026 Workshops (GC Wkshps)
2610.26153.summary: This work develops a physics-driven self-supervised graph learning framework that directly optimizes the distortion-aware precoder under nonlinear correlated power amplifier (PA) distortion, without relying on expensive optimizer-generated labels for a user-centric satellite system. We minimize nonlinear PA consumption subject to user quality-of-service (QoS) constraints under PA nonlinearity for a downlink multi-input-single-output (MISO) satellite system. Our pipeline jointly designs the precoder and admission control that minimize nonlinear PA consumed power. In particular, a graph neural network (GNN) for the design of a distortion-aware precoder is optimized end-to-end in a self-supervised manner using a differentiable Itô-Hermite model of the true modified Rapp amplifier model. The precoder output by the GNN is used to initialize a low-complexity distortion-aware signal-to-interference-distortion (SINDR) tracking algorithm that jointly optimizes for power and admission control. Our proposed physics-based pipeline closely tracks a successive convex approximation (SCA) based solution in consumed power performance with the advantage of faster runtime and a wide operating range covered during training.
2610.26153.title: Physics-Driven Framework for QoS-Constrained Satellite System with Non-Linear PA Distortion

2610.26200.summary: Let $q=p^f$, where $p$ is prime. We prove that every $q$-ary linear code meeting the Griesmer bound, with positive dimension and minimum distance $d\ge1$, is $p^{\max\{0,\nu_p(d)-f+1\}}$-divisible, as asserted in Ward's conjecture. Arbitrary projective column multiplicities are allowed. The geometric ingredient is a bound independent of dimension: a nonzero scalar-invariant function $F:\mathbb{F}_q^k\to\mathbb{F}_p$, with $F(0)=0$ and prime-field algebraic degree at most $(f+s)(p-1)$, vanishes identically on at most $p^s(q-1)$ linear hyperplanes when $0\le s<f$. A truncated digit-sum inequality forces selected coefficient polynomials to be homogeneous of ordinary degree less than $q$. Weighted moments on a projective line then bound their linear factors, while a second-moment argument handles the complementary support configuration. An elementary finite-difference calculation supplies the degree bound for divided weight residues. Endpoint shortenings prove the basic divisibility layers; endpoint lifting, a surjective linear functional, and residual-code induction extend the argument to every valuation. We include the proofs of the classical ingredients, identify their sources, and distinguish the present argument from an earlier reported unpublished proof.
2610.26200.title: A Hyperplane Bound and Ward's Divisibility Conjecture

2610.26245.summary: In this paper, a counterexample to Lemma 5 of the paper referenced in the title is provided. Consequently, the formulation of the method of data-driven gaps presented in the referenced paper relies on an additional assumption, namely, that the conditional distribution of the training dataset given the learned model has identical data-point-specific marginals. To overcome this limitation, a generalized formulation of the method of data-driven gaps that does not rely on Lemma 5 and does not require the training samples to be independent or identically distributed is presented. Through this formulation, the applicability of the method of data-driven gaps is extended to a broader class of data distributions and randomized learning algorithms.
2610.26245.title: Corrections to ``The Method of Gaps: Exact Expressions for the Generalization Error of Supervised Learning Algorithms''

2610.26344.summary: In this paper, we investigate the impact of practical phase-shift constraint of reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) on multi-antenna systems employing maximal ratio combining (MRC) and receive antenna selection (RAS). Since each element of RIS can apply only a single phase-shift at a given time, the system performance degrades substantially when multiple receive antennas are active simultaneously. To quantify this effect, closed-form outage probability expressions are derived and asymptotic analyses are carried out over Rician fading channels. We show that the practical phase-shift constraint of RIS degrades the diversity order of MRC and in addition, RAS outperforms MRC, contrary to the conventional performance ordering of these techniques.
2610.26344.title: On the Performance of RIS Transmitter with Receive Combining Techniques

2610.26353.summary: GNSS signal acquisition is the process of detecting and estimating signal parameters by exploiting correlation operations that provide processing gain and enable the detection of signals below the noise floor. The design of an acquisition engine requires balancing achievable sensitivity, computational complexity, memory requirements, power consumption, and implementation complexity. In particular, increasing coherent and non-coherent integration times improves sensitivity but can significantly increase receiver processing requirements, limiting its applicability in low-power and resource-constrained receivers. This paper presents a comparative analysis of L1-band signal acquisition complexity by evaluating the required integration time and corresponding implementation requirements for different signal designs under equivalent acquisition performance targets. The analysis considers the impact of signal characteristics, including spreading codes, secondary codes, modulation, and signal bandwidth, on coherent and non-coherent acquisition performance. For a given attenuation level and target probability of false alarm and detection, the required integration times are derived and translated into acquisition complexity metrics, including arithmetic operations, processing time, and memory requirements. The analysis is applied to Pulsar X1, a LEO-enabled PNT signal, and representative GNSS L1 signals to determine under which attenuation, assistance, and integration conditions the higher received power of LEO-PNT translates into reduced receiver acquisition workload. By relating the required integration to arithmetic operations, processing time, and memory requirements, the study provides a receiver-level comparison relevant to both conventional and snapshot-based receivers, where reducing acquisition processing can directly contribute to lower energy consumption.
2610.26353.title: Signal Design Impacts on GNSS and LEO-PNT L1 Band Acquisition Complexity: A Case Study with Xona Pulsar

2610.26355.summary: Most existing studies on pinching-antenna systems optimize the antenna positions or activation states under a prescribed waveguide deployment, where mutually parallel waveguides are commonly adopted. However, it remains unclear whether, and under what conditions, such a deployment is optimal from a communication-performance perspective. To fill this gap, this paper investigates long-term waveguide deployment optimization for pinching-antenna systems over a rectangular service region. We first consider the fundamental two-waveguide case and derive a closed-form sufficient condition, jointly determined by the waveguide height and the service-region aspect ratio, under which a deployment parallel to the longer side of the service region is globally optimal. We then consider the general multi-waveguide case, where the orientation and offset of each waveguide are jointly optimized without prescribing any deployment pattern, and develop an adaptive exchange algorithm for the resulting nonconvex optimization problem. We further show that, within the parallel class, the waveguides should be aligned with the longer side of the service region, while in the large-height regime, the globally optimal unrestricted deployment asymptotically concentrates all waveguides on the centerline along the longer side. Numerical results validate the proposed algorithm and reveal how the preferred deployment geometry depends on the waveguide height and service-region shape. In particular, nonparallel deployments can provide noticeable gains in intermediate-height regimes, whereas parallel or center-concentrated deployments become favorable in other regimes.
2610.26355.title: Waveguide Deployment Optimization for Pinching-Antenna Systems

2610.26385.summary: In analog coded computing, encoding basis functions are typically chosen to guarantee exact reconstruction and improve numerical stability. However, the same basis functions also determine the statistical geometry of the observations available to colluding workers, and hence directly influence the privacy of the underlying data. This suggests that basis selection should not be viewed solely as a reconstruction or numerical conditioning problem, but rather as a joint privacy and accuracy co-design problem. Motivated by this observation, we revisit Analog Lagrange Coded Computing (ALCC) and show that the full orthogonality constraints imposed by the conventional Lagrange basis are stronger than what is required for exact recovery. We retain only the interpolation constraints necessary for the data bearing basis functions and require the noise bearing basis functions merely to vanish at the data recovery points. This yields a parameterized family of generalized polynomial encoding bases that preserves exact reconstruction while introducing additional design degrees of freedom. We then derive a basis-dependent characterization of differential privacy for colluding workers and formulate a privacy-calibrated numerical optimization problem that jointly selects the data and noise basis functions to reduce reconstruction error while satisfying a prescribed \((\epsilon,\delta)\)-DP requirement. The resulting framework therefore treats the encoding basis itself as a privacy-design variable, rather than selecting a fixed closed-form basis a priori. The same design philosophy is also compatible with alternative privacy metrics such as mutual-information leakage. Numerical results show that, at the same privacy level, optimized basis functions substantially reduce floating-point reconstruction error relative to conventional ALCC.
2610.26385.title: Basis Selection For Analog Coded Computing Under Differential Privacy Constraints

2610.26396.summary: Peres's iteration of von Neumann's procedure is completed into a bijection of $\bits^N$: the recursion runs to exhaustion, nothing is discarded, and every input splits into fair bits and residual bits. The residual strings form a complete prefix code that determines the number of ones of the input, so the fair bits are exactly uniform given the residual for every exchangeable law. For a Bernoulli source the likelihood factorises exactly, in decoding order, into a factor $1/2$ per fair bit and a Bernoulli factor per residual bit, with biases obtained by iterating two explicit maps. The number of fair bits per input symbol tends to the entropy almost surely, also on larger alphabets. Code B stores the fair bits and codes only the residual with an arithmetic coder; its ideal length is that of the two-part code, at most $\log\_2(N+1)+1$ bits above $-\log\_2\Pr\_\theta(s)$ for every input $s$ and bias $\theta$. Code C uses Rice codes instead. In experiments up to $N=2^{20}$ its mean regret stays below $200$ bits, where a Rice coder on the raw input loses a fixed fraction of the entropy on skewed sources. For sources with memory, the Burrows--Wheeler transform of the reversed string arranges all context orders in one tree of intervals; coding the leaves of a pruned tree as Bernoulli strings adapts to every Markov order up to its depth, and on suffix-closed trees the leaf weights determine the split points.
2610.26396.title: Universal coding with the exhaustive peres transform

2610.26450.summary: Binary Goppa codes are important in coding theory and cryptography. It is well-known that the minimum distance of a binary Goppa code defined by a squarefree polynomial of degree $r$ is at least $2r+1$. Though from the classical results of C. J. Moreno, O. Moreno, F. Levy-dit-Vehel and S. Litsyn that the true minimum distances of binary Goppa codes are $2r+1$, when the extension field degree $m$ is larger than $(r-1)^{4r}$. There have only very few families of binary Goppa codes with determined true minimum distances. In this paper, we give necessary and sufficient conditions for binary Goppa codes such that their minimum distances are $2r+1$ and $2r+2$. Infinitely many infinite families of binary Goppa codes with minimum distance $2r+1$ are given. In particular, we construct such codes for every Goppa degree $r$ in the range $2^{h-1}<r<2^h$ over $\mathbb F_{2^{2h}}$. For every $2\le r\le\lfloor2^m/3\rfloor$, we also obtain at least $2^m-3r+1$ distinct monic squarefree Goppa polynomials of degree $r$ over $\mathbb F_{2^m}$, such that their related binary Goppa codes have minimum distance $2r+1$. We extend a criterion for $q$-ary Goppa codes to split auxiliary polynomials and obtain some infinite families of $q$-ary Goppa codes attaining their designed distances $r+1$. We also construct infinite families of binary Goppa codes with minimum distance exactly $2r+2$.
2610.26450.title: On True Minimum Distances of Goppa Codes

2610.26480.summary: Recent work suggests that standard synchrophasors are inadequate for capturing high-frequency data center oscillations, primarily due to filtering and windowing attenuation during phasor estimation. We prove that widely used periodogram and RMS energy detectors remain largely robust to it and confirm this by simulation.
2610.26480.title: Does Synchrophasor Attenuation Preclude Detection of High-Frequency Oscillations?

2610.26500.summary: We develop a vision--radio-frequency (RF) cooperative integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) framework that jointly uses visual priors and RF observations for transmit-side beam control and receiver-side clutter suppression. Within a narrowband snapshot model, visual target priors and historical RF detections guide control in dynamic vehicle-to-infrastructure networks with roadside clutter. In this framework, posterior angular uncertainty determines beam control and the selection between communication-for-sensing and sensing-for-sensing modes. To reduce sensing overhead while accommodating unreliable visual information, we develop a reliability-adaptive beam scanning scheme that allocates a bounded scan budget according to visual target probabilities and RF history, while reserving an adaptive fraction for exploration. At the receiver, visual geometry identifies clutter support, and RF observations estimate the corresponding complex reflection coefficients. Motion-aware residual filtering is then applied before angle--Doppler detection to suppress clutter while preserving slow-moving targets. Furthermore, communication and sensing power allocation is formulated as a per-direction linear program, subject to signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio constraints evaluated at angles sampled from the posterior distribution and a total-power budget. Simulation results show that the proposed framework improves tracking over static and vision-only beam control and reduces sensing overhead relative to full scanning. The proposed scanning scheme also provides greater robustness to visual blockage than fixed-weight scanning, while the receiver better preserves slow-moving targets than temporal cancellation when visual target information is available.
2610.26500.title: Vision--RF Cooperative ISAC for Dynamic V2I Networks: Adaptive Beam Management and Semantic Clutter Suppression

2610.26566.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly applied to 5G/6G network optimization, yet differences in empirical evidence, evaluation methods, and computational requirements complicate comparisons of reported performance. This scop ing review synthesizes 72 peer-reviewed journal studies pub lished between 2022 and 2026, selected through a PRISMA ScR-informed process from 893 records. The review examines empirical tools, AI/ML techniques, optimization domains, and operational readiness. Evidence classification identifies 37 studies (51.4%) using real-world or physical-testbed evidence only, 25 (34.7%) combining measured and simulated evidence, and 10 (13.9%) relying exclusively on synthetic or simulated data. Offline analysis was the most common evaluation setting, accounting for 45 studies (62.5%). Three principal findings emerge. First, empirical measurements improve contextual relevance, while simulation and digital twins support scalable experimentation but introduce validation challenges. Second, algorithmic effectiveness depends on the optimization objective, data characteristics, and computational constraints rather than model complexity alone. Third, predictive accuracy is more consistently evaluated than the network-level effects of optimization decisions. The review there fore introduces the six-module Evidence Fidelity and Operational Reporting (EFOR) checklist to improve evaluation consistency, reporting transparency, and operational relevance.
2610.26566.title: From Data to Deployment: A Scoping Review of Empirical Tools, Techniques, and Operational Readiness in Data-Driven 5G/6G Network Optimization

2610.26649.summary: In the seminal paper [13], Farrán and Munuera introduced a method to establish generic information on the $m$th Feng-Rao distance via a function on arbitrary numerical semigroups that serves as a lower bound on the generalized Hamming weights of dual one-point algebraic geometry codes whenever the semigroup is Weierstrass. In the present paper, we study what we shall call the primary and dual, respectively, $m$th relative Feng-Rao distances, which serve as lower bounds on relative generalized Hamming weights of nested primary and dual, respectively, one-point codes under similar condition. A unified method for establishing generic formulas for $m$th relative Feng-Rao distances of general numerical semigroups is developed and for a large variety of numerical semigroups generated by two elements, closed formula expressions are established complementing Delgado et al.s work [8] on the $m$th Feng-Rao distances of such semigroups. Finally, for non-singular $C_{ab}$ curves, we develop a method to estimate the $m$th relative generalized Hamming weight of dual and primary one-point codes in those regions where the generic methods may fail to provide best possible results.
2610.26649.title: A study of the $m$th relative Feng-Rao distances with a special emphasis on $C_{ab}$ curves

2610.26683.summary: The service rate region of a distributed storage system describes the set of concurrent demand vectors that can be served without overloading any individual server, and is a fundamental measure of how effectively redundancy is used. In this paper, we investigate aggregate service rates in distributed data storage systems based on linear codes over arbitrary finite fields. We first derive an upper bound on the aggregate service rate for an arbitrary subset of $t$ data objects in terms of the dual distance and the sizes of their smallest recovery sets. For systematic generator matrices, this bound simplifies to an expression depending only on the code length, the dual distance, and the cardinality of the selected subset. This result extends existing bounds and provides a subset-wise formulation of the First Dual Distance Bound. We then establish conditions under which this upper bound is attained. We apply our results to several important families of linear codes, including MDS codes, Reed-Muller codes, constacyclic codes, and extended Golay codes, and obtain exact values of the maximum aggregate service rates for the corresponding subsets of data objects.
2610.26683.title: Bounds on the Service Rates of Linear Codes and their Connections to Combinatorial Designs

2610.26808.summary: In this paper, we generalize the code basis reduction to non-Hamming metrics. We propose a block basis reduction (BKZ) algorithm for codes that works for all coordinate-additive metrics. Our algorithm is a generalization of the algorithm of Ghentiyala and Stephens-Davidowitz, which in turn is an adaptation of the famous BKZ algorithm for lattices to linear codes and the Hamming metric. For block size~$2$ (LLL), we propose a polynomial-time algorithm with complexity~$\mathcal{O}(n^4 q^3)$ operations in~$\mathbb{F}_q$, where~$n$ is the length of the code and~$q$ is the alphabet size. For the Lee metric we provide an implementation of our algorithms and present experimental results on finding low Lee weight codewords.
2610.26808.title: Block basis reduction for linear codes in non-Hamming metrics

2610.26842.comment: Under review for a publication in IEEE Transactions on Signal Processing
2610.26842.summary: Phase modulated continuous wave (PMCW) radar is an attractive choice for automotive sensing due to its high dynamic range, interference robustness, and support for integrated communication and sensing. In multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) PMCW radar, code division multiplexing (CDM) separates transmit signals, but non-ideal auto- and cross-correlation properties increase range sidelobes and degrade dynamic range. This paper proposes a Doppler-compensated space-time coding (STC)-based MIMO PMCW radar framework that separates transmit signals before range correlation, eliminating cross-correlation terms under perfect compensation and allowing the same binary sequence to be used across transmit antennas. The Doppler influence on STC decoding is analytically characterized, showing that chip-wise and inter-STC-slot phase distortions increase range sidelobes and generate ghost components in the direction-of-arrival (DOA) spectrum. To mitigate these effects, Doppler is estimated first, followed by joint fast-time and STC-slot compensation before decoding. Residual STC leakage under imperfect Doppler estimation is quantified, and the processing is extended to multiple moving targets through Doppler-bin-dependent compensation. Theoretical analysis and simulation results demonstrate reduced range sidelobes and suppression of DOA ghosts, while maintaining flexibility in code sequence design.
2610.26842.title: Doppler-compensated Space-time Coding for MIMO PMCW Radar

AI.conclusion: 环面波束工程可作为OAM无线链路的实用波束设计手段，在保持涡旋相位的同时抑制发散并改善多模链路均衡，具有硬件可实现性。
